title: Cole Kmet, Cam Lewis on finishing training camp strong | Press Conference
text: Well, you've been with Caleb for three years now, two plus years now. How have you seen him grow over that time? You guys got really close early on. How have you seen him grow on the field in that time? >> Uh, I I mean, I just think it's things I've said in the past like Operation the Huddle has just continued to get better and better. And um, you know, you can you can tell his uh rapport with with coach has just grown so much since uh since really a year ago. So, you just seeing that growth in the huddle uh each and every day. What [snorts] did you guys take from that short series you guys had? >> Um, I mean, I thought it was just good to like get out there in terms of kind of getting your game day routine going. We're going to be playing quite [snorts] a bit of prime time games this year, it looks like. So, uh, kind of getting that night routine going as to what you do leading up to the game, um, I thought was beneficial for us. So, um, all those type of things and obviously we're not heavily game planning teams right now, but, um, just to go out there and, uh, execute some plays. I I thought that was that was a good kind of drill work for us there. >> Cole, that uh, long drive period kind of practice. >> Yeah, it sucks. >> Pretty gross. >> Yeah, pretty. But I mean, what do you guys feel like you get out of those periods? >> Well, I think it just comes down to how do you execute when you're tired and, you know, when you don't feel like going. So, um I mean you definitely get to a certain point where uh you know you get pretty tired in that drill plays 8 9 10 11 and um [snorts] you know you got to be able to hear the play call and and kind of revert back to your training and and you know trust your rules in that regard. So um it definitely gets difficult as you're as you're tired and you know you can see younger players who do that for the first time like they struggle just cuz they they got so much going on in their head already and then you add fatigue to the situation it just makes it that much more difficult. So, um, there was definitely many, many times last year where that those type of feelings come up in games. They're kind of few and far between, but I mean, I can think of the game against Dallas where I forget how long that play play drive was, but um, you [snorts] know, you have them throughout the year and you want to be able to sustain and finish and I think it's just good conditioning for us, especially at this point of the of the camp. >> Does the crowd noise uh back at all? [snorts] >> Yeah, I mean, it definitely does. Um, it's like the most annoying noise there is. I don't know if like any fans sound like that uh in any other stadium I've been in, but uh it definitely uh definitely bugs you in the huddle and when you're communicating haunted scrimmage. So, it's it's good work for us. >> You had a snap against Dylan, I think, during that long drive period. How have you seen him maybe develop from start camp until now? Yeah, I think at first, you know, he definitely playing with a little bit of hesitancy in terms of uh maybe not knowing where he needs to be when he needs to be there or play recognition. And I think that that has sped up over and over again. um each and every day he's been out there and um you know I've seen it, you know, even today like he he made a few good plays on Coulson I thought were good coverage plays where um I thought earlier in our camp like you know we were kind of getting the best of him and you know he's kind of come back and and done a really good job in that regard and I think he's been more physical in the run game kind of feeling his presence there. So um you know it's [snorts] just a matter of time. A lot of these kids, they come in, they're super talented, but this NFL game is so different than what it is in college. And it just takes time for them to to kind of when they get their feet wet and and getting used to the play speed, the play style of the NFL. And um it's been cool to see him grow each and every week. And I know he's going to help us out big time this year. >> Well, we see that, you know, your kind of role in the offense, particularly in passing games, just it's kind of evolved over the last year or even last two years. How do you just kind of what's your outlook like just kind of doing whatever they're asking you? >> Yeah, it's all about winning. So like whatever we got to do to win. So um yeah, I mean if that means you know catching six, seven balls a game, I'm here for it. If that means hey I gota you know be the guy and and pass pro help in pass protection and things like that and and you know be a main focus in the run game, I'm all for that as well. So um not that hard when you know the main the main goal here is is to win. >> Does it feel like you guys are ready right now or I mean how do you like >> readying >> like ready like if we played Sunday like we've done enough that we're ready to go? Um, I I mean I don't know about that. I think like you always want to use all the time you can to get ready to go for that week one. And you know, there's still uh there's still a lot of work to be done this week. I think we all understand like we got to put our head heads down uh this upcoming week in Tennessee and and [snorts] really get after it in this joint practice and then and then into the game and then um we got that, you know, now extra by week of of camp to kind of hone things in before week one. So um I still feel like there's a lot of work to do and a lot that we can get better at. What's at the top of what's at the top of that list for the offense? What do you [snorts] like needs to be taken care of, >> man? Well, I think well, I I think one is first is like finishing out camp strong. Um, you know, you get to this point and we get you get a little fatigued and kind of experience it last year, you know, that coach is going to take care of us on the back end of things, but making sure that we finish this thing through the way we should, uh, is going to be really important. And I think that's a huge indicator of how you can finish out the season. And that proved to be true for us last year. [snorts] And then I think it's just continuing to establish our identity. I think we've seen that physicality show up. Um but just continue to have it on a more consistent basis and um you know we're always striving to get better and better. Although I think it's looked good. Um we're always trying to get better in that regard. >> Well, as you watched Darnell Wright come into his own last year, [snorts] what struck you just kind of about his growth and what he meant to the offense. >> Yeah, well I mean he's just a he I mean he's one of the freakiest athletes I've ever seen. Um, so I think for him just to kind of let it loose and, you know, understand where he needs to be, uh, his communication has gone up, you know, tenfold since I've been with him his rookie year. And, uh, I think it just comes from, you know, the certainty now that he has playing the position, understanding the intent of run plays and, um, you know, where we're trying to hit him and things like that. And, uh, you know, maybe the first few years, like I was always the one kind of giving him a call or like, "Hey, where you going here on this And now he's I mean his process at the snap is is so good. And um you know I I feel I feel really good when I'm on that right side playing with him just because you you have a good feeling of and knowing that he he understands what's going on and it really helps helps me do my job um at a faster rate as well. >> Can you describe the mentality that you have um going into the 2020 season 2026 season you and your teammates? >> The mentality we have. Yeah. To win. I mean to win um I think you know whenever the expectations uh going into last year weren't I think were kind of mixed in here and in everywhere else but this year you know everyone has expectations of you know playoffs and Super Bowl um and uh you know that that's a that's those are big expectations to have but we've always had those expectations in the building so um you know it's a lot to go after but um it's definitely what we want. Co, what have you seen of Devin Bush and uh any adjustments that he forces you to make out there? >> Yeah, I mean, well, going against Deon in Cleveland last year, so like familiar with the player. Um, you [snorts] know, really, really fast sideline to sideline, so he can run really well. Good coverer. Um, so he offers you a lot in that regard. And, um, he's definitely been a good challenge for us, uh, this camp as tight ends. >> There was a moment today in practice where it looked like Ben brought the whole team together, which we haven't really seen. I'm assuming it was Ben, but what was that? >> I think it was Jaylen, actually. Yeah, it was Jaylen. Yeah, I think just like kind of ramping it up a little bit as we were getting going with some of the team stuff and um kind of just heightened the competitiveness atmosphere and I thought that was good by Jaylen to kind of step up and and get us going there and I thought uh it was one of our ended up being one of our better practices the of the camp so far. >> With Coloulston, if you had to hypothetically like step into the shoes of the defensive coordinator >> Yeah. >> What are you What are you going to try? Yeah, I think it's tough. Uh, it's tough because, you know, those DB bodies are are uh are not big enough to cover him and he's definitely elusive and and and faster than a lot of linebackers you're going to see in the NFL. So, um it's [snorts] going to be tough. It'll be interesting to see how how teams go about it, especially when, you know, if we we got 13 out there, you know, you got 12 or 13 personnel, um you for sure don't want the backer on them. You know, you don't want you don't want the safety. They go small on us like we're going to run it down your throat. So, um, you know, he's definitely a weapon that opens up a lot of things for the offense and, um, I'll be interested to see how how defensive coordinators handle that throughout the season. >> Let's go. One more back. [snorts] >> Um, can you tell me what specific parts of your game are you working on in this training camp? >> Yeah, right now pad level, you know, you get towards the end of camp, you get a little fatigued and uh, just making sure I hone in my pad level at the line of scrimmage. That's that's a big thing for the pad level. >> Can you describe what that means? I'm sorry. >> Do you want me to show you right here? No, I'm kidding. [laughter] >> Dylan Theam, man. He's doesn't look like a regular rookie from our vantage point. >> Yeah, smart smart kid for sure. Plays fast, very instinctive. Uh, I feel very comfortable. You know, we're still learning, uh, day in day out, you know, getting on the same page, what we see, how we want to see it, how we want to disguise and stuff like that. But, uh, he's been improving every day. So, I'm lucky to be working with a, you know, good rookie like that. Johnson talks about the the safety competition and just the competition secondary. How do you internalize that? What's your response? Uh >> I compete every day. I compete every day. Uh you know, it's 31 other teams of the same stuff going on. You know, some people get cut there and he's like, "Oh, he's not performing here. Let's see if we can bring somebody else in." So, I'm not just, you know, competing internally, you know, in house with the with the team we have here, but everywhere else. So, um, that's how I always looked at it, you know, being in the NFL. Your guy got your job is not quote unquote secure, you know. Um, always had that chip on my shoulder. So, I don't look at it as a as a big thing. I go out there and put my best foot forward, go to, you know, compete my butt off, try to help my team win football games, and the outcome is going to be the outcome. >> How do you assess your camp from specifically from the beginning to how you're doing now? >> To my standards, it's just all right. Um, I feel like I can be a little bit better in certain areas. Like today I didn't feel like I had my best practice, but um go watch the tape and and um you know, learn some stuff and be better, you know, tomorrow. But it's just steady growth. Like I don't want to peak here in training camp, you know, two weeks before week one. I want to keep getting better day in day out and you know, be peing uh winning the the division and going to that playoff run, you know. >> Are you still managing kind of preparing for the dual roles? >> Always. Okay. >> Yeah, always. So, I mean, right now I'm learning a whole bunch of stuff. So, um I'm never li limit myself to one position. Uh just try to be of value uh to the team. Whatever they need me to play, I'd be able to play it at a high level. >> You said just all right. What haven't you liked? >> Um I don't feel like I made enough plays on the ball, you know. Um I do my job and do communicate pretty uh you know, fairly well. Um but [clears throat] I don't I don't know. It's just like I said, it's just not not up to my standard. It feels feels like a little a little rocky like uh you know I'm still learning you know the defense how DA wants it to be played but um prior yeah years prior years and those camps felt like I made a little bit more plays so it felt like it was a little bit better overall maybe you know coaches may feel like it was a pretty good camp but like I said to to me it doesn't feel that way so uh still got some you know room to get better and that's a good thing. >> Coaching that last long drive period sucked. Yeah. >> What specific perspective? >> Yeah, we sucked. Uh I feel like on the defensive end, uh first play, [gasps] first play of it, we gave up eight and nine yard, you know, game right up the middle. Don't want that. You know, you need a two yard, three yard game at at most. Uh we had a couple mas on on the pressure, which I I feel like it falls on me because I'm the I'm the one that communicate on the back end. So, like I said, I got to do better. Um we just didn't get it done. A lot of big plays. Um, and we just, you know, just getting conditioned, you know, for the for those long drives because, you know, it can't happen in the game. But I feel like we just didn't execute well. But it's always in the world. Like I said, >> in DA's defense, how would you describe everything on the safety's plate? >> Um, [sighs] I mean, you got to be a communicator, honestly. You got to know where where people should be. Get them in the right position. Uh, be able to be instinctive and make plays. I don't feel like it's too fairly hard on the safeties in the back end, but you got to know what everybody else is doing, which I feel like isn't any safety in any scheme. >> There was a moment I can't remember who the linebacker was, but you said something about communication to him. Just I don't there might have been something like a big completion and you seemed kind of frustrated with the communication in that moment. Like is it >> going along as I guess as you would expect it to? Where are the areas you think you might need to clean it up? Um, [sighs and gasps] I feel like it's not going to always it's not I feel like it's never going to be as clean as you want it to be. Like we're going to make some mistakes. We're human out there. Uh, bullets are flying. A lot of different things are going on, a lot of different variables. So, um, we try to strive for perfection. So, we want everybody to know what they're supposed to do. You know what I'm saying? So, um, if you're playing corner, we call it pressure on and it has nothing to do with you, you should know somebody on the other side is splicing. That's that's kind of how I I look at it and that's where we're kind of growing to as a defense. Just knowing what you're supposed to do and what the man next to next to you is supposed to do. So, um like I said, we don't we don't have it figured out now, which is it's okay. We still have practices. We still have meetings. We still have room to grow as a defense. And that's a good thing. You know, you don't want to top out here like we're the best defense training camp week four right now. It's not going to be the case. So, uh I said room to grow. Just want to keep going here day by day. >> I guess Jaylen might have called the team together before one of the team drills towards the end of practice. Yeah. >> What what what message was he trying to get across? >> Feel like it wasn't good enough. >> I agree. It wasn't to our standard. Uh you want to win the division backtoback years, you're the hunting now. We what we did in the first half of the practice wasn't, you know, to our standard. So brought it up, told the guys that and we moved on. >> Have you seen that in the in the past on other teams? Yeah. Yeah. You want to be player driven. You don't want the coaches to keep going, you know, yelling down your neck. Um those I mean all the good teams that I've been on freaking five, you know, divisions, been to the sup I mean not Super Bowl need to be there, but uh to play off like my whole career and and you know in my previous stop. So um that's how I always been. You don't want like I said, you don't want your coaches breathing it on your neck whole time. So, um, you want the guys, you want the leaders, even if you're not necessarily don't have a C on your chest. You still need to speak up, especially if you feel like your brother's not preparing or playing to his level of play. So, um, that's always a good thing. You know, you know, you never will not um, respect that. >> There's a little scrap little scrap today with I think it was Salon and uh, and Xavier Woods. Uh, seems like you guys haven't had too many of those like battles like that. Uh, do you need more of that or does you know you like to see that? >> Well, I really don't care for it honestly. I don't feel like it is what it is to me. Um, do what you need to do in between a whistle. You know, be physical there, play nasty there, play violent there, and once the whistle blow, it's done. But if it gets to that point, you know, defend yourself. Stick up for yourself. You're a man, you're going against another man, just not going to let him dog you out. So, do what you got to do. Sean, >> beside that though, like what have you gotten to know about Xavier Woods since he got here? >> Quiet guy, but very smart, very instinctive uh player. Um knows a lot. Been in a lot of different defenses. So, I always kind of pick his brain uh whenever he is talking or whatever, you know. But, uh he's a good ball player, man. I'm just glad we got another one here. >> Last one. >> So, you mentioned that uh Jaylen said that you guys didn't have your best practice, and again, like you mentioned, you were in week four. So, can you talk to me about what is the mindset that you guys have when you guys come together? And what are you doing as a team to help build chemistry to prepare for the season? >> Go out, go to dinners, chill with each other. Um, see what you know they do outside of football. You know, their families, you know, you just got to get to know people, you know, especially if you want to lead them. Just like I don't I don't know you, so I don't really kind of respect you. I'm not going to listen to your, you know, whatever you're saying. So, I want to get to know you on a personal level and when I get to know you on a personal level now, I I will be willing to follow you. You know what I'm saying? So, uh we just like I said, we just still coming together. You're really not going to have it figured out in first four weeks of training camp. You know, we we started in the spring, yes, but it's a little bit different now. Now, it's just like we're solely focused on one goal and we just, you know, still trying to get that bond together and it's going to come week by week, day by day. So, just taking, like I said, we're just taking it one day at a time. Um, getting closer, you know, to one another.

title: Ben Johnson says a few positions are still up for grabs | Press Conference
text: All right. Uh good morning or afternoon, whatever time it is. Um little bit of a rinse and repeat here this week just from a from a plan in terms of our team. We'll uh get a good one in today and then travel day tomorrow down to Tennessee. Talk with coach Salah. I think we got a really good plan to get some great work in in our joint practice on Thursday. And uh and I think it'll be a great opportunity for our team to come together. I thought last week was exactly what we hoped it would be from that regard. a lot of guys spending times together, um, going out to dinner, things of that nature, and what we'll be able to do, a little bit more team bonding this again this week. So, I'll go and open up from there. >> Was there a connection that led to setting this up with Titans, or was it just kind of >> No, you know, there's u there's a degree in the springtime of of coaches trying to ask each other if they want to do a joint practice or not. Um, and yet you kind of you have to wait until the preseason schedule comes out to be sure that that it all the stars align. And so, um, we didn't know that Tennessee was going to be one of our preseason games, but as soon as we found that out, um, I think coach S and I both had a had a good vision for for coming together and how it could help both of us. So, yeah, it was good. >> Oh, go ahead. Wanted to circle back on the seam shot to Coloulston from Saturday night. when you and Caleb got together and watched through that, >> what was the discussion that you guys had in terms of what you saw and what you wanted? >> Yeah. No, I I think it it boils down to whenever it becomes third and 20. Um you look back and you say, "How could we have not been in that situation?" So that's that's first and 20 right there. Um when he takes alerts, we call some of our our receivers on routes alerts. Coloulston was an alert on that play. He's right if he hits it. If he doesn't, then there's other places we could go with the football. He understands that thought process. And um he's just like me. We don't want to be caught in those third and 20 situations. And so first and 20, we might just take the aggressive aggressiveness level down a notch and uh make sure we keep getting back on track. >> I saw I think it was the Cardinals coach was talking about presentation at the owner's meeting um which they talked about the benefits of multiple joint practices in terms of staying healthy. from your guys's point of view, uh, is were you in there for that meeting and and also what's the value do you think of joint practice? >> Yeah, well, they yeah, there was there was some data. Um, just in regards to one or two joint practices could be could be better for the team going into the season. Um, I certainly love it from an intensity standpoint. Um, you find out a lot about your team during these practices, just who rises up to the competition. Um I think we got a number of competitors on on our roster. So um that was good to see last week. We'll see it again this week. Um but just in as far as our training camp was scheduled, a lot of thought and intent goes into how we're ramping these guys into it. Um the quality of reps that we're getting throughout. Um you oscillate a little bit. Some some really high volume and intensity days followed by bringing it down. uh where do the red zone days kind of fall into that because you know it'll be less fun. So point is there's a lot that goes into it. Uh trust a lot of the guys in this building to to give me the right feedback. We adjust within a practice. We adjust within a week and then certainly we we adjust over the course of camp to to what we need. So this week will be just like last week. You know we'll assess as we go through the week what our workload's like and and uh where we need to go from there. in a preseason game. Uh guys had a lot of uh penalties obviously particularly pre- snap when it didn't seem to be as much of a problem throughout camp. Do you have a sense of why that was happening and how you play? >> Yeah, it's just something that we continue to address and we talk about um you know the week before we only had two penalties. So uh I I feel pretty good about the path that we're on. Um I I you bring it to their attention. in their prideful group and and they know how important it is to not shoot ourselves in the foot. You know, we we had a few really good runs that got called back, an explosive pass that got called back. Uh we had a sack on defense that got that got negated because of a penalty. So, um pre- snap certainly we need to be better than postnap. We just need to be more conscious of where we're putting our hands and uh our guys will do that going forward. Talk to you about there's some pub guys, not Tyler that we got to talk to you about. Elijah Hicks, Shamar Turner, Keshan Elliot, Noah Su. We've been told everything from nothing major to on their way back, but none of these guys have been in camp. Are you anticipating all four of them starting on puff to start the season? >> Uh, it depends on who it is. You know, I think Elijah and um uh Elliot, they'll be back sooner rather than later. Um whereas Shamar and and Noah um we're we're still working along that that road. So, uh, unknown at this point whether whether they'll be on pup or not. >> Ben, one more from the game. Uh, end of half. What do you like about the sequence there? >> Oh, shoot. Uh, for our offense, right, because defensively we gave up a touchdown. Um, we we've talked about that just both sides of the ball. We need to be at our best before the halftime there. We feel like that that's an opportunity for us to steal some points and steal a possession. The first game we were pretty good. I think we have a net of three in the in the last two minutes of the first half. This last game we were a net of minus four because defense gave up the touchdown. Um great job by the offense responding. Um kind of dipped our toe in the water a little bit to see if we could get something on that first run and and we did. It was it was really well blocked and ended up being an explosive run for us that got us going. And then uh you know to piggy back on that with the completion timeout and then 12 seconds left to get a 19 yd gain and still be able to clock it with that amount of time. That's big credit to to the offensive unit. You know, we we showed them some scenarios. I think the fastest one I'd seen um was Teddy Bridgewwater in in Denver a few years ago where he was able to to not quite get 19 yards, but he was able to get in field goal range in in 11 seconds like that. And so for us to get that amount in that amount of time, uh, that it was was pretty awesome. Kudos to Logan Jones. He's the guy that I highlighted to the team just how quickly once the ball was released from Case's hand, he was already up ready to get that ball spotted and snapped as fast as he could. And um, for a young player to be that smart and aware of the situation, I thought that was really impressive. >> Ben, what was your evaluation of the left tackles? >> Yeah, there's still um, that's still an ongoing spot. It's it's a hot spot for us. Um obviously we talk about it almost every time uh I'm up here and and yet uh I don't know that we are 100% sold on who that guy's going to be for Carolina yet. Um we're going to still work through it. That's where today is going to be huge for us. Thursday is going to be huge for us and Saturday is going to be huge for us as well. Um that that spot I tell you another one would be safety. Safety is another spot where we're hoping over those those big three days there that uh we we were able to come to an agreement on who it should be going out there game one so that we can go forward from there. >> Ben, what are some things that you'd like to see clean up in the next couple weeks to show you that he's >> good to go? >> Yeah, I mean, uh I've been pretty consistent that that I'm I'm happy with where he's at right now. I'm uh I love the approach that he takes coming into work every day. I love his demeanor on the field right now. There's a level of professionalism that uh that I think radiates from him. Um he everything he's doing from warming up all the way until the end of practice like there's there's a mission in mind and so I appreciate that about him. Um we're going to continue to focus in on some situational work uh two-minute in particular end of half end of game. um you know it's been a little bit mixed bag over the the last few weeks in terms of the success of the first unit in those situations and so that that'll be a big one for us and then uh there's some coverage recognition things that we talked about yesterday that that I'm challenging them on but we'll keep those in house. >> Couple more please. >> Hey, um what are some of the biggest differences between the team this year and last year? >> Oh shoot. Um that's that that dreaded word last year. Uh yeah. uh you know, it's a completely different group, you know, and uh you we're going back to work. I I'm proud of the way they're working right now. I think they're doing a great job of uh of accepting the messaging every single day, going out there. We're forging our new path. It's a new chapter of Bears football right now. And uh and yet the biggest thing for us is establishing our identity, which I think that's been been even though we lost the game last week, it it was on our tape. We have a defense that's swarming. We have a defense that's fighting for every blade of grass. Um I think they're our little guys are doing a great job tackling in the open field for it being at this point of camp right now. Um that's what we want to be about. And then offensively, you know, we got that push the pile mentality and that showed up again last game also. So, uh that's really what what I look at first and foremost after every game is how our identity is starting to to forge itself and identify itself on game day. thinking with this year, coach, is there a part of this team that you think might be underrated that people outside the building don't really know >> from a personnel perspective? >> Um, yeah. I mean, I think I think our interior defensive line's better than than probably um the outside world gives them credit for. And uh I I know it's some guys are they might be rookies, they might be uh free agents that that people don't know about as much, but um the way they've gone about their business, I I've been really impressed with. So, at the end of that, >> Javon seemed enthusiastic about some of the pre- snap improvements he's made with the guy, Javon >> Dexter. Yeah. What have you seen in him this camp that that tells you that he's moving in the right direction? >> Yeah. Well, I mean, that's that's the thing. He's always been he's a big guy and um he does a great job taking care of his body and being available. I mean, he I don't think he's missed the game in his career yet. He's he's done a great job. Um and yet, we've challenged him to to do some technique things a little bit different this year. and and when he does it, it's a beautiful thing cuz he is a strong he is a big man and he's willing to to run guys down sideline to sideline. I think I think that's what's awesome. Um the consistency level is is what we're still trying to get on a day in day out a play in play out perspective. But um when he does it right, does it the way that we're we're looking for it's it's a pretty thing. >> Super important football question. What do you think of the uniforms? >> What uniforms? I haven't even seen him. Yeah. >> Orange pants. >> I haven't even seen Yeah. >> Stacy, you got >> I just wanted to know your thoughts on Jordan. I mean, did you see the dive out of bounds? >> Jordan Oh, yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. >> What is your What is your thought on the sixth rounder? >> He He's a beast. He uh I mean this guy he's an incredible athlete and he's still learning the game of football to a degree and and yet it's it's amazing what he brings to the table. He's been the same guy every single day. Smile on his face. He loves football. He loves the process. title: Atlanta Falcons coordinators Tommy Rees and Craig Aukerman speak to the media | Press Conference
text: So, uh, Tommy, you guys obviously going to judge the quarterbacks by what they've done during preseason, uh, but how much their past NFL career, primarily last year, would that factor into your decision? >> Yeah, just probably a little bit. You know, I think you look at the whole body of work. You certainly know um, where guys have been in their career. You know what they've done, you know, in real games on a on a big stage. So there's some, you know, certainly there's things you can draw back to and talk through and, you know, know that guys have handled things in the past, but you know, we've started camp all the way back in the spring with a fresh slate. You know, this is a new offense for Tua, new offense for Mike, you know, new offense for the rest of the guys. So, you know, really trying to evaluate how they've handled that and handled what we've asked them to do and been pleased with the progression and want to continue to go here over the next two and a half weeks. >> How'd Mike look yesterday to you? Yeah, it was first of all, it was great to have him out there, you know, like just for the human as hard as he's worked to get back. Um, you know, dealing with a knee injury and coming back again, there's a lot of joy, you know, personally for him to be out there on the field. I think his teammates had a lot of joy for him and um, you know, he did a nice job. The thing with Mike is he's been doing a lot, just hasn't done the full speed work yet. So, getting him, you know, back caught up to the full speed play, you know, mentally he's been sharp. He's been in walkthroughs, he's been doing seven on seven. So, you know, continuing in those full speed reps will be very valuable. >> What would you say too is fitting into, you know, the system that you guys have here now? >> Yeah. Um, I think there are some consistencies and some things that, you know, as you get through camp and as you get ready to play, you start to um hone in on what each quarterback does well and you really want to devise the offense in terms of how they how they play and what suits their eye and what things, you know, really help them play at a high level. Um, and and I think he's done a nice job. I think he's taken a lot of ownership in the operation side of the offense and um you know we've asked him to do some things he maybe hasn't had to do in his career but he's taken a lot of ownership of that and really taken the work and you know he's stressed that amongst upon himself uh to execute at a high level in terms of those things but pleased with Tua. Um, you know, one thing about him is like when things are clean and he's as accurate as as they get, you know, and so it's our job to stress the other 10 guys around him. Uh, to play with great detail, play with great understanding so that things are clean and, you know, we're able to execute at a high level. >> What are some of those things that Tua hasn't done in the past that you guys are asking? Yeah, I don't want to get into the specifics of the scheme necessarily, but um certainly, you know, we ask a lot of our quarterbacks in the operation side of things and, you know, we have ways to, you know, divvy those responsibilities out, but it starts with the quarterback and, um, he's really taken ownership of that and handled it pretty well. >> Having two lefthanded quarterbacks, >> what kind of challenges or unique things does that present? it it doesn't, you know, it's just you have to like flip your brain in terms of, hey, this is more friendly for on this hash because the quarterback's usually right-handed. You just have to, you know, for us, you have to train yourself to start thinking a little bit differently there. You know, certainly for me, um, really never had a left-handed quarterback. Um, so it's, you know, for it's more for us than it is for them. You know, I think the players around him get used to it and, uh, really not a huge challenge that way. One thing that Tua said last week or a couple weeks ago was that it's usually more of a challenge for the quarterback, the lefty quarterbacks, but because there are two of them, >> right, >> it it actually kind of it switched because now it's actually a challenge for y'all instead of them having to adjust. >> Yeah, there's a great conversation like early in camp like do we flip the drawings so that they don't look like right-handed all the time? Do you leave them as lefty? And you know, poor Mike Beard, our QC, you know, starts flipping all these things to make him left-handed friendly. But yeah, I don't think it's a huge deal to be honest with I think you have enough reps where where things kind of even themselves out. Um, we have a lefty center, too, which is rare, you know, so that's a that's another aspect to it. >> How how much um how difficult is it to to judge the two quarterbacks when you got two had a whole body of full practices >> and Michael obviously has not. Is that difficult in that judgment process? >> Yeah, it's certainly a different scale, right? you have live periods, you have situational football, you have things with, you know, a real pass rush. Um, so you have to evaluate him on a on a little bit of a slope just because, you know, one guy's in walkth through and one guy's in seven on seven and mentally you're trying to make sure the operation's correct and that his eyes are in the right place and that he's picking everything up. And to Mike's credit, like we talk about maximizing mental reps, maximizing reps when you're not in there. We really feel like he's done that. you know, two of those there's more, you know, hard evidence on the field. But, you know, it's our job as coaches to sift through each of those processes and make sure that we can get a fair evaluation on both guy. >> Is Michael going to play in his last? >> It's really not a question for me to answer. I might at around close to 120. How pleased are you with the way you guys handled that to where attempts wise they're kind of [clears throat] >> Yeah, it was a um very strategic in how we approached it. So to have a guy that's a team's guy, a first round pick, a guy that has a really bright future, a guy that you know is going to be all pro pro bowl, that's our goals for this year. To have that type of love and respect from him and him want me to play next to him, that meant a lot to me. So at the at the very get to see a tackle that had that love and respect for me, man, I was willing to do and go to lengths for this guy for his career to be better. I tell him all the time, I said, "Man, if I have to make myself look bad on a play or I have to do something on a play so that you can look great, and it's not that he asked me to do that, but I'll do that for him." We hadn't even gotten into the type of football player he is, but the type of raw talent, the type of ceiling, um, you can't even see his ceiling, I don't think, and he just has so much potential. But for me, man, I've never been just about the football. For me, it's the type of dude he is. like this is a great young man that's 23 years old. Uh that carries himself like he's 30. Um that is able to be coached. Not it's not like I'm coaching him that much, but he's able to see where he can get better. You see him growing. You see him want to be great. A lot of times you get guys that are, you know, I guess you can't say a lot of times, but very rarely you get a guy that's 6'8, this type of stature and size with this amount of a athletic ability, but at the same time, he wants to be great. He wants to be coached. He wants to see how he can be better. on top of all of it, he's a good human being. I just think it's rare. I think his parents did a great job. He's always smiling. He brings energy. Um, love playing next to this guy, man. >> Same question for you, Amarius. What do you like and respect about Dalton, >> man? So, I'm a big football guy. So, I remember whenever the buzz started coming in about Dalton possibly coming on a visit. So, I remember hitting my agent up. You can ask him word for word. I said, "I need all information on this guy." >> [laughter] >> Like me, like being a big football guy, the um the Vikings O line, they had a pretty good O line. I remember from Darashaw over to O'Neal and I just remember seeing like some film on dog. I was like, "Oh, he plays hard." And I was like >> whenever he came on his visit, hopefully I got to see him. I don't think I I don't think we ran into each other. Maybe we shook hands maybe. But um I just remember we signed him and I was very happy about it. I was like, "This guy plays hard. He does it the right way." Um like I said, um and that's what you want in the old line, man. You want as your guard, I mean, and I was very I was very I was very happy with that. I was very pleased with the decision whenever he finally decided to sign. Um like I say, I started off with um um Cody and um Lucas and just going with those guys, but ultimately it was me and Dalton at the end of that. Um and like I said, we've we've grown closer on and off the field, man. I'm just thankful for the brotherhood that we have. Um we talk every day, uh whether that's about football or just about, you know, just like stuff off the field. And you know, we've gotten close since um since we got on the field with each other. we continue to get close because I just feel like to be a good old line, you got to be you got to be tight, man. You got to know this guy's why. He got to know my why. Like I got to know why he ticks. He want to know why I tick. Cuz like you want to like you got to understand like you're also playing for yourself, but you're also playing for I'm playing for him. I'm playing for his family. He like I got to feed my family. He has to feed his family. Ted has to feed his family all the way down from stealing no. So, like I said, when I feel like when you take the selfishness out of it, um I feel like he's one of the most selfish guys I've ever played with, man. He just it's always what can I do? Uh how can I help you? And instead of like what can you do for me? So, that's what really like, you know, made me grow close with Don. So, >> so when I hear that from each of you guys, I do pick up a big brother, little [clears throat] brother vibe. Not in the sense that the big brother is teaching all the lessons, but in terms of how close you guys have become despite the age difference. Yeah, for sure. I think it's sometimes crazy. I mean, I have five I have four brothers. I have two older, two younger, and my youngest brother Sheldon is about to be like 25. And the way I view my little brother Sheldon is like, that's a little that's a little baby boy. You know what I mean? And then like Mims, I'm treating him like he's my buddy at 30 years old. And I think the other day in in the stretch, I said, "You're 23? Oh my gosh." I don't know if you're thinking he's big brother because of his size, but uh man, I [clears throat] he is like a little brother to me, man. But he's also more more than a little brother, I'd say, is a friend. And I want to see him succeed. And that's when you know that in my opinion, Dan, that you're going to have success. What I've found is it's not always the closest team, but man, when you have close-knit teams like this, and I don't want to let Mims down, and I feel that. I go to practice every day, and I might be fighting for my job. I might be fighting to be in the league another year, start another year, all these things, but like I don't want to let Mims down, and I don't want to let Ted down. Like, I think about that. I don't want to let Joe down. I don't want to let Scott Peters down. So, like when you're thinking those things, man, I think that's when you have a great team. So, it's pretty exciting. >> You joined the team about a week before the season began last year. Do you remember walking into the room and seeing him physically for the first time? >> Like him, I knew of Mims from the day he was drafted. I mean, I'm a football guy like Mims. not as much of a football guy and I hate to even admit that but I mean during the season we literally our O line coach and us we all ask Mims for the scouting report the injury report like this guy has all the information so like if if there's breaking news he knows first if there's like he knows all of this man guys coming off IR guys switching a like he just he's a football guy he cares about it so even though I hadn't met him I had known about Mims man I'm close with Justin RScotti and Ruscotti got here a couple years before I So, I'd already been talking about MEMS when making the decision to come here. Like, I think people forget like there was a lot of options for me. And I'm not acting like I'm this highly touted. It's not like I got paid a ton, but in terms of what I was willing to accept, there was numerous teams I had went on visits to. And if he doesn't think the big reason I came here is because of him. He's crazy. If you watch that guy on film, you say that's a guy that I can play well play well with and want to play well with. >> So, Amarius, he was in two padded practices before the season opener last year. He winds up playing almost the entire game against Cleveland and plays great. Ted Carris had the famous statement, "This is the most stunning display of football professionalism I've ever seen." What did you think of what he did the first time you guys played together? >> I just, man, like I say, it just shows of how much a vet this guy is, man. I just know when I was first thrown in the fire, whenever Trent went down my rookie year, my head was spinning. Like I just remember, oh my god, I'm standing on the sideline when he got hurt. Like Cody's about to go in. Coach like, no, you're about to go in. Like that's what we drafted you for. Get in. But like, like I said, it just shows like how much of a pro he is, man. Cuz most guys will get in like like I said, Cleveland Brown, like Cleveland Browns have a good defense, man. So for him to get in and play how he played and just take the communication. Just only being here a week, man, just shows how much of, you know, a good player he is, man. Like I said, a lot of guys can't do that. So, it's a testament to him and how he's wired and how he just, you know, loves the game of football and cares about his teammates coming in a week and, you know, getting thrown in the fire against a, you know, instate rival and then a AFC North opponent. So, it just goes to show how much of a football player this man is. So, >> it wasn't smooth start to finish, [clears throat] excuse me, last year. >> You lost your job in week two, Amarius. I know you felt you played badly in week four against Denver. How did you guys help each other through the ups and downs of last season? >> I I I think Mims is such a pro that to be honest with you, I think I'd be giving myself too much credit if I had to go to him and help him get through the ups and downs. But I will tell you that, you know, for me, it's always seeing Mims for the positive things that he does. So, if I ever see him being down on himself, I I try to remind him of what he's really great at, next play mentality. I think he does the same thing for me. I can speak to when we played next to each other and what worked for us was, "Hey man, let's go out there and take a one play at a time throughout this game. If we see things that we think we can make mid-game adjustments, that's fine. But one thing I always valued about Mims is like during the game it gets hectic and you know, say we have a TE and both of us are like, "Hey man, we have no clue how we just got beat on that." Right? Maybe I didn't get over and punch and I didn't push my guy to him. Maybe Mims turned his shoulder. Who knows what it is? But every time we came back to film on Monday for being 23 years old and in year two last year, the way he was able to come back and digest the film and see his wrongs um and me see my wrongs. You expect that a guy in year eight, but not for a guy in year two with his raw athletic ability, I gained so much respect for him. So, uh I think he helped me through the ups and downs by what I mentioned at the beginning. He always supported me, always was a fan of me, always liked the idea of playing next to me, and that meant a lot to me. Um, but when it came to him, I think for me, just speaking positive life into him. >> How did he help you, >> man? Like I said, man, I remember just >> like you said, week four was not a great game for me. And I, like I said, dog mention week four and week two, Dan. Come on, man. [laughter] >> Week four, I promise. >> Jaguars again, >> there's plenty of Yeah, man. Week two and week four was just it was just not good games for me. And like I said, man, like what you need in that time right there is just just for me, I just needed to just accept the fact that, you know, this is not my best performance. I never want to put that on film again. Like I said, nobody plays a perfect game ever. They're like the greatest guys in the league have had horrible games. It just is what it is. And I'm very fortunate to have those games early rather than late and grow from those. And it's just good. Like I say, you have vets in the room who have he's been playing a long time. I'm sure he's had a bad game before, even when we played together, but it's just how you overcome those bad games. And then two, at a young age, I had to realize from guys like him in Orlando, just do not let one bad play or a couple bad plays affect the whole game cuz there's times where I would get down on myself, but you can't you can like you can't let it because it's like it can it can ruin a whole game. And I rather I rather have two bad plays in the game than have a whole whole game where I'm just all over the place and I'm a mess. And really, like I said, the main reason he helped me is just realizing like, man, we're in this together. You know, O line's hard. It's the like it's literally five is one. You can't play. It's not one guy messes up. We all look bad. So, just realizing that these guys have my back and just realizing that it's not going to be perfect all the time. It's just how can we move forward and how can we make it better and how can we fight and win this game. That's all that matters. Like I said, we're we're fighting our like we fight our butts off and we know it. It's just the fact of just like just [clears throat] we got to understand that we may not get the the national the like the national credit that we deserve on some like sometimes, but as long as we know as a five we're playing good together, we're with each other, we have each other's back, that's all that matters, honestly. So, >> all right. I had the gall to mention a couple of bad games. Let's talk about the last seven games last year when you became the full-time starter at Right Guard. PFF graded the Bengals number five in the NFL in pass blocking success over the last seven weeks. What clicked? Why was there such a dramatic improvement for the entire offensive line over those last seven games? >> I think we kept grinding. We always had it in us. We were doing those things early on. Mims makes great points in terms of sometimes the national media, sometimes even local media can get fixated on something and not [clears throat] be aware of where you're growing and where you're working to. And we kept our heads on straight the whole year and we kept working. We never quit. We continued to believe in ourselves. We continued to gel. We continued to fight for each other. And sometimes it takes time and we started to jail towards the end of the year and we started to get it figured out. We started to figure out Scott Peters. I tried I started to figure out Mims and Ted and they figure out me and we started to build this continuity. And with time, man, this practice makes perfect. And in the game of football, nothing's perfect. But I think just with time we just aged well and we just continue to get better throughout the year and we saw it start to pay dividends. And if we hang our hat on that, we'll come out and we'll have an awful game one and it it won't be what we want. But we're not hanging our hat on that. We're going back to work in camp now. We're leaning on each other again. And I mentioned it earlier, but you you know you're going to be great when you really enjoy the guys around you. I mean, we laugh all the time. You see us at practice. You see us in the locker room. Like we enjoy each other. And I think that's dangerous for opposing teams. >> Your thoughts on the last seven, >> man? Like I said, man, it's just I feel like we just really had to get in the classroom. Like I said, where I really had to just like sometimes it's good as a old line to just get the uncomfortable out. Just as a as a man, I feel like it's hard to just be like, "Okay, I was wrong." Or, "Hey, like I did this." But once you do that and once you're like vulnerable enough to like understand like where you need to grow in areas that you know that you don't want to say, that's when I feel like once you like realize like what you're doing wrong and what needs to be fixed, that's when you become a [clears throat] good pro, a good football player and all that good stuff. And like I said, man, we had some uncomfortable talks in the O line room. Um teammate to teammate, coach to teammate. like um coach Peters told us what we need to he he listed a whole a whole thing like a whole like literally every person on our O line what we need to get better at and I had about three or four things and then like I said I took it personal and we just had to go to work and I just feel like we did a good job of that and that's how we you know we we practiced on it and I just feel like those last seven eight games is when we really started to jail because like we had those uncomfortable personal conversations and we were able to fight through it and like understand each other to a deeper level and just like like I said play harder for each other because like I said, we weren't winning as much, but it was ob it was obvious we were getting better and like I said, we don't want to hang our hats on how we finished the season, but we do want to like >> ascend from there. >> Yeah. >> So, >> when the season ended, you were a free agent. The day after the season, you talked about it with reporters. We have footage of Amarius in the background campaigning for you to come back. And the thing that you said to me that day, Omarius, was, "I am campaigning for the best right guard in the NFL to return." How much did you appreciate him going to bed for you? >> I appreciated him lying. Um, I I believe in myself a lot. I'm a good right guard, but I thought that was great. Um, >> but man, I will say like even my wife, she said something that actually stuck with me about what Mim said. She was talking to someone after the season and she was talking about Mims and what he said and she said, "You know, the cool part about what Mim said is no one made him say that." Like she's like, "Dton, were you like going up to Mims?" Like I'm like, "I didn't I never went up to Mims once and said like, "Hey man, help get me back." Like for him to care enough to say something that kind and to want me back is like that's a really special thing, man. I've been a lot of places and I've met a lot of guys I have great relationships with. But I will say one thing, you know, I've never had teammates like Ted and Mims. I think the those were the two main ones that like really campaigned for me to come back, man. And I never asked them to do that. No one told them they needed to do that. And that's something I'll carry with me my whole career, my whole life. Um that meant so much to me. And that's why I want to come back. Like that's why when it came to free agency, I free agency was in a week and I I could have probably made more in free agency. I'm just I'll just say that like I we had went to the combine. There was discussions. We all know how free agency works. I I probably could have gotten a a bigger contract somewhere else. This is where I wanted to be. I You don't have Mims at another place. You don't have Ted Carris at another place. You don't have OB at another place. So, um at length it meant a lot. That's for sure. >> You got your wish. Yeah, [laughter] like I said, man, I just saw what we did in a short amount of time and how we went from literally not knowing each other, just knowing of each other, going through the worst parts of our, like I said, the worst parts of the season together and then going to the best parts of the season together and just in those short amount of time. So, that's imagine what we can do literally having over almost a year up under our belt knowing each other now and then going into the season, how much better we can be. Like I said, we're playing beside each other. I'm very familiar with him. He's very familiar with me. I know what makes him go. He know what makes me go. And it's just, like I said, the sky's is the limit for us, honestly. >> let's wrap it up with this. There's a lot of enthusiasm in Cincinnati for this team. I think rightfully so. But before your first practice, Zack Taylor stands up in front of the team and writes six and 11 on the board. That was your record last year. I know that you've taken that message to heart. Yeah. In the sense that, hey, >> optimism is great. >> Yeah. But we've got to be humble and do the work to prove that we're better than that. >> Yeah. For me, I just appreciated it because that's the truth about what we did last season. And I'm more of a realist. I I think the enthusiasm and optimism in town is awesome and you want fans excited and you want to be excited as a team. And all the additions that the front office made is great, but like I'm more of like, hey, we have to put in the work. If we just sit here and relish with the fans, relish with everyone else, and act like we're great, I don't think that we're going to have the team that we want. But if we can just say, "Hey, we were six and 11 last year. We have work to do. Who cares what we look like on paper? We got to freaking grind." Because that's that's why we became a good offensive line last year. Literally, the whole reason is we we blocked out the outside noise. We focused on us and we kept growing. So, I think we need to do the exact same thing now. And I think that that can lead to success this season. >> You see it happening 100%. Short and sweet. I like that. [laughter] I'm just saying >> you're not talking. You're all about business. >> No, I'm just saying 100%. I'm I'm just very excited. >> You know, we got the other side of the ball. I'm very excited about them. >> And a full year of everybody coming back. >> big brother Dalton Risner, little brother. The only time you ever called little, not so little brother, Amarius Bims. Thank you so much for your time. Have a great healthy season. Appreciate you. Appreciate you.

title: Browns Legend Joel Bitonio Joins the Show! - The Bark Tank - 8.25.26
text: It's the Bark Tank, everybody. Hello, friends. Yes, we have a quarterback decision. We'll get to that shortly. [music] Let me tell you though, the Bark Tank is presented by Spectrum, built for big moments and here for Cleveland. >> [music] >> I am here in the home office today. My name is Andrew Siciliano. We thank you for joining us. As you join, yes, you know and I know and we all know that Deshaun Watson is the Browns starting quarterback. We will get to that coming up shortly. I will also tell you that coming up shortly, friend of the program and now, welcome to the dark side, member of the media, Joel Bitonio will join us as well. He and I spoke immediately after the game with the tornado watch um having hit and the dark skies and the rain like it was a scene Saturday with all the weather at the stadium. We had a delay of an hour. Joel and I on the field after the game. He might have a future in this business. That comes up in a second. All right, you know by now Deshaun Watson is the starting quarterback. It is what you got to know. Todd Monken wants to win games and he thinks this is going to give the Browns the best chance to win the games. That that that's it. Big picture. Go to Jacksonville week one, Deshaun Watson, it's your team. After that, Shedeur Sanders is the number two. Browns open at the two tough road games. That is significant here, certainly. It's week one at Jacksonville, week two in Tampa. Deshaun Watson is the starting quarterback. Monken on Monday said, yes, not only best chance to win, obviously, but he said it was close. And he said that Shedeur took the news well. He told both quarterbacks in his office on Monday separately, Deshaun first, Shedeur second, but that Shedeur had a smile on his face the entire time and that he, in Monken's words, understands the long game. Okay. And that it's not a week-by-week thing. It's about winning in Jacksonville. Again, it was close. He said from the outside that it's not about one practice and not about one game. It's about the entirety of the 6 and 1/2 months since he got there to Berea, to the Cross Country Mortgage Campus as head coach. And that he has to take everything into consideration, and that he thinks Deshaun right now gives the Browns the best chance to win. That's what the fans think. He says, "Ultimately, the fans want us to win, and he wants and they want a good product on the field. When we don't," Monken says, quote, "I understand their frustration." He understands it. He says Shaddur has closed the gap. He says Shaddur is a developing player, and that Shaddur, again, I'm going to say this, understands Look, ultimately, the coach is paid to win games, okay? He's paid to win games, and right now that's on Deshaun. That's on his shoulders. As a first-year head coach, as any head coach, the coach has the authority to figure this out, and if he thinks this quarterback or this player at any of the 22 starting positions gives the team the best chance to win, then he's got to make that decision. I love Todd Monken. I'm going to say this. I've said this repeatedly. All my interactions with him >> [snorts] >> as good as any that I've had with any head coach, anywhere at any time, truly. And he's going to go with his gut, and his gut says it's Deshaun Watson. I think Deshaun handled his Monday press conference well. He came out. He apologized for Saturday. He said that he understands, like Monken, fans' frustration, and that he wants to win, and he's got to earn the fans' trust and respect by winning football games, by playing better. Now he has a chance to do that. And that chance begins Saturday, not this Saturday, but it begins week one in Jacksonville, September 13th, and then the game in Tampa the next week, week two on the 20th, against the Buccaneers. As for this Thursday, this Thursday, neither Deshaun nor Shedor will play. So, it's going to be Dylan Gabriel getting the start, and it's going to be a lot of Talen Green. I'm excited for Talen Green. Nathan has told you repeatedly how excited I was on draft day when they, the Browns, took him in the sixth round. I jumped up in my chair in the studio in Berea because I was that excited to see him play, and I said, "You know what? The preseason's going to be fun because of Talen Green." >> So, we get that chance coming up this Thursday when the Browns close out the preseason at home. It is an Amazon game, a Prime Video game with Al and Kirk and Kaylee in the building. A lot of Talen Green in the second half. I think you're going to like him. I think you're going to like him a lot. What else did we see this past Saturday? Let's run down the good. I thought Shedor played pretty well in the first half. I think you guys all saw that as well. I think Luke Floria, how cool of a moment was that for a kid who grew up in that stadium with Brown season tickets, who grew up in Mentor, and went to Kent State, and then to score a touchdown at home, wearing the orange helmet, that's that's pretty cool. I'll be honest with you, I kind of got emotional calling that. Like, how cool is that? I've imagined doing that. I don't have Luke's ability. I don't. So, I can't even imagine what that was like for him. That's pretty special. Thought Austin Barber held his own at right guard. He was throwing guys out the club. When the Browns took him, offensive lineman from Florida third round, you're like, "Maybe a swing tackle? Could [snorts] he be your right tackle? Could he eventually develop into your left?" Well, Spencer Fano is your left, but either way, he's a piece of your future on that old line. Maybe maybe that future is at right guard. He looked pretty good. So, that was the good from the game. Special teams also a good Cole Wilson a nice return. Andre Smith keeps nailing his kicks. Corey Bojorquez with another nice punt. West Paul also looked pretty good. I thought Winston Reid continued to play well on defense. That is significant and moving Mike Hall outside that's a big deal with the Alex Wright injury. If Mike Hall can stay healthy, he is a force whether it's inside and now potentially outside as well. All right, those are the positives. Now the negative. I mentioned Alex Wright. That is just a kick in the gut and you feel for him because hey, he's he's he's worked so darn hard to be the leader and to be the ascending football player that he is. I mean, it was a gut punch. You kind of had a feeling that's what the injury was when it happened on Friday. You were hoping and praying that somehow it was just a strain. Somehow it was just a pull. Somehow it was just a sprained ankle, but it wasn't. It's a torn Achilles and he is out. So, Alex Wright's done for the year and you hate it for him and you hate it for the team. The good news is they signed Derrick Barnett a veteran who's been in the system with the Texans and with the Eagles same system and Derrick Barnett should slide in there and give you some valuable leadership in the locker room and in the position room with Jacques Cesaire but also more importantly get after the passer and to play some good football. Joel Bitonio played amazing football when he was with the Browns. He also did an amazing job on the sideline on the sideline on the News 5 broadcast and up in the booth with Joe Thomas and Chris Rose during that weather delay on Saturday. Full disclosure, we did this right after the game. so before the quarterback decision was announced on Monday. Joel Bitonio, everybody. >> So, this is the Bark Tank postgame with a sideline reporter, Joel Bitonio, and I think we can bang this out before it rains, buddy. >> It's starting up here, but we can get it done pretty quick. >> So, clearly this is on the field immediately after the game as the rain is about to fall, and we don't know what Todd Monken's going to do. He's about to address the media. Joel, let's let's play it this way cuz by the time this posts, he may have already made his quarterback decision. Let's start with Shedeur. He had the first half today. Give me the case for Shedeur Sanders starting week one at Jacksonville. >> I think he looked good. I think he's your young, most potential. You see the big plays. You saw the touchdown pass to Florio. There's some big moments there. I thought he had command of the offense better today, and it was an improvement from one week ago. >> And last week, when he came into the third quarter, he also had some big moments. Like they brought the blitz, he got hit, he stood in there, he hit Floria again downfield for a 35-yarder. He seems so much and Nathan and I mentioned this in the booth today. Whether it's the footwork or not running out the back door, he's calmer in the pocket. It is slowed down. Not getting through your reads is another thing, but the line gave him protection today and he had time to do that. >> Yes, I I would agree with that. The line played a lot better for him this week, and that showed. He was more comfortable, but he's been at peace with it. I think he's been at peace with his competition, and that's really good to see in a young quarterback. >> So, let's look ahead to week one. It's on the road, two games on the road, and these are two teams that have playoff aspirations. Jacksonville made it last year. Tampa was oh so close. They needed help on week 18 and didn't get it, but it's going to be tough weather, tough defenses. Jacksonville plays a lot of zone. Does that factor at all? >> I think there's a factor there, you know, you have Deshaun who has so much more experience. He's played a long time. He probably can see through the zones a little bit better. When you're playing man, it's like, is my guy open or not? Zone, you have safety help, you have corners rolling, you have linebackers dropping out. You're not really sure what you're seeing. That could be a benefit to Deshaun. Before this game, I would say Deshaun was probably the favorite. Sanders put out a better performance this week. We'll see what coach Monken wants to do. >> So, I know you were a man about town shaking hands and kissing babies on Thursday. You and Joe Thomas, the Hoff, were wandering around at at the CrossCountry Mortgage Campus for the joint practice. Did you get any real read on either of those guys? Let's start with Shedeur at the joint practice. >> Um I missed the first part, but I got to watch the last two. I think both of them had really big plays. There was a couple nice moments for each guy. It's hard in joint practices cuz those are like, "Hey, we're going to only run first down plays here. We're only going to run third down plays." Both did really well. At the Detroit Lions. >> And Ndamukong Suh and Nick Fairley. I was a little bit more nervous for that game than I was for calling the sideline. >> Chris Rose, Joe Thomas, and Aditi Kinkhabwala. But you nailed both. I have no doubt. Ndamukong Suh didn't beat you, did he? >> No, he was mostly playing over Greco. I got I got Fairley, so I we only played two series. So it was it was good. >> I mean, Suh and Nick Fairley, I love them, but they they they don't want to play in the preseason. >> That's one thing I learned that game. I was very nervous. [laughter] >> Ndamukong Suh, obviously a fantastic career and now a fantastic podcast as well. This guy, a fantastic career and a fantastic profession and a second career coming up in the media.
