Because then everybody else can really soak up and understand what the offense is asking of you. You're not going out there and running plays. You're running the offense. And so then it changes the way that everybody goes out there and performs. You got young guys able to make big plays because they know exactly what they're supposed to do when the quarterback doesn't have to think about anything else. >> Yeah. And the other on the other side of the ball, you have Deario Davis. He's your mic linebacker. He's worked with Aaron Glenn, of course, in the past. AG is calling signals out there and you know that 56 is going to get everybody lined up. Another thing about making Fitzpatrick number 29, you never know where he's going to line up on the field. He's moving all over the place. >> Yeah. And that's a huge weapon, right? We talk about some of these better teams. See, the Seahawks are one of those ones that you really talk about where you have somebody that can line up all over the field. It really puts a strain on the offense because you don't know where that guy's going to be. You don't know what position he's at. And now it's making you really confused on the offensive side. So, that's a that's a great weapon. And Deario Davis is a guy, he's a heavy hitter. We saw him on Friday making big plays. You know, he's cerebral. He's a guy that really understands what he's looking at. He's been around for a long time. >> All right. So, coming up on the other side, we're going to bring in one of the starters of camp. That is Mason Taylor. But in fact, earlier today, I asked quarterback Gino Smith what he thought about the secondyear tight end's progress. >> You know, I always liked Mason. Um, I watched a ton of college football, so I knew who he was. you know, he made a lot of plays at LSU and uh also know about his dad and all that, but you know, he's a guy to me who's like that safety net. Um he always he's always in the right spot. Um he's got great hands, he runs great routes, he's a big physical guy, he can block well, and you know, it's only his second year, so he's going to continue to get better. And um we put a lot of work in in the offseason. He was always willing to get out there. It was super hot, but you know, he didn't mind it. Uh South Florida kids seem to be that way. Um, but he's a guy who I think is going to be a great player in this league for a long time. >> You are watching training camp live presented by Honda Eric Allen alongside Quincy Anunoa. We're now joined by Jets tight end Mason Taylor. Mason, from your perspective, what's been the biggest difference for you in year two? >> I feel like my confidence is definitely up there. Um, I feel like I have a little bit more experience under my belt. So, everything moving a little bit slower for me and that's that's been a good thing for me. And you know, building off of that and keep building off of that confidence is going to be important for me. >> Kind of building off of that, right? I think the biggest thing I see a lot of times for rookies is you don't really get a break, right? You go from draft prep right into training camp or at least OTAAS. So, how do you feel like that has kind of changed for you now? And has it helped you a lot more having that time? >> Yeah, 100%. I mean, getting your body right in the offseason was the biggest thing for me. I mean, going from the senior bowl to the draft process to uh rookie mini camp to OTAAS, I mean, it's just a a whirlwind of a bunch of things. So getting that time off to spend with your family, then you get your body back into shape was good for mentally and physically. Uh so now we're ready to go. >> All right. A lot of great plays out there on both sides of the ball today. Long practice. Yeah. >> One of my top highlights was you and seven on seven. Can you take me through that one up the sideline? You had a pretty good defender on you make a Fitzpatrick but make and you came down with it. Yeah, I mean, uh, Gino threw a great ball on a outbreaking route, kind of like a sail route and I just went up there to go high point it and, you know, made the catch. So, I was It was a great throw by Gino, though. Props to [laughter] him. >> Yeah, definitely. I mean, little little self-disclosure, I played with Gino when he was back here the first time and, uh, you know, one thing I always like about him is that he's willing to give you an opportunity. How excited are you about that this year with a guy that's going to throw that ball and whether you're open or not, he's going to give you a chance? >> Yeah. No, I mean, that's great to hear as a receiver. Um, but doing things like that in practice, like showing that trust, um, that you'll make the play, you'll you you will keep the ball out of harm's way is important. So, building off of those things and keep doing that, uh, builds not only my confidence, but his as well. >> How valuable was that opening drive for you guys as a unit to play with Gino in a game like in a game against the Steelers? I know it was preseason. You guys are looking forward to the Titans in week one for the regular season, but that was the first time we saw the first unit out there in game action. No, that was awesome. I mean, it was definitely exciting and the outcome of the the drive marching down the field like that. I mean, it was definitely fun to see. Um, and Gino led us. Um, we had a great long drive and I mean, we made plays, converted third down. So, I mean, everything you wanted on the first drive and yeah, it is preseason, but going out there from, you know, going against your team in practice every single day, doing that against another team is is definitely important. >> I want to have a little fun here. Um, your dad was on Dancing with the Stars, right? Um, is there gonna be a chance that when you score a touchdown this year, we'll see a couple moves. >> Maybe a couple. Not not like Dancing with the Stars, though. I can't dance like that, but maybe a couple. I might might have to get creative here and there, you know. >> What are your thoughts now offensively where you guys are at? This was the final training camp practice. You guys have the game Friday night, final cuts Sunday, and then before you know it, prep really ramps up for the regular season. >> Yeah. Um, like practice has been great. uh getting getting to the back end of this this uh fall camp has been great. Uh and just I feel like our offense has been taking that step each and every day. Uh today was a long practice like you said. I think we put together some really important drives, move the ball pretty well. Um and I think we we we know what we have. We know what we could do and we have a lot of guys that can make plays on offense and I think coach Reich is going to put us in positions to succeed. So, it's just exciting uh taking that step each and every day through training camp and putting it all together today, showing what we could do and then on Sunday as well. >> One of the things this guy keeps on talking about, he says 85. Yep. He's popping there in the pass game, but you've improved tremendously as a blocker. What's gone into that? >> Just uh time and work. I mean, trying to be as consistent as possible. That was my main areas I wanted to do. I showed flashes of it last year, but I think to be more consistent playing in and play out, you know, not having mental errors or any of that type of stuff, technique errors. A lot of it was technique. Uh, so harping on that and individual drill before after practice and just getting those things square win. >> The other thing that you told me in the offseason was, listen, I was okay with the production last year, but I really want to work on yards after the catch >> and getting down the field. How has that developed here this summer? >> I think it's been pretty well. I think it's been pretty well. Um, you know, and again, that's confidence. Like I said, building that confidence with your run after the catch, having a plan with the ball. Um, and that mentality of the first person is not going to bring me down. So, having that mentality and those three things, you just keep working on it and you'll start to see improvement. >> South Florida guys, your quarterback's based down there. He was telling me >> today in fact, that you got in a lot of work passing together in the off season before camp even started. What were those workouts like? >> Oh, they were awesome. I mean, they were hot, I'll tell you that. [laughter] >> Florida is no joke. And we're on that turf, but it was great work. Um, and him being down there, it was a tremendous opportunity for me, not only him, but me as well, to get to get work with him, and it was it was awesome. So, it was definitely a benefit of him being down there. >> What's it like working with a veteran who's seen it all in Gino? and Quincy touched upon it before, but as far as just him, his command in the huddle and then also, you know, you're going to get a good look in terms of what he's seen pre- snap. >> Yeah, like you said, I mean, experience, his his he's he's a vet. I think his experience is takes over on the field and just learning from that as a young guy is definitely really important. Just seeing how he moves on and off the field. Um, I think it's one of those things that you got to take take it everything in like a sponge and just learn from it. I think uh the tight end room is one of the most exciting rooms this year. Honestly, you guys, the four of you guys have been making plays, right? We're excited to see Kenya Zadique. How much do you guys feed off each other's energy in there? >> Oh, we I mean, we have a great relationship, all of us. We're super close. And I think that that speaks to the volume of everyone in that room, the character of everyone in that room, and just, you know, we come out here to work and push each other every single day. Yeah, we make plays and we hype each other up. No one's, you know, we're we're being competitive. Yeah, we're all working for the same job, but we are we are super close and bonded, and that only makes the room so much better. We have so much talent in that room, and that's Reich's job to kind of see what everyone's roles can be uh to help his team. >> What's Sadique like behind the scenes? I mean, we're seeing him run on an adjacent fields. We know he's nearing a return, but as far as how he absorbs the offense, and maybe does he come to you and say, "Mace, what did you see here?" Or is he more just watching the way you guys go about your business? >> Both. I mean, he'll he'll ask questions here and there. He's a little shy at first, but he's starting to open up a little bit. We're getting under his skin a little bit. So, uh, he's awesome and we're going to have it. We're going to be excited for him to have him back, another weapon. And like I said, just take the room and keep building and making that room something special. >> Yeah. >> How cool was it for you guys? You watched the first drive the other night. You're part of that. You're blocking. You made a key catch on that. Garrett's got the third down conversion. And I think you guys went two for two on the third downs there. But Galani's touchdown. Um, >> what can you say about his progress? Because I entering the summer, nobody's talking about Galani Woods. Now he's he's raised some eyebrows. >> Yeah, I mean he's took a tremendous step. Um, he's a a great person, great human, and him coming out here working every single day, works his tail off. He's a huge guy and I mean he makes plays and like I said like he's he's violent in the run game and you see uh last Friday he was violent in the pass game as well. I mean he's getting down downhill. He's 67 lbs running downhill at you. You don't want to tackle that and he punished he punished that dude. So I mean it's just it's just funny. We hype we hype him up on the silent about it. I mean just like like I said that the whole room we we feed off of so much energy in that room and we really are super close. >> Let's get you out of here with this one. You mentioned coach Frank tight end friendly offense and you have a quarterback where everybody's live. So as far as his personnel group has got a lot of options out there. Can you speak to He just said it. Frank Reich was just addressing the media. He said I don't consider that we have 11 starters. We have 15 starters. So you got to have your head on a swivel, right? Because you never know when the ball's coming and also what you're going to be asked to do. >> Yeah. Exactly. like like like I said in practice, that's where it starts. All that trust, you know, being able to move the ball efficiently in 12 personnel, 13 personnel, and installing 14 personnel on the goal line the other day. I mean, the more we could do, the more we could show Coach Reich what we're capable of, the more he could just open endless options for us as tight ends. >> Mason, appreciate your time. >> Thank you. >> Definitely. >> New Jets mini plans are on sale now for the 2026 season. Choose between the green or white plan to lock in the same great seats for four exciting matchups at Metife Stadium. Get yours today at nyjets.com/minans. You're watching Training Camp Live presented by Honda. Eric Allen and Quincy and Nunwa here with our final segment of the summer. It's what you've all been waiting for. It's time to hand out some hardware awards. Most outstanding player here during training camp. >> Uh I think that one has to go to number seven, Gino Smith. He's played really well throughout training camp. He had a great game on Friday, right? to really wrap up exactly how that training camp has been for him. So, this is the guy that's been a leader and I think he is the most outstanding. >> Gino has been accurate. He's showed great command. He's so poised and this is a young offense and I think this is a perfect fit for a guy as far as ball distribution and also just being a leader. >> Yeah, definitely. And I think that it's an offense that's really going to uh enhance his strengths, right? They're also going to give him plenty of opportunity to push the ball down the field which he really enjoys. I think we've been able to see some pieces of this offense, but I can't wait to see what else they bring out week one. >> All right, I'm going to jump around a little bit. How about most improved player from day one of camp until now? >> I think that one has to go to Jordan Clark. I mean, this is a guy where he played some ball last year, but he wasn't exactly where he was supposed to be at times. This year, I feel like he's been in the perfect spot at every time. Sometimes he's been out of position and still made a great play. He's going, he's blowing up screens behind the ball. He's making great plays on the ball. I think just overall this is a guy that's improved, a young player who's really pushing for that spot in the safety safety room. >> Man, I like that. You know, he started on the practice squad last year. He played down the stretch and you see the comfort and that's a tough position to play the nickel spot. >> Obviously, the Jets are hoping D'Angelo Ponds gets on the field as well soon. And I'll tell you what, Jarvis Brownley's been really good himself here during camp. How about most unsung? Maybe somebody flying under the radar. Yeah. So, honestly, I think I'm gonna go with something some people might not might not expect. I'm gonna go with Brandon Stevens. >> Oh. >> So, there was a moment in the joint practices where, you know, he had a pass caught on him and it kind of felt a little bit like last year, but throughout training camp since then, he's been making plays down the field. He's stopped multiple passes that have been that have gone to Garrett Wilson. He's done so many different things in the pass game. He's still that guy in the run game. Um, you know, I'm excited to see where he goes this year. >> That's interesting. How about an honorable mention for Dylan Pum because he's the new starter up front. We didn't hear his name m much much throughout camp and that is a good thing and that guy I think really fit in well throughout camp. >> Absolutely. And you're talking about a guy that came from the Raiders. I think there was a lot of talk about that Raiders offensive line. So for for him to come here and us not to hear too many bad things and kind of see him being a good leader is has been really um improved. >> How about most consistent? You could go with Gino on this one, but where are you going to go? >> Most consistent. I would have to say >> day in day out. >> Dane Beltton. >> I think I think I might go Dane Beltton, right? Um, you know, again, I might be I might be shifting a little bit, but I think Dane Beltton is that guy. I think from day one to now, right, you could probably put him in a different category for what awards we're going to come to, but Dane Beltton has been a guy that has shown up and now we're seeing him push for that number one spot. We're talking about a guy that came from the Giants who was supposed to be a special teams guy, but he's continued to show up and show out every day. >> I like the belton selection. We knew he was going to be really valuable on special teams. He been all over the place on defense. You see Andre Cisco coming on the interception of course against the Pittsburgh Steelers. And the Jets have the ability to play three safeties because we're talking about Ma Fitzpatrick. He can play big nickel and then you can have two safeties out there. Don't forget about Malachi Moore as well. I think this one's going to be easy. >> Top rookie. >> No, top rookie. Got to go to David Bailey. You know, you bring him in as number one. He's been exactly as advertised. He got his first sack last week, making a great play. A quick move, too. You know, this is the guy that we can't wait to see more and more what he's capable of doing. We saw him getting into coverage and people were talking about that. But listen, that the the fact that they're putting that on his plate, there's a reason he's a Stanford grad. He's going to continue to learn. and he's going to continue to improve, but just off the bat, he's making uh guys angry and joint practices, so I'd have to give it to him. >> Yeah, I I just love watching him. He's got a non-stop motor. Not only is he athletically gifted and has that great first step, but we just watched him working with the bags. He's always staying after practice and working on his hands. He wants to be great. He told us >> the greatest feeling in the world is sacking the quarterback. He got one against the Steelers. We don't know if we're going to see him Friday night, but watch out in Tennessee and and beyond. Okay, >> how about a player poised to take a leap >> here in 2026? >> Poised to take a leap. >> How How >> That would have to be Mason Taylor. >> Okay, >> we had him on the show. I think that is the guy, right? Um I've been watching him uh his run blocking has really taken off, you know, multiple times. I'm seeing him move guys off their spot, climb to the second level, move guys off their spot again, making amazing grabs. We saw it today. We're going to continue to see it throughout the season. This is a guy that has had great hands, but now he's even improving in the run game as well. >> All right, final one, and this is going to be our final whistle. What do you know about the Jets right now? And what's your biggest question mark? >> What do I know about the Jets right now? I think that uh I would have to say that what the one thing I know about the Jets is that they're going to push the ball, right? I think in past seasons we've seen them kind of be a little tentative in pushing the ball down the field. I think this year we're going to see some big plays, right? I think that's something that's in Gino's makeup and I think Frank Reich really wants to pull that out of him. He has so much confidence in him. Every time you hear him talk about Gino Smith, he talks about how much he's absorbed the offense, how big of a leader is he is. And so I can't wait to see how much he allows him to just be himself because I think it's going to be a big season for >> Man, that was a good take. How about biggest question mark? >> The biggest question mark is going to have to be right. There's a couple ones, but I think you know in one route I would have to say where are we going in the kicker, right? Well, how is that going to look? How's that kicking room going to look? But I think on the other side of it, right, is um safety room, right? Who's going to play next to Mika Fitzpatrick, right? This guy's pushing, right? We talked about Andre Cisco was kind of in a low, but then he gets that interception. He actually made a big hit in the game as well. Dame Bell has been performing, but that's still a room where, you know, there's going to be some competition and guys behind him will push him as well. So, I think that's going to be one of those question marks that we can't wait to see week one. >> A great transition and this is a bittersweet day for us because this is our last training camp live presented by Honda for 2026. But you know what that means? The regular season is around the corner. We will see you all soon.

title: Jets Training Camp Live: TE Jelani Woods Breaks Down Camp | NFL
text: It is officially the last week of training camp. The regular season is less than 3 weeks away. Of course, the New York Jets are going to open up in Nashville against the Tennessee Titans. Today, they came back to the practice field. They'll have a practice tomorrow, and then the preseason's going to wrap up Friday night as Aaron Glenn will lead the green and white against the Giants. Of course, the Jets last Friday went into Pittsburgh and shut out the Steelers by a 17-0 score. Geno Smith played one drive in that ballgame with seven of seven, and then Aaron Glenn got him out of the contest. Geno picked up where he left off, and that's where we're going to start here on Training Camp Live presented by Honda. Eric Allen alongside Quincy Enunwa. Two-minute situation at the end of practice. Geno came out smoking, and he ends the drive with a touchdown pass to rookie Omar Cooper Jr. >> Yeah, and I think the biggest thing for me is the way it ended, right? Passing it to Omar Cooper Jr., a rookie, a guy that you know has had some up and downs, but I think when you finish off and you do it in a in an unstructured format, that shows that you're able to do it regardless of what's going on around you. >> All right, Q. We're watching Geno right now. The bottom line is if you give him a clean pocket, he is going to beat you. On that two-minute drill, he hits Garrett Wilson up the sideline who goes out of bounds. Quick short pass. Then he goes to Mason Taylor for a couple completions including a long gainer over the middle and then finally he gets inside the red zone with this great anticipation on a pass to Garrett Wilson. Because before Garrett Wilson made the break, Geno's throwing that ball and when number five looks up, it's on his hands. >> Yeah, exactly. He did that multiple times throughout practice. There was a nice touchdown even in the beginning of practice where it was a deep long throw. I think that was also a move the ball period as well. So, it's just good to see the the chemistry between them. Good to see everybody able to perform well regardless of what's going on. >> One guy that you have talked up throughout camp is entering year two. Kind of flew under the radar a little bit because the Jets took Kenny Yeboah with the number 16 overall selection, but Mason Taylor has popped and he did so again today. >> Absolutely and I'm loving what I'm seeing not just in the passing game, but also in the running game. There's been every game that he's been in I've been able to see him show up. And I think you know, when you talk about a guy that was looked at as more of a pass-catching tight end, he's a guy that's shown that he's got the strength, the the the the balance, everything he needed to be a good run blocker as well. >> Hey, a ton of injury updates here today from Aaron Glenn, but before we get to AG, just one note. Joseph Ossai practiced fully today. He had a couple sacks. He was all over the place. >> Just flying around. It's even in the last period as well. You could see him, he was excited to get out there. I think that's what you love to see when a guy's been out for some time, he goes out there with high energy, kind of brings up everybody else. >> All right, let's get that injury report right now from Jets head coach Aaron Glenn. >> I'm excited to have these guys back at practice. So, uh Nate Shepherd was back out on a limited basis. Um Stiggs was back out on a limited basis. Uh Ossai, he's back to going full. Um J.J. Kingsley, um in in Amari, he's back to going full. Sweat's back to going full. Kiko's back on on basis. And um and Trey, he actually had a lip uh in the game, you know, so he's he's just fine. So, excited to have those guys back and man, just getting the update on some of our other guys and the way that they're operating. Um man, I'm excited with the news I'm getting on those guys. So, um again, they those guys still working um through their injuries, making sure that we do the things we have to do to get those guys back for week one. Um still targeting that date for the rest of these guys. I'm talking about Siddiq, Ponzy, um Bruce, where I still talking to those that week. So, excited about that. >> You're watching training camp live presented by Honda. Eric Allen alongside Quincy Enunwa. We're joined by Jelani Woods. Take me back to Pittsburgh Friday night. How good did it feel as far as the way you guys moved down the field on that first drive? >> Uh it felt really good, you know, just being able to execute the plays that you know, we kind of ran throughout the week. Uh course, it wasn't against the Steelers, but uh just being able to execute and um you know, start off fast. You know, be kind of explosive. I'll say, you know, taking care of the third downs, the critical third downs, getting those reps in, you know, that typically leads to success, I guess, starting off the season. Just being able to execute at a you know, starting off fast at an early pace. So, that was pretty exciting to do. >> I think a lot of people expected this tight end room to be pretty talented, right? I think you've been a pleasant surprise though. What would you make of kind of your training camp so far while you've been here? >> Uh I just put pretty much trying to put my head down and grind, you know, whatever they ask me to do, that's something I take pride in doing. Um and just like I said, my big thing is executing and you know, just put my best foot forward, working hard. So, like I said, whatever they ask me to do, that's that's my thing. I'm going to I'm going to get get it done. >> When you guys were in the red zone the other night and Geno comes in the huddle, did you know that was going to be a touchdown? The one that the little roll out there. >> Honestly, no. I didn't know it was going to be a touchdown cuz you kind of never know. But, you kind of see the defense a little bit when you go walking up to the line and um yeah, it was a quite a surprise for me once I turned around and I seen it was wide open. So, yeah, I just tried to go as far as I can and get in the end zone. >> We'll go a little bit to your background with Frank Reich. Obviously, he was one of your former coaches. Do you see a lot of similarities in offense he's doing now or did he change it up a little bit after being in college for some time? >> Uh I think with the experience of him, you know, going around to different places, he definitely changed it up a little bit. But, um it has some, you know, similarities within, you know, um the past years and now and then going through college, but uh yeah, it's pretty much different. >> You referred to him as a quiet assassin. Why? >> Cuz coach Frank don't talk, man. >> [laughter] >> That's that's one thing. He doesn't talk, but you you understand his presence. And um he he can motivate you with it in different ways and sometimes it's very funny. I'm not going to lie. He's very very funny. [laughter] But, he has that presence to himself that uh he can speak to people without even actually having to say anything. So, um you know, that's why I kind of call him a quiet assassin. Then, of course, there's the play calling and the geniusness of him. Like, he's he's genius. So, he he knows how to move things around in offense and, you know, without getting into much detail, but he he knows how to use everybody also. >> Yeah, that makes sense. I think one thing I saw about your background is that you played quarterback in high school. >> Mhm. >> And I always I always think that, you know, quarterbacks probably have the best hands. You know, you you got to work with the ball the most out of everybody. >> And you really displayed it, right? Do you think that that kind of plays a big part into some of your best catches you've had in training camp? >> Uh absolutely. I feel like that definitely plays a part and then just mentally knowing where to be. >> Yeah. >> I feel like plays a part cuz the more you know what you're doing, the kind of better it is to be able to make plays, you know, and things like that. So, uh like I say, I say 50/50. It's kind of both both >> How How would you describe your career to date? Early round pick of the Colts. Man, you have those injuries. You missed a couple years. You had to have a lot of perseverance to be where you are right now. >> Absolutely. Uh I'll take it a day at a time. That's That's my motto. Every day I wake up, pray, I give God the glory. Like um my parents, I talk to them every day. And yeah, I take it a day at a time, minute at a time, and just enjoying the process, honestly. Like that's kind of my my thing, just enjoy the process. And then uh when it's time to work, it's time to work. When it's time to chill, kind of take my mind off things a little bit. Cuz sometimes, you know, it can be overbearing, but uh just going through the injuries and stuff, I kind of don't look back in the past, cuz you know, it's a new day, new opportunity. So, I kind of just, you know, keep looking forward, and you know, just keep chugging along, honestly. >> What do you think the next week is going to be like? Because you got the preseason game Friday night, and then before you know it, cutdowns on Saturday. >> Mhm. Honestly, I don't know what's, you know, going to happen, but it's just it's, you know, time to ball, time to kind of, you know, hone in on more details of what uh we thinking about running or anything like that. So, it's going to be kind of It's going to be kind of weird, but it's always kind of weird, but uh it's kind of some you know, it takes some time Like, you know, kind of quiet the storm, I guess. >> Well, with that being said, we've watched you throughout training camp. You've made a number of plays. How do you feel about your summer, the body of work you've put together? >> I feel good, but also, you know, it's you got way more uh things I can get better with, way more plays I can make. Uh but I feel good. I feel like I put uh somewhat my best foot forward, you know. >> Do you think this has it your best training camp throughout your professional career? >> This is probably the most comfortable I've ever felt, I guess. Uh I would say like, you know, being Ricky uh it's kind of nerve-wracking and you know, just the the moving of different things and everything like that. But uh you know, my second year, third year, I was always worried about, you know, mentally worried about injuries, you know, and things like that because of what happened. But now I kind of just feel very comfortable. And having great tight end coach um Alfredo, like, you know, he he he's definitely uh like kind of I would say a player's coach. So, he instills a lot in us and then he asks for in return, he asks for us on the field and off the field to put our best foot forward. text: Did you do a lot of center work before this off season? >> Um I was told to start the off season this year it was emphasis for me to get snaps at center. title: Saints IOL Easton Kilty on getting reps at center, learning from Erik McCoy and David Edwards & more
text: Hi, good how are you? >> Did you do a lot of center work before this off season? >> Uh I would say to start the off season this year was emphasis for me to get snaps at center. Obviously the more versatile more versatile you can be the better the better it is for your position specifically especially as an O lineman to be able to play all three positions on the interior and tackle on the outside side. Uh I really emphasize that this off season playing center. So I played a couple couple practices here in training camp just playing center and I getting used to that. So >> And is this your first exposure to center or did you play it anywhere else beforehand? >> Yeah, I guess my first true exposure actually snapping the ball and playing center this year. So >> What do you what do you think about it so far? What do you like about the opportunity? >> Yeah, like it's another opportunity to take advantage of and it's obviously it's not it's not something that's easy by any means but it's you're making calls for the entire offense and it's a role that I'm willing to accept and keep challenging me and I'm keep working at it moving forward. So >> Obviously snapping the ball is different but in in what ways is playing center different than what's the adjustment like beyond the obvious? >> Yeah, so like it a lot of people you see it's you know under center you're in shotgun and a lot of it's it's it's like totally different forward than from where you're at guard or especially when you're at tackle like your your feet are square you got to take you got like the steps the steps in general are just everything has to be on point. You're making the calls you're making you're calling out the coverages and everything just has to be on point for the offense to run efficiently. And especially like just making sure everyone's on the same page as the O line. And it's just it's just it's a whole different like ballgame. It's a lot more to me it's a lot more mental than anything. Just making sure you're on the right page making sure you're making the right calls every single play. >> I assume Eric is a big resource in adjusting to that. >> Yeah. Yeah, like Eric Eric's one of the best centers in the NFL. Like he wouldn't be We're excited. Um like I think he's one of like top centers in the NFL. Like he's a he's he's a great great guy to learn from. You can just get his tips, pick his brain here and there. Like he's he's he's been there, done that. He's He's one of the top leaders in our O-line room. And it just makes us feel able to pick his brain here. Him and Dave Edwards just pick their brain. They've been in the league for a long time now. So it's nice as a young guy to just learn from them. So. >> What do you kind of like about the evolution of the run game uh for you guys from the system last year to what's being implemented this year? >> Yeah, like I like um our like we made our emphasis on this off season just being being more into it as O-line, just emphasizing like that's our main main point of our offense is to O- O- offense goes as our O-line goes. Like we we want to be the leaders up front, being able to emphasize like we're going Hey, we're going to we're going to run the ball this game. We're not going to not going have 30 rush yards a game. Like we we want to be able to run the ball cuz if you run the ball, you open up the pass game. Like everything just moves forward. Like everyone just rallies behind you, the whole offense. So. >> You like that about the responsibility? >> Yeah, like it's it's it's like it's a lot of responsibility, but it's it's it's a great responsibility to have. And it's a lot of It's a lot of learning on my part, just being able to learn the learn the play calls, learn just learn everything. Like you're pretty much just starting over at a new position. So you're learning new footwork, new technique, new new mental challenges, but it's it's all it's all for the benefit of yourself. So. >> And do you do you kind of take the the compliment of like being trusted to learn the calls and communicate everything like that? Like that feels like that's a that's a positive kind of weight you You this in you type of way. >> Yeah, like it's like I I I'd take any challenges is like a a good thing, especially um here just being able to learn like a new position is it's it's something that's fun. That's like having something challenging is fun. And you know what? To learn it just makes if you move move to guard, it just makes your job easier cuz you know what call's going to be made. You know you know like you know what to understand the defense is helps any position in general. So, you know what safety rotation and all that like what what games they're playing like you just it just simplifies everything, especially in the NFL when everything's a lot faster, so. Thank you, guys.

Because they're touching the players, they're helping the players become better. And um so very much very similar, Jeff, to like a draft process. Yes. you're doing a interview that may last five, six, seven hours if you if you combine some of those, right? But you're also vetting that person as well and everybody they've worked with in Sean's case, teammates in Sean's case, um, you know, guys that coached them. Um, and so we felt really good about the person and and what, you know, you want coaches to check a lot of different boxes. Can they help guys get better fundamentally? title: Nolan Smith & More On Their Personal Growth During Training Camp
text: Hey Nolan, thanks for taking the time for us today. We're gonna start with Ed and then go to Mike. >> Yeah. Hi, Nolan. Uh, thanks for doing this. We'll go to Martin and then Jeff. >> Hey Nolan. Um I was curious as far as you're concerned, what's kind of like the biggest difference in you um this off season or during training camp as opposed to last season? I mean, is it health? Is it more than that? Like what did you really want to work on going into this season? >> Um just some some personal things, but mostly, you know, health. Um making sure I can make it through the all 18 and um making sure my arm strong enough. Nolan, obviously you've been a football player for a long time, but when you find out earlier in the offseason that you've got a guy in your position room, uh Joshua, who's never played football before, what goes through your head, uh as far as like expectations for a guy who's never played the game before and then when you look at him now, uh are those expectations exceeded or what's kind of your view there? >> Yeah, man, he's night and day. Um I'm really proud of him um for the effort that he brings and he just plays the game the right way. you know, I try to teach him just play the game the right way and everything that you want to happen for you. And um that's kind of the same approach I take for myself. You know, I try to play the game the right way. Are there any lasting effects from those triceps injuries? And as you go forward here, I know you play a certain brand of football. Is there any way to to try to prevent injuries like that in the future? >> Um, no. It was a bang bang play. You know, um, I'm doing a move going to the ground and stuff like that. It's nothing that prevent it. Um, it's just, you know, last year, you know, the wear and tear of the game and keep tackling and stuff like that. Um, but I had a full year to reheal and, you know, I'm ready to go. Um I and I do play the the game a certain way and there's only one way to play this game and you know I'm gonna keep putting my foot my best foot forward any way I can. >> We'll finish with Ed. >> Hi Nolan. Um just I imagine you were pretty excited when you saw your two dogs get uh new contract extensions, Jordan and Jaylen. Uh do you find any added motivation in that? Do you do you feel yourself thinking, "Hey, I I want to be next. That's what I want." Um, no, no extra motivation. You know, the motivation isn't for the money. The motivation is to build championships and legacies with my brothers forever. Um, not many people say that, you know, you can win a Super Bowl and several national championships together with the same group. And, you know, that's a legacy that, you know, can speak for itself. So, you know, I I don't look into the money aspect of that. You know, we trying to build something special. >> Thanks, Nolan. We appreciate your time. >> Yep. Thank y'all. Hey Jod, thanks for taking the time for us today. We are going to start with Brooks and then go to John. >> I got you. [clears throat] >> Brooks, you're muted. >> I can't hear nobody. >> Sorry about that. I was trying to shout through that. Um, >> what's up? We were talking to Vic last week and he was saying like inside linebacker he thinks is the deepest unit on the team. Yeah, I mean, well, of course, you know, as everybody know, our our room has a standard here and, uh, you know, we had a a great vet, you know, uh, that that knows how to lead the way, that, you know, knows how to impact all of us. Um so I've been playing right guard for the last like seven years. A little bit of center mixed in there. Uh thankfully, I've had experience starting games the NFL at all three inside. So, it's just a matter of kind of getting back into the groove. >> How helpful is it to have guys that you played next to like Elijah Morgan in the room? So, it's not something that I'm foreign to. >> What about Sorry. >> What about coming here? Why why did you want to come here when they called you? >> Yeah, I think for me, um you want to go where you're valued and the Patriots valued me more than other teams. So, um, it's a great organization. You know, it speaks for itself. I've had a rough couple years in some different teams. So, I'm excited to be somewhere, you know, with the tradition that they have here. >> Kind of went off questions. >> Yeah. Um, they were mandated a few years ago for linemen unless you wore a specific helmet. So, it's really just, I think, a push to get guys to wear the new helmets with the new technology. And as someone that's been in the league for a long time and been through many iterations of different helmets, I can say that the newest helmets definitely feel the safest. I don't really know like how you quantify that. But just from like a kind of anecdotal standpoint, like I like the new helmets and then the Guardian Caps is just an added layer of protection on top of that. >> Greg, what was your uh first visit here like? >> What was it like? >> Uh it was thunderstorms and flights canled and delayed. Um, but yeah, coming to the facility, brand new, beautiful. Um, I have a lot of familiarity with players and coaches in the building. So, it was uh it was a cool experience, you know, just kind of catching up with some people I haven't seen in a long time. Um, so I have family that lives up this way in, you know, New England. Um, and then you try and try it out in practice to see if it fits your game and if not then you know you throw it away. Um, and then you just kind of like make things your own. So whether it's you know for me in pass protection I'm a little aggressive. I like to jump set. Um, in run game I probably use my hands a little bit more than my shoulders. So, it's just kind of a byproduct, too, of when I was younger, defenses didn't move a ton and guys were a lot bigger. Now, defenses are getting a little bit smaller, faster, there's a lot more movement. So, you kind of have to adapt and evolve with the game as the game changes. >> I know you haven't been here long, but what are your sort of first impressions of >> uh I mean, he's obviously a stud, like great quarterback, excited to be around him and just, you know, help him if I can and learn from him, you know, on other stuff. Is it difficult for you sometimes to adjust to a quarterback or someone that can lead the >> I think in general it's the only difficulty is like you're not exactly sure where someone's going to set up but I've been with you know last year with Jackson I was with uh Cam Newton um you know Russell Wilson a little bit so I've been with a lot of quarterbacks that are mobile so it's not uh you know I would say that Drake is more someone that can extend plays. He's not someone necessarily that needs to run around to make a play. So, I think that's like what makes him kind of unique and special. >> I know this night didn't go the way you wanted, but what do you remember about Monday night? I >> actually told this to coach Rabes. Um, when we were getting ready to play, you know, we were like pretty fired up to come here Monday night, play the Patriots, and everyone was chirping about how, you know, their schedule and this and that. And there's been a few games in my NFL career where you play against a defense and it just feels a little bit different. And that was like one of those games where they just they were flying around. They were hitting hard and it was a very physical game very early on. Um, and I've been a part of a lot of NFL games, but that one like stood out. So, um, that was another reason why I wanted to come here and be here is because they seem to have guys playing football like the right way. >> Have you reconnected with Christian Ellis about the Jackson? You guys talked about that? >> We haven't talked yet. No, but I'm sure it'll come up. >> Do you see that? I know it's summer, right? So camp to camp, but any change to that since you've been here? >> Uh I mean it's been my second practice. We've been super situational, so uh thankfully there hasn't been, you know, so much violence yet, but uh you definitely tell that it's there. title: Ryan Cowden: "We Have Such a Collaborative Effort." | Patriots Press Conference
text: You just talked to Christian. That's probably the topic that I think some Christians mind. We talked to Elliot this morning. What could you share us just on the organization's stance on where things are? >> Well, I think exactly what you just said there. I think the organization has spoke enough here with with coach, with Elliot, with the ownership speaking. So, I think for me to stand here and say anything other than what's already been stated from those three, I [snorts] I don't think I have them there's enough been out there already. >> Ryan, Elliot spoke to us today, said that the offer that the to Christian that in terms of fully guaranteed. >> I'm just going to go right back to what I said with Mike. There's been enough statements and questions through Elliot, through Braves, through ownership for me to sit up here and go through on that same line of questions. I'm just I don't think there's any use to that. >> Yeah, you know, Kan, first of all, all the best to Kahan. like he made some huge plays for us last year and I honestly I think coming here new and not having past history with Kahan I thought he made tremendous strides from from OTAAS in last year to training camp he came back with a whole different mindset um really did a great job. I'm sure there were some points in time during this process when your name's out there right wrong and different I'm sure it's hard and uh with the other additions it's difficult and he did nothing but handle himself like a pro. Um he did he made some huge plays for us last year and we just wish him nothing but the best. Yeah, Jaylen, excited to see him come in here and and just be part of our program. I texted him last night and just said, you know, just be ready to insert yourself into how we do things here. And that's not the same everywhere. Um, obviously, I think Elliot spoke a little bit earlier about our evaluation of Jaylen through the draft process last year. And look, his his job is to come here and earn a role and compete. Um, there's some traits that we liked and um we're just excited to get him inserted into our program. With Christian's negotiations, do you feel like the sense of urgency increases as the season opener near? >> No. >> How important is Christian to what you guys do on defense? >> Uh, I think like a lot of players, um, whether it be Christian, Milt, Carlton, Marcus Jones, Draymond, like there's all these guys, Splain, I think defense is truly one of 11 and I think it takes 11 guys. So, he's just equally as important as a lot of guys across the front. Brian, boy mentioned adding depth to the roster. Is there any position in particular you look at? >> All of them, right? No. Um, look, the depth thing is is uh we're constantly not happy on the personnel side with or complacent with the depth anywhere. That's just that's just part of our our DNA. Are we are we deep enough at running back, DTackle, edge, corner, all of it? We look at it daily. Um, sometimes players develop faster than you think, sometimes they take a little bit longer. Um, so while they're in those development phases, like I think coach talked about the other day. Part of playing these games, seeing them in these situations, um, part of that seeing how can they develop? And honestly, when people talk about depth, I think a lot of times they just rely that depth usually speaks to experience. Like everybody feels more comfortable because it's experienced. And I think everybody feels more comfortable with depth that way. But a lot of these young guys, I think you just have to it's a trial by fire a lot. >> What do you hope to see from Kyle Williams? >> You know, I think Kyle had a great off seasonason. Um was one of our offseason award winners and and he really put a lot of time in and I think Kyle that room, we've said it, there's a lot of talent in that room and Kyle just what the biggest thing for Kyle is when he gets his opportunities to make the most of them and and he knows that. Um as a receiver, what you can't control is when the ball's thrown to you, but your job is to get open and when you get those opportunities, make them. and he knows that um the other night I know he probably had a couple where he'd want to make maybe a play on but then his numbers called you know and he puts a lot of fear in defenses with his ability to stretch the field. >> Ryan, this is not among the questions that have been asked before. Um is trading Christian a consideration at all? >> I think we're continuing to work on the negotiation side of Christian and you know I think that's where that stays. >> You mentioned Jaylen needing to get himself involved in the program quickly. Some other guys you guys signed midsummer, Hassan Haskins, Greg Van Ro, who got involved pretty quickly, at least from what we've seen. What have you seen from them in their time here? >> Uh, you know, Hassan's a a great guy. I have some history with him from being in Tennessee with Hassan uh when we drafted him there and um just know the kind of person he is. So, I had no doubt that even though he'd been out like he was going to be in shape, he was going to really Han's an all-in guy. Um, and then with GVR, um, I was opportunity when I was with New York, uh, prior to coming that we had signed Greg and watched what he did over these last few years, and I thought Greg's been really impressive, uh, here towards the back end or or age-wise, the back end of his career. But what he's done is pretty impressive. And in a short period of time, watching him the last two days pop in center, both guard spots, three days in, like it, he's really done a nice job. Really a professional approach and kept himself in shape that way. with Brett. You had him in for a try out and then um didn't waited a little bit to sign him. What was kind of the reasoning for not signing him immediately after the workout? >> Yeah, we didn't we didn't actually have a workout. He it was a visit. So sometimes those get reported maybe the same. Um Greg was a visit and I think a visit for Greg was he's a veteran player in this league and I think it's important for him to feel the building out too. What what what do you guys what's the vibe here? You want to sit down with coach? uh we want to sit across the table from him and just talk about the fit, the situation, the role. So sometimes that's part of it before you know then you say, "Hey, we want to make this move." >> Right. I'm just curious. You guys have so many experienced guys in the office. >> You know, we that negotiation like I said, we're going to talk about I'm going to repeat and echo here a statement about the front office is a collective group of people. That that's our front office and I and I think coach mentioned that. Um there's not a front office back office. It's a collective group and that collective group has been a part of this process. >> Brian, when it comes to your core special teams units, you lost some guys to free agency, some other guys that might be banged up. How do you feel about the depth for those units? Are you comfortable maybe having to rely on some of your younger players as >> Yeah, you know, um the trust factor is what it comes down to in the kicking game because those those when kick returns, punt returns, a block punt, those usually you lose games. if you give up return touchdowns and conversely if you if you hit them those help you win and lose games and so that's why it's such a vital piece of the game um and you do sometimes you want to rely on guys who've been there done that um but inevitably you have to lean into these young players and uh Jeremy and Tom do a great job of trying to get guys up to speed they're always dealing with a revolving door of people right we get injuries there's a new guy comes in can you get him ready for punt kickoff so um I think that's why you see so much emphasis put on even in the joint practice ices putting those guys in situations see if we can trust them. >> Brian, speaking for yourself, >> do you have any suspicions about why Tan was available for so long and it just seemed like the return there just interest wasn't there outside the league? >> Uh, you know, I I can't I I I don't know that answer. Um, I can't speak to the market like we always want to see what that looks like all the time, whether that's free agency, whether that's the trade market. um those things are unpredictable and year to year and um I can't speak to that. Like we we made a decision that we thought was best for us and that was the deal with Houston. So um I can't speak to the the marketplace at at all what that looks like whole time. >> Right. When you're constructing the 53 man roster, is it a consideration at all of we might not be able to slip this guy through waivers, we can't get this guy through waivers. Is that a consideration for those final spots? >> Absolutely it is. We sit there and we we try to look around the league. our our pro staff does a great job of canvasing the league through these preseason um this whole training camp process. Where are teams heavy? Where are they light? Where do we think they're going to be active at the at the cut down? Um it's a calculated risk sometimes. Um when you're at the back end of the waiver claim, that's that's a great thing. Uh but it's also, you know, some good players that become available are going to be gone before you get that opportunity. So certainly when we talk about cutting our team down, we do sometimes always or shouldn't say sometimes, we always think about, you know, what's the exposure rate here? How do we feel? Are we comfortable that this guy can get back to us or not? >> Did you anticipate questions? >> Harold Landry not getting back to this point and is there still hope he might make it back on the field? Yeah, anything, you know, that guys have going on injury-wise, that's, you know, kind of out of my realm. I'm not going to speak to that here. Harold's going to do everything he can to get back when he's healthy and and when that is, he'll be back out there. >> Last question. >> I wanted to ask you about the two undrafted guys that seem to maybe have elevated up Jacobs. Just from a scouting perspective, knowing that they didn't get drafted, can you share with us how they landed on your radar? Was there an area scout? >> Yeah, you know, I I sounds repetitive, but we have such a collaborative effort and our postdraft process between the coaches and the area scouts, the nationals, our, you know, myself, Elliot, there's a lot of people, Lonzo. So, um, we get our pro staff involved. So, guys like that that they really do and they sit there and go through a bunch of stuff and rank guys and, you know, Tanner was a guy that was up in the top of that from the post-draft process. Um, a lot of a lot of what he made him attractive to us is his his demeanor, the way he plays the game. There's that play style. You guys have seen it everywhere. The the effort and finish and that that's a real part of what makes Tanner who he is. Um so I would say that's something that stood out in the process for us. Um you know and then you mentioned uh who Oh yeah, you mentioned Khalil like um I happened to be at the Alabama Missouri game u with our area scout Alex Brooks was there at the game and I mean this was all over the place. you just, you know, wasn't a very heralded as the transfer from South Alabama to Missouri finding his space and he was all over the field and um so you kind of leave that game and you're going, okay, who's this guy? And that's a new that's why that live exposure is always good for me. But um then you start tracking those guys that just make plays and again I I shout out to all our scouts. There's there's a number I think they did a great job in the post draft process with a lot of guys here that are competing for spots now. >> That's right. >> Good. Thank you

title: New England Patriots Defensive Coaches Address the Media | Patriots Press Conference
text: What's it been like now all these years later to go against him in these practice? >> Same thing. You know, it's good to see him and Gonzo out there competing. And it's good to see him uh just, you know, being able to be out there and play fast, play aggressive, and uh yeah, it's been just great to see his, you know, maturity. Guys get mature as they get in this league. Been around a couple teams, and so it's great to see him back in in this uh this place. >> What's the uh chess chess match been like with Drake and KP every day? Well, that's probably a better question for them. Um, but again, it's not a one-on-one thing, right? There's 11 offensive guys, 11 defensive guys, but I think it is, uh, you know, cool to see, uh, those guys be able to be out there, whether it's disguising, um, whether it's holding the shell, all those things. Um, I think it's good to go against a seasoned quarterback like Drake and a couple guys at the safety position and in the defensive backfield in general, um, that are able to hopefully give him some different looks. >> Have you seen from Jaylen Reed from afar? or what do you expect him to bring to your room? >> Yeah, I I don't have any expectations right now just because, you know, so focused on the guys we have here. Excited that he's here and looking forward to get started with him. >> I know you have a history as a nickel defensive back coach with the Bills. Is there any overlap for you with the safeties and the corners that slot spot specifically and kind of what is that like how the roles can kind of overlap a little bit? >> Yeah, I mean I think that in this league you see guys that have certain titles, whatever. But um you know I've been around nickels, safeties, corners and coach them all. And I think that the corner position now in my opinion is just as important as any starter, right? You know, uh 5 years ago, 7 years ago, it was just, hey, your next best corner can be your nickel. But now it's a it's a specific position that I think uh you look to in the draft to recruit a certain type of guy and then also we look um to coach him a certain type of way. You know, he has to have some characteristics the safeties has. He has to have some characteristics that corners have and uh you know, we coach it that way. Okay. feel like the the three safety thing is becoming more popular just across the league and like Reed has done that a little bit in Houston. Just how have you seen that evolve and what do you think has led to to that being a more popular package? >> I think that uh just in the NFL it's a cyclical thing, right? So, um you know, for so long, past 10 years or so, it's been uh three corners with the Nickelback and then two safeties. And so, I think now it's just becoming you're seeing some more 13 personnel. you're seeing all these tight ends that are able to give a conflict to a defense because they're able to run block, but they're also able to, you know, run routes and maybe uh uh have a mismatch on a linebacker. So, I think whatever it takes for our defense specifically to be able to match up well, that's what we're going to do. Maybe it takes three safeties, maybe it takes three corners, whatever it takes three linebackers. We're going to try and match up the best we can against the personnel that we get. talking to to By a few times, he's mentioned that it's a new defense for him compared to what you guys did in Tennessee, which I think is cool because you guys have a lot of same coaches. Like, how have you seen it evolve? Is would you say it's a new defense or more of like an evolution of what >> I think it's just been enhanced over the years, right? You never want to stay stagnant, right? That's one thing that Braves always preaches to us. So, every offseason since 2018, you know, he's uh charged us in our own positions to go figure out new ways to do things and how to enhance our defense. We have core beliefs that haven't changed from 2018, but the way those are presented, the packages that we have, they've changed and I think, you know, we're going to continue to evolve and change because the offenses are. And how much is that evolution internal and just what you see with your own team and how much that is adapting to the things that the offenses are kind of doing every year to create challenges? >> I think that's yes and yes, right? You know, uh you want to make sure that you're trying to stay a little bit ahead of the curve, but you're also looking and seeing what teams are doing across the NFL, even if it's teams that you don't play, and kind of see what the next thing that the offense is trying to do and uh try and combat that. But for those guys, just the ability to do that. And really, all the best players at any position have the ability to do things better than a coach can coach it. We try to coach as much as we can, but at the end of the day, it's a game that's not perfect and it's moving super fast with elite athletes. So, there's a lot of stuff that you just make a decision based on, you know, you kind of educated, not guess, but information and pull the trigger when you can, and that's what they do. What have you noticed about Christian, you know, even just off the practice field, maybe when he wasn't able to practice about how he approached meetings and attentiveness and things of that nature behind the scenes? >> I mean, he's been the same guy as far as my dealings [clears throat] with him where he doesn't say a whole lot, but if you look at his notes, he's hearing what everybody's saying. He's taking notes and uh he's at a very high level football IQ and he's been doing that, you know, when he's here, when he's been here, that's what it's been. It's not been anything different. We all know the the things slowing around, but when it comes time to we're doing work with DBs or defensive unit or the team, he's been the exact same professional since day one when I met him. >> There would be human nature, I think, for for somebody who's looking at potentially getting a new contract to be concerned about their physical well-being. Would there be any concern on your end that if Christian doesn't get a contract by the time the regular season rolls around, he might just get some even if it's subconscious on his part. He might get a little less than the full Christian. I don't think so with any player because at the end of the day, uh, when people that evaluate film turn on the silent tape, they don't think about our circumstances. They think about the results. And I think he knows that. I think our players know that. And that's what it's been with each guy through the time we've done this. >> Thank you very much. >> All right. Uh because when you look at it right now and a lot of people don't understand when you watch film and you come in at this time didn't have the spring we do a lot on defense right and so you get a young player like that we're just getting them lined up you know you're getting them lined up know the defense do your job be in the right position you know when he starts mastering that now you got to start working on all right what is offense is trying to do what are the backfield sets right how's this tackle going to set you up and and and and pass where his hands I mean there's so much more to it right now he's just getting lined up, but he is studying his butt off. Um, he he's doing all the right stuff and he's getting better every week. I mean, this kid's going to be a special player. I don't think very many coaches say that right or out the bat where guys going to be here for three weeks. He's going to be a special player. >> I was going to say, how does that attitude get you excited for for coaching, too? >> Uh, I'm not a gambler, but I kind of look at at at, you know, maybe anything in life as gambling. You got a kid that's that's big like him, that's athletic like him, that's meaner in a wet mule. He loves football. not gonna say he's gonna be Jason Taylor or LT or any of that stuff, but it's gonna be hard, very hard for him to fail. And so, um, I know who the who the kid is and what he wants to be and he's going to work at him to be that. So, I'm excited to have him. Excited to work with him every day. Glad he's here. >> Obviously, we haven't seen Harold out here. What level of confidence would you have if if Gabe had to be the back up there on the edge to start the year? Uh, I'd have confidence, you know. I mean, you know, you start look at the base stuff, you know, Herald's the same, Jack, wherever, but uh um again, just the way that he prepares, you know, are there going to be some some uh some learning moments and some things that Yeah, I I've never in all my years coaching and playing NFL, I've never seen a kid come out and just figure it out they weren't. Even if they've had all spring and all this other stuff, they're such a huge part of development and just taking time and making mistakes. You can't learn until you make a mistake. And so yeah, there's going to be some times, but I feel comfortable because I know who the man is and what he's going to the time that he's going to put in and the effort that he's going to put in it. >> Some changes within your group with Harold Francis and then Chase with in Washington. How confident are you that you guys can be productive here starting season? >> I am confident. I I love the addition of Draymond. You know, Ponder is making huge strides. I mean, he made such a big stride from year one to year two. Uh and I think Gabes there when you really look at it when Harold's uh you know not I was surprising right now the only person that really got reps last year is in that room is Ponder and that wasn't really till any year. So, you're really looking at a whole new room and uh but I like the pieces that we've got in, you know, got mixture of young Draymond's done it and he's been a part of he's rushed inside, outside. He's another violent human being, physical, loves the game. And so, uh love that addition and and uh and like we said with with with Gabe, you know, and then ponder his big strides that he's making. So, I feel good about the run and and uh I think we're going to should be all right. >> With Draymond, he seemed out here every day with you working. How much do you appreciate that? You mentioned love of the game. He has to have it for the amount of work he's put in before practice to try to get better. >> Yeah, that's him. You love those guys year eight, year nine that that uh they're still willing to to learn, find something. You know, Coach Reed used to say it as came when you're done learning, you're done. And I think that's anything that we do in life. And you know, he's got such a an open mind. And you know, I tell these guys to try on new shoes. You know, try them on, see how you feel. If you like them, you don't, you don't. But he's like that. and then he works on what what he's good at and u >> he's just uh you couldn't ask for a better kid to have in the room. Shouldn't say a kid, but he's he's just that type of guy, you know, he does it the right way. You know, when you have some of these guys that's that don't put in that extra work and and there's been talking saying stuff, you know, guys have a tendency to tune them out. He he he he's a he's a real man and he takes his job. That's why he's played as long as he has and started his career inside. Now he's on the edge his last two or three years. And so it's it's it's special to have him in the room. >> But just going back to Gabe during the spring obviously when he wasn't here was say hey you're you're missing out on reping time and you guys couldn't control that situation >> but Kim on task is obviously very important. Is he eating into some of the the the two months missed and some of that time missed in the playbook and around the facility? >> Oh absolutely. I mean that's that that's such one of the biggest stages of of a young man's career. really anybody, any player that misses a whole spring and all the different things that were we're adding and changing after a season and and just working on your technique, your footwork, your hands, it's going to struggle with anybody, but for a rookie is very tough. That's, you know, that's why I'm shocked kind of where he's at and where he's progressing right now just on the defensive standpoint and learning. Uh because you're you're talking about a guy that didn't come close to do as much that we're asking him to do right now. You're adding all the dropping con stuff. See here every way we teach rush set an edge and understandingful. I mean it's it's impressive where he's at and he's got a long ways to go.
