title: Jeremy Springer: "Build Some Chemistry." | Patriots Press Conference
text: Obviously, you have some injury, or at least one big injury that you've already dealt with on special teams. How do you feel about the depth with your group? >> Man, I think, you know, with special teams, you're going to you're going to play a lot of young guys, and a lot of guys that are maybe at the bottom of the roster, but that's what's so cool about special teams. I'm just enjoying that. You know, those guys will continue to grow, and they'll figure it out at some point. They'll get better with game experience. They'll make some mistakes, but that's kind of where where they kind of grow special teams. So, I'm I'm looking forward to seeing a bunch of those young guys, and the guys that are, you know, maybe not first or second depth chart playing for me and getting grown from that standpoint. >> How big of a blow is it to have Braden out for so long? >> Anytime you have a starter that you lose to injury, it's always tough. But, in this profession, I mean, that's part of the game at the end of the day, right? So, we're looking forward to move on and and get him healthy when he gets healthy, and and next guy up, and then we'll go out and compete and see what that is. >> Do you want Do you know when that might be when Braden will come back? >> Uh no idea. >> What are your thoughts on uh Andy? Just kind of the the camp he's had and and how he's received >> Andy's done a great job, man. He's done a great job through camp. Uh he continues to progress. There's always abs and flows of being a kicker, and that's why you kick you know, you don't kick every day, but you kick a lot of days, and that's all experience part of it. You go through some adversity at times, and you got to grow from that, and hopefully it's in the preseason, hopefully it's in in practice. So, we get to the regular season, we get all the rest of that out of the way, and we can hit the ground running. >> Jeremy, is um Matt the kind of guy that you'd be okay with rolling with for a few weeks here? Is there like a feeling out process? Not that it's a tryout, but like is is there a an assessment process that you >> you love to have a veteran in, a guy who's been there, done it before, especially has gone to Seattle, and Matt's been there, done that. He's been around the league for a while. So, I'm excited to see what he can do, and and uh we're practicing today, so we're going to get him rolling, get him organized, get him with the with our kicker, and and get things going. >> Did you have any prior connection with Matt before this? >> Uh no, zero. >> Baron uh performed well enough to be uh you know, considered for some special teams duties down the line, maybe? >> what? Props to to Baron for doing that, coming in there and catching a punt, and having to go in there and execute in game, and in an actual NFL game, you know? And I'm I'm proud of the guy, and he didn't even bat an eye. So, it just speaks to the kind of kid he is. >> We've seen you guys rotate through a few different people on kickoff return. Just with the new rules and as the roster turns over, what are you looking for in that role and are there maybe there's two guys back? Is it same skill set with both guys or is it two Do you view them as two separate roles? >> Uh they're both the same same kind of role. Uh both those guys got to make good decisions. They got to be able to run through the smoke. Um they got to be fearless and uh you need depth. That's why you see a lot of guys back there because the average team went through about five or six guys last year. So, we're just trying to build depth because as the season progresses injuries do happen or guys move up the depth chart. Um that will affect us in the long run. >> Coach, when it comes to your core unit, you've obviously lost some guys in free agency, injuries kind of piling up at this point. How do you feel about that unit right now and are there any guys that have been that new additions that have kind of stepped up to something? >> Um like I said a little while ago, I just think, you know, No, no, it's fine. I just think um you know, as you go through this you're going to play a lot of the young guys. They're going to make mistakes. They're going to grow and uh that's the whole thing about special teams. Like they get better on special teams and they graduate to offense and defense. So, hey, as guys get injured, next guy in. Let's see how they progress. Throw them in the fire. Uh let them make some mistakes and let them grow from it and uh we'll be better for it. >> Do you feel like you have Uh do you feel like you have the opportunity with Mike the rest of the team here to kind of like I don't know, lobby for someone, a young guy who you think about the wide receiver depth chart got a little lighter, but it's still a deep area. You say, "No, this guy could make a real difference for my unit and maybe that's where his spot is on special teams." >> I think that's how it goes before in most teams, you know, I think guys that you think excel on special teams and they're at the bottom of the roster will get that chance and then again, once they they start showing things on my end, you know, the offensive coaches see it, the defensive coaches see it and then he progresses to graduate to be maybe a starter on the defense down the road and and that's the that's a great thing about the game. You're exactly right. Like I'm going to get some young guys that might not be doing anything on offense or defense, but they're going to play for me and excel and then become a starter. Elijah Ponder is a perfect example of that. >> Mike referenced um I think it was after the Colts game, not right after, but maybe a day or two after. He was asked about Andy and some of the misses in that game and he talked about the holder situation and the or the snapper situation, I think at the time. Now, the holder might have to change with Matt in for Bryce. Do you have to get like more reps with those three guys together or do you have to be careful with Andy not to overwork him, you know, as you're trying to get that chemistry? How do you How do you develop that chemistry that those guys need? >> You know, that's that's part of coaching, man. You just kind of figure out that the middle ground there where you have to build a little bit of chemistry, but then you also got to be able to manage the legs and and do things the right way so they're healthy going to week one and they play, you know, hopefully 24, 25 weeks of the season. So, that's our that's our job to do that and manage that, but you know, they're going to be getting the reps, build some chemistry and see where that where that leads us. >> Obviously, you can only control what you can control, but are there a certain number of veterans you'd like to have in those core units, especially with rule changes and some guys being in roles that you've never done before? >> Uh for me, it's just like No, not really. I I just like to go go with the flow of things and and which guys are progressing, which guys are ready to go and figure that part out and if it's a lot of young guys, a lot of young guys. If a lot of older guys or veterans, a lot of veterans. So, I just kind of go with the flow there. >> What have you seen from Assante Haskins? Seems like he's been in the mix in some different groups showing some physicality. >> He's a veteran that's been there, done that. You know, he's played a lot of football. So, I'm excited about him. He's physical. He's built like a linebacker, but plays running back. So, with that skill set, you can move him and place him around in different a lot of different spots. >> In that same vein, how have you seen Efrem grow in our training camp? >> Oh, it's great, man. Efrem just He comes to work every day. He's He's a pro a pro's pro and that's the reason why he continues to progress where he's at. >> You've seen him in person at the tackle. Just what do you like about his skill set at that level? >> I just think you like a guy that has some conviction back there. The guy that can run a huddle and is smart, that can that can see things and and adjust on the fly and I think he's got that and he's a He's a good blocker and receiver for us. So, you know, for as I see that, it's just good to put guys in places where their strengths are at. >> I know Jaylen too just scouted him yesterday. That what he was saying. He was pledging to be more violent on special teams. Just what do you like about his skill set on special teams? >> Safety that's violent, plays plays fast. Every Any time you see one of those, they can plug and play in a lot of different spots, especially on special teams. So, I'm excited about that. >> What have you seen from Brandon Pili and Channing Tindall when he was healthy at the Gunners policy? >> You know, those those guys continue to progress. You know, Channing's been out for a little bit with an injury, but you know, KP's done a great job. Channing's taking all the coaching from TQ, and those guys continue to progress. I mean, it's all those they got to get in the game situations. They got to progress through there, and they got to lose some, they got to win some. And when they do that, it helps them get better and learn from those mistakes, just like Slater did when he was young, just like Slater did when he was young. But, I'm excited to see their development. >> What is it like not having Brandon out there, and do you think that that's something that could bleed into the regular season? >> You know, for me it's you don't ever you can't replace like an All-Pro type of guy. So, it's always a a loss for me that leadership on the field, but he's always around. He's around helping us out. And when we get him back, we get him back. But, until then, you know, he as long as he continues to progress and help our young guys out, that's what I'm looking for. >> It seems like at times on kick return, the middle of the field was a little more congested with four bodies. Can you give some insight into that and how that's different from maybe more standard looks? >> Well, because a lot of your games are going to happen inside. So, you're going to put a lot of different pieces inside so that you can adjust with different levels and different body types because majority of teams are going to in the preseason are going to probably double one guy, maybe an interior guy to kind of spread open the field. And that's just kind of a standard thing most teams do in the preseason. As team as the season progresses, then you might see different formations, but with the way the formation reads, it's a lot easier to get guys in the middle to to double guys inside to create holes inside to create bigger spaces to mention. >> Yeah. I appreciate it.

title: Zak Kuhr: "We Strive to Have Great Energy." | Patriots Press Conference
text: I know there's always a long laundry list of things you want to address at this time of year, but where do you feel how do you feel about the state of the run defense at this point? >> Yeah, I think it's improving every day. Uh the more looks we get, the better we're off we are. And we're just continuing to work on the fundamentals of that, the technique and the run game and just the chemistry of the second level feeding off the first level, the third level feeding off the second level. >> Z, you got a new safety yesterday. just what do you like about Jaylen and his skill set? >> Uh it's still to be seen. You know, Brandon just got here, see what his uh his skill set is and work with him. Uh I know he's come here ready to work. >> Zack, what have you observed from from Gabe thus far? Obviously, only been here for about a month now. >> Yeah, he's continuing to work on the fundamentals. He's got to really focus on the technique and the fundamentals from ground one, but he's willing. He's a great great kid. He works his ass off. He's physical. He's violent. So he's fun to coach. He's fun to be around. And he's just got to keep working on on, you know, from one to two to three to four. >> If he gets a one to two to three to four where you see the more consistency in the violence in the >> Yeah, absolutely. Yeah. I mean, I would say the violence, especially on practice, is consistent. It's just now the technique with it. Sometimes when you try to be, you know, violent and you let the the fundamentals of technique get out of hand, now you're in a in a bad position, not able to make a play. Do you guys have an idea on how long you'll be without Harold and how difficult is it to sort of replace that type of veteran leadership reduction? >> Yeah, I don't I don't know the timelines or anything like that, but I would say Harold still provides that veteran leadership in the meetings. You know, he's very active in the meetings. He's a great teammate. He's professional values handling his his workload right now. And I I still think he gives pointers and tips those guys in that room. So, he's still the presence there. How integral is Christian Gonzalez to this defense? >> Yeah, I think everybody is. Christian is I think the other 10 guys are on the field are and uh you know, everybody has an important role. We can't just go out there with just one person and expect to play good defense. It's we saw a couple examples the other day in the red zone. You know, one guy didn't see the same thing the same as another and we gave up a touchdown. Uh it can't just be on one person. I think everybody has an important role within the defense. You mentioned I think back in mini camp like more communication trying some different things in mini camp in the red area. How do you feel like that's come along? >> I think it's improved. It really has. I told the guys this morning seeing the improvement from red zone day one to red zone day two to red zone day three to four. The continual improvement as we you know lead up to week one. It has been some uh some good things down the road. >> Zach, you guys haven't been shy about bringing in pressure in the preseason. What are the benefits to that as opposed to just rushing forward to see what guys can do? I I would say we've done a mix of that. Uh you know, it's it's part of kind of what you just said. What can guys do? Who can pressure? Uh how do guys do on movements? How do guys in the first level win on a movement on the O line? How guys in the second level feel off the guys in the first level doing the movement? How do they feel the stunts? How well do they handle that? and the guy pressuring himself and then putting also the secondary uh in the dis, you know, uh, how do I say this? Not the best spot, right? And, you know, a little more under stress and coverage. How do they handle that? >> I know he hasn't been out here the last couple days, but what excites you about Craig Woodson going into year two? >> Uh, a lot. The experience, you know, obviously he made some plays last year, has continued developed, uh, especially as a vocal leader out there. I think KB in there has helped him and just seeing where he will transition uh you know to to year two. I think there's a lot of room for him to still to develop and grow. He's got high ceiling and excited to see where he goes with that. >> Being back with Tennessee, there's an emphasis on turnovers. Is that a coincidence or is that the direct effect of Kevin Bard being on? >> No, no, I don't think that's KB being here. I think last year every single day we talk about takeaways every day. This year we talk about takeaways and we emphasize it. Sometimes we get a lot. Sometimes we don't get as many. So it's just kind of how the game goes. >> Zach, Kevin's mentioned a few times that this is actually a different system than he was in in Tennessee, which I thought was interesting with all you guys being similar coaches. And without giving away too much, like it would you agree with that? Like do you think or maybe it's evolved? I don't know. >> I I would agree with that. It has evolved. uh you know there's some still some core principles but as you go through the years and the same calls especially with the same people you start to see all the holes in it and then you start to adjust those and next thing you know it's transitioning to a whole new defense. Uh but yeah I would say it's somewhat different for sure. >> Have you seen him just step back into it even though it's it's a little bit different? >> Yeah, he's he's doing just fine. He's he's a professional. He's one of the few guys that sometimes when you want to take the work load off that veteran player, he wants the reps. He wants to keep working in it. Uh, and like I say, he's just a true professional and he's he's doing just fine. >> Ellis made a point yesterday to speak about Gonzo's energy and having him back on the field. What does that energy look like to you? >> Yeah, I think anytime a good player's out there and he's competitive and making plays, it feeds off into another player, whether it be Gonzo or Christian himself. Uh, I'd say every day we strive to have great energy within all 11 guys. >> How much of a sounding board still is Jerrell Williams to you? And how integral is he still with everything that you do? >> Yeah, he's a big sounding board for me. He's a mentor to me. That was my first year in the NFL. I worked with him and I always bounce ideas off of him. He's still a huge part of the defense. Uh, he's a great sounding board for the front guys as well with Clint Smitty. Um he he's a huge part of this staff and with his leadership and with his knowledge of defensive football and front play. >> You guys were uh in the playoffs last year the blitz rate went up like over 40% some places.
