We have to generate our own energy, especially when we're on the road cuz like in a situation like this, if it's a game, it's going to be a hostile environment. So, we got to be able to like pull like pull our hands out of our asses sometimes and and and get back on track. >> Obviously, 10 years >> when you're not in games very much, I think, >> how do you how are you able to prepare? How different is it now from? Yeah, I mean it's definitely different um because you have to like use the practices to really like prepare your mind and your body uh for the games. I mean luckily just having the experience that I've had like you kind of know what to expect in the games and kind of know like when you feel game ready. Um but you just have to be like really really intentional about the work that you get in practice. Um the coaches do a good job of like structuring things that way as well so you're constantly building up for that. But um sure like the games help but the preseason is a much different speed than a regular season anyway. So, it's like you get a little bit of a look, but it's not like like if you go into the regular season expecting it to be the speed of the preseason, you don't get your head hit crack. >> Chris, obviously, what have you thought about the back quarterback position? >> Um, I think we got some really good guys back there. Um, obviously like Jake's been around for a while. Um, he's been doing his thing and you know, he has a ton of experience and then Jaylen is here and like you guys saw what Jaylen can do uh last week, right? It's a young exciting player. Um, has a strong arm but like has a lot to learn, right? So, I think that we have some some potential in with with both of those guys. And I mean, just we'll see how it plays out. >> Mhm. >> Do you feel good about where that group can be healthwise for? >> Yeah, I do. Um, it's like guys are training in the right direction, right? And, you know, we we have we have a good athletic staff that will get these guys prepared. Um, but again, it's like it's hard to predict super far out, right? But regardless, I feel like we have a a room that I'm confident in. Um guys that can go out and make plays. Um as you as you saw today, Ted's making plays. Uh Ted's making plays. Like we got we got guys that can really go. >> Coach, was saying that the game is slowing down for him, which is allowing him to play full speed. >> Yeah. When did you start realizing when the game slowed down how quickly you were able to pick things up just >> um I mean honestly I think it was like probably like midway through my rookie year. Um I was in a different position than Ted was or than Ted is rather like I had like obviously Mike Hump and and DJ confronted me so I was like the next guy rotating in. Um and they all were healthy going into the year. So during training camp, I was getting a lot of like reps rotating, but I didn't really get a ton of like game time until like middle of the year. So it took me a little bit of time to kind of get adjusted. Played a lot of special teams and so Ted's in a different spot. But I think he's been doing a great job. Like he's very receptive to coaching. Uh he wants to be he wants to be a great player. So I think he like the sky's is the limit as you like he he has some unbelievable potential to make some really really good plays. Like he's so explosive especially for that size. He has the ability to jump, make tough catches. like he's doing some really good things. >> Thank you. >> Sweet. Appreciate it, guys. Y'all be safe. >> My bad. >> How's it getting back? How you feeling? >> Uh, it feels good just to be out there with my brothers. Um, it always sucks when you're not out there with them. So, um, just being back at joint practice today, I got to get my feet back up on me, but it it just feels good just having my teammates with me and encouraging me to be back and, um, excited for me to be back. So, it's it feels great. >> What do you think of the offense performance today? >> Uh, we got some stuff to clean up, but I mean, uh, not not every day is going to be a perfect day. We've seen ups and downs in football. Um, one day you look great, one day you look bad. So, I mean, today we just got to go out there and, uh, go go back to the hotel and watch film and, um, fix our mistakes. Um, all our quarterbacks great. I mean, um, no matter who's in there, we trust them. They trust us. So, um, whoever's in after Baker is legit. So, I mean, every last one of our quarterbacks from, uh, Connor Baslick and JD to Jake, all those guys look great. How important is it for you? Does that mean something to you? >> Uh, 100%. Um, you always want to play in a game, get banged around a little bit before you go into week one. You don't want week one to be Cincinnati and stuff like that. So, it's it's definitely something I'm looking forward to. So, yeah. >> How nice was it to see Tristan back out there? >> Oh my god, it looks great. Um, Tristan, he's a big piece to our offense. Um, he he looks great as always. Uh just glad to have him back and him getting his feet up underneath him too. Um like I said, it always sucks being out for any player, but um having Tristan back is it feels very great. >> I know you're not the biggest guy in the world. >> I stood by him the other day and I like I didn't know like really who I was standing next to until I like looked to my like left and I just kept looking up and I'm like What did you think of the two guys? >> Um, like I said, it's always some improvement for both teams. Um, I think we has show some good, some bad, but those are things we got to work on. This game is not perfect, so we got to go out there and u execute a little bit more better, a little better, and then um just do a repeat tomorrow. >> T, what did you make of Ted H out there stretching the field, making a couple plays? Uh he's Ted's doing what he do best. Like that's what we drafted him for. I mean he looks great. Even though he's a rookie, he's getting the hang of it pretty quick. Um Ted is a like I said a big piece of offense, too. And he looks great. He's like he's getting confident now. Um it was a little bit shaky and I pretty much that's what every rookie that comes in and but now he's getting the hang of it and knowing coverages, knowing DBs, leverage and making this opportunity count. a little bit of emotion. How do you feel like that's going to play? >> Um, I mean, this game is emotional. Um, you see, like I said, you see ups and downs all day. Um, but you got to be able to control that emotion to go out there and execute the game plan. Um, you want to execute more than play with emotion. I mean, this game, you play this game only really two ways. It's fast and violent. Um, once your feelings start getting into it, that's when you decrease. So, I mean, you just got to keep improving and uh doing the fundamentals the correct way. Anything else? >> Thanks.

title: Todd Bowles Discusses Joint Practice vs. Jags | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Afternoon, morning. I thought that we got some good work right out there. I thought we played more with the emotion than we did fundamentals. So, we got to clean that up cuz those guys haven't played in a while, but I thought it was very good work. >> Coach, what did you think of the team from an energy standpoint with they brought out here today? >> Tons of energy, like I said, tons of energy, but we got to work on the technical stuff. You've got to kind of take emotion out of it sometimes when you're not doing it fundamentally right. We had some good plays, we had some plays that we can coach better and they can play better. >> You got to see Tristan and a little bit of Blake More saying. What did you think of those guys today? >> I'll look at the tape. I didn't watch them all individually, but you know, they came off healthy, so I'll see what the tape says. >> I know you got to answer the other day, but Paul Rudzitis had a snap in the offensive side of the ball in the game the other day. What did you see after seeing him on film and where is he good and where can he improve? >> It was his first start, obviously there's some things he can improve on fundamentally and technically, but he fought and he battled his tail off in there. >> Is there any way to gauge these practices versus the similar offense and defense maybe you can see a little bit? >> No, it doesn't. I mean, both of them have their little tweaks in the system. They're not directly the same, so you still got to play and you got to play even Reggie Keith. No, they will coach and they come off the ball. >> Uh we saw Adrian Barnes of the PVU in that last little bit of college. What has been the biggest growth for Barnes so far since he arrived? >> Just understanding the defensive system. We knew he was talented, but he he's kind of calmed down instead of making plays exchanging one for one. He's playing the right way and he's doing little things right and it's the stuff he does when the ball doesn't come his way that's been impressing us. >> What do you hope to you think you can away from these last two joint practices for the rest of the season? >> Uh just to get good work in, you know, we got to get ready for the season after this. So, it's going to be important for the other guys, the younger guys, to step up and make plays. There's cuts coming up. There's going to be some close calls, and the other guys, you know, they got to get ready for the season. They got to get used to playing 50, 60 something plays as opposed to six to eight plays per snap. >> You obviously saw him up close two years ago, but what is it about Liam this just offensive scheme and his coaching that makes their offense so dynamic? >> Him and Zach are very similar. Uh very smart. He knows how to run the ball, understands how to run the ball. It's not necessarily about my guy's better than yours, but it's about scheme and getting the edge and getting the extra blocker or the extra half a man so they can get their guy through, and he does a good job that way. >> We saw Zach Triner make a couple of plays today. What does he do correctly that puts himself in the right position to get the ball? >> He's an instinctive football player. He's very smart. He's just not strong. He's savvy. He knows how to slip blocks when it's time to slip blocks, and you can't teach that. Uh right now I'm leaning towards not playing him, but we'll see how tomorrow goes. >> How did it look to see Zach Triner against play in the preseason game and not participate today? Any kind of update if he's dealing with anything? >> Uh it's his groin. We've been dealing with a groin. >> What was it to see Christian out there for the first time in team drills up against uh >> It's good to see him fresh, obviously making progress. So, we just got to keep making strides. >> You saw Chip Kelly practicing as well. Would he be available Friday or just have a limited practice? >> Too early to tell right now. We'll see how he came through this one. >> Chase Claypool had a little bit. What did you think of Chase today? He really showed up a few times. >> He showed his speed, obviously. I didn't watch the offensive side of the ball. I got to see the tape on that. All I saw was the two-minute, but he flashed out there. He flashed in practice. I'll look at the tape and see. >> Coach, what did you make of Alex Highsmith when he got into it with one of the Jaguars' offensive >> Well, he wasn't the only one. I mean, you know, there's pushing give and take on both sides. Obviously, we started some, they started some, but it didn't get out of hand. He's one of our bell cows on defense. He's an emotional guy, but we got to learn how to play with emotion and keep it the right way. >> You saw Campbell going up one on one sometimes with Travis Hunter and having success. Where has his growth come the most where have you seen his his growth come in >> His growth has come in understanding the offense. That allows him to play faster. He's not thinking as much, so he's not playing half speed. He's playing full speed. He understands where to go and where to be and that allows him to play a lot faster. >> You said you guys were playing with emotion today. Where where do you think that that that came from? >> That comes when you get off the bus. Obviously, when you practice against somebody else, you try to show. They play with emotion, we play with emotion. We just got to play the right way. >> Okay. Thank you. >> Yeah.

title: Bucs Travel Upstate for Joint-Practice in Jacksonville | Training Camp Report | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Welcome into another edition of Training Camp Report presented by Advent Health coming to you this morning from Jacksonville. Casey Phillips here with our playbyplay announcer Tony Castraone as the Buccaneers are about to do joint practices with the Jaguars. Of course, we had one a couple weeks ago with the Jets. Now we have it again with the Jaguars. And of course, coaches talked about how important these practices are getting a lot of guys work. Uh before we get into talking about the practice today, wanted to talk a bit about that last preseason game and just some of the the takeaways we saw of who was really that game important for, who came out shining, what was uh some of the the major things you saw while calling that game. >> Well, I I think you know, everybody says you can't really take too much into consideration about results in preseason because of all the obvious reasons, but you still would rather win the games. And for uh the Buccaneers to come from behind in the second half two weeks in a row now and actually get the job done I thought was incredibly encouraging. And the guy that led the charge is Jaylen Daniels. And uh you know obviously he's competing for a spot. He's trying to make that 53man roster. But you have to be really impressed with what the young undrafted quarterback out of Kansas has done so far through his two preseason games. I think um you know I was reading a CBS sports column talking about every rookie quarterback giving uh all over the NFL giving them grades A through F. There are only five A's in the NFL through preseason camp so far. And Jaylen Daniels got one of them. And when you consider eight drives, four touchdowns, one field goal, two come from behind wins, and no turnovers. He's really done everything that's been asked of him so far. So that's the guy that has really stood out to me so far. Obviously, um it was good to see some of the starters get out there. I think it's been kind of interesting at the running back position. They are treating Kenny Gainwell just like Bucky Irving. He's got very similar reps. So, they really truly are looking at him as a 1B. Um, you know, I think uh it it's been interesting to see on the defensive side of the ball how guys are kind of coming in and out and getting different reps. Um, you know, the the linebacker position, particularly on the outside, I thought the edges were able to get after the quarterback. That was a really positive sign. Um, we're still seeing David Walker show up in in ways that have been interesting. So, uh, I'm really encouraged by the whole team's progress, but Jaylen Daniels to me stole the show. >> And, and because of that, you know, a lot of people have been wondering, hey, what is this quarterback battle looking like? And, and preseason's always interesting because whether it be training camp or the preseason games, it's very easy to take, you know, a few moments or a few things and extrapolate out of, oh my gosh, this, you know, what does this mean? But it's hard to tell sometimes, especially when guys are not going against the ones always or whatever. So, what would you say from what you've seen, what you've heard about what this could mean for the backup quarterback position? And, you know, two, three, how many are you keeping? Like, it's just a very interesting debate now that Jaylen Daniels is forcing them to have. So, what would you say that this has uh told you about that position? >> Well, I I think it's told me kind of what you just set up is that I'm really excited to see which direction they decide to go. Are they going to keep two? Are they going to put three on the final roster? because Jaylen Daniels has made a name for himself, but they've got a good backup in Jake Browning, who, you know, he played pretty well. He went nine to 12, uh, 84 yards, and this is a guy with a lot of experience. Uh, I I've known Jake a long time just from covering him at the University of Washington. This was the most prolific passer in the history of California high school football with 229 touchdown passes in four years. That's an outrageous amount. Then goes to University of Washington. sets an NCA record for most starts at quarterback with 53, winningest quarterback in the history of the Pack 12 Conference. Those are some pretty good resumes that he brings into his NFL career where he was on the pack practice squad with the Vikings for a long time, then goes to Cincinnati. 17 games, 10 starts. He did have those interception problems last year, but the whole team did as well. And when you look at what the idea of having a veteran quarterback like Jake Browning behind this offensive line, which right now is rated as a top three in the in the NFL with this slew of receivers, these kind of weapons at running back. Jake Browning in that scenario could be really really good. He's a very smart guy, a very heady quarterback, and a guy that just has experience that you can't replace. So, you know, yes, Jaylen Daniels has flashed on TV. He has really put it on tape the last couple of weeks, but you can't count Jake Browning out yet either. And that's why I think it's really interesting. Is it a battle for QB2 or are they really starting to consider putting three guys on the 53man roster? That's what I think we'll learn a little bit about this week. >> Yeah, I'm glad you brought up the offensive line part because we know that ended up being a major factor in that preseason game because you were on like your 14th tackle. It was just crazy. It felt I was like, wait, how are we doing this again? This was our story line last season. I would like to not be talking about it even in the preseason. But um you you did have a a change in of course what they were going to do with Baker with some of the guys you know that you were probably going to run the ball a little bit more. You weren't going to risk a lot of things knowing that you had several people injured. So now looking at today's practice, who's in, who's out? What do we know? Of course, they don't have to put out a real injury report. They don't have to tell us any of that kind of stuff. So what can we tell about some of the updates of of guys that maybe were out in that game that are coming back, working their way back and and who might be able to get some work in at this practice? >> So no Justin school today. He's not in pads, but good news is Tristan Worfs is out there in pads. And also Ben Chuck Wuma is back. And so I think, you know, who knows how much we'll actually see them today, but the fact that they're suited up, the fact that they're practicing, I think is a really good sign. You know, I think last year the offensive line stealing the show as a storyline. Uh the the ones not taking a single rep together in regular season play all year. You don't want to have that be the issue again. And so, um, that is definitely something that we're going to be keeping an eye on today. Vita Vea is in pads. I think that's something that again, you don't expect him to go out there and take every single rep, but you do want to see what he's able to do. And I think that's a really positive sign for what could be looming week one, a few weeks from now on the road against Cincinnati. But again, I think um at at this point in a practice like today, the best ability is availability. And I think that's just really what I'm watching every single practice. who's in, who's out, why is it a pitch count thing? Is it an injury? Uh does the injury look like something that's going to be long-term, medium-term, short-term? And just this is the last week to gauge all that stuff. So, that's what I'm really paying attention to today. And um the offensive line is is certainly going to be one of those areas of focus. >> Yeah. Outside of that, uh what are some of the things that you feel like you want to keep an eye on knowing it's again a joint practice as compared to being by ourselves at our own facility? Certain individuals, certain other position groups that you feel like as you walk around here, you're going to be keeping an eye on. >> Yeah. secondary has been a little bit banged up through camp and so you know just kind of curious to see are we getting some pieces back there. Uh Benjamin Morrison was a guy that was able to talk to the media and and is in pads today. So how much is he able to go and contribute? I just felt like in that uh in the joint practices against the Jets uh the the the pass rush looked good but I thought it looked better against Kansas City under the lights in the preseason. And so, you know, with that being an important part of what they wanted to do in the offseason, beefing up that part of the game, uh, I'm excited to kind of just keep an eye on that, not just off the edges, but the different ways they want to try to mix things up and and apply pressure and then, you know, just getting that rush from the inside as well. >> And then we'll close with this. I know that for you this was your first time getting to actually call a Bucks game in Raymond James Stadium. And then you were visited by a very special guest that Gene Deckerhoff came back to wish you luck your first time at at home, which I thought was very cool. What was that like for you getting to have him there, talk to him beforehand, and then just being in the actual stadium that's the home stadium for the first time, calling a game? >> Yeah, it was it was awesome. And I got to say, the crew showed up and I thought the crowd was really, really good. I mean, we were in a very sleepy Metife stadium for week one and then to come home for week two and to see how, you know, there were seats all the way up to the very top row row that were full. That lower bowl was was cranking. The energy was high. It was awesome. I thought it was a really great home crowd experience uh particularly for the preseason. But but Gan, man, I mean to see him was awesome. He may have retired from calling the games. He has not retired his passion and love for the Bucks. He made the trip and he uh he he was just you know how he is like he lights up the room when he walks in. And so to have his support to have him come and talk to me as much as he did, it was awesome and humbling and and he's just so awesome. It it was really great to see him. >> I love it. All right. All right. Well, that's going to do it for us from this first joint practice here in Jacksonville. We'll be back tomorrow morning to cover what happens in this one and preview not only tomorrow's practice, but the game as well. So, we'll see you then.

title: Baker Mayfield on Importance of Execution | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Jacksonville was pretty physical. >> Um, it's tough. Uh, I thought, you know, they gave us some good looks. They were playing with their hair on fire, I'll say that. Um, we definitely, if this was a full game, I don't think we would have came out on the the winning side of it. Um, so just little eye opening. Got to get back and watch the tape. you know, it's never as good or as bad as you think it is, but um I think from from my standpoint, it they out physical us, and that's that's never what you want to have. So, um didn't doesn't matter who we have out there, you want guys that are going to do their very best to be the more physical team and want it more. And I don't I don't know if we did that today. So, uh the tape will tell, but yeah, two-minute work was decent. Obviously, Lightning kind of cut it short. Um but yeah, at that point in practice, guys, we got to get in game shape. Guys were kind of huffing and puffing a little bit. It's it's hot. I get it. Uh but yeah, we needed it. >> You got to see some stuff back. >> Yeah. Uh really good. You know, obviously just slowly working him back in there. Uh not trying to overdo it, you know, most important thing. Need him for the regular season, but um yeah, definitely definitely great to have him in there. Just you can tell the whole line when he's in there, there's a relaxing um style, just the the comfort that it is when he's in there. just they have so many reps together, communication, obviously the caliber player he is, but um yeah, it's great to have him back. >> What did you do with Liam together? Why did you guys play so >> um Liam's a players coach, you know, somebody that um you know, he has a system. Yes, he has his bread and butter that he wants to get done, but he always adapts to the players and personnel that he has. And so I think just his communication style when it comes down to that as well. Um yeah, Liam Liam's a close friend of mine and happy for him. He's a hell of a coach. >> Tristan coming back. That's good. But what do you know from Paul Rubel? Obviously a big body. What's it like behind a guy? >> Yeah, I mean he is a giant wall. Uh that's for sure. I definitely can't see over him. Um can't see over any of them, but definitely not Paul. Uh you know, he's been thrown in the fire for us. You know, obviously uh Ben Chukes, he got hurt as well. Skoolie had a little uh little injury as well. So Paul getting a lot of reps. So uh it's been it's been good for him. a lot of learning experiences, but um yeah, to to be able to have depth this early in camp at tackle is good. So, just hoping they continue and improve, but I'm I'm proud of Paul. With that many guys out in five, seven drop. >> Yeah, I mean, when you have edge rushers like they do, um you're not trying to hold on to it too long. uh trying to make it easier on your guys up front, especially when they're pretty exhausted in practice, trying to get the ball out of your hands and and let your playmakers do the work. >> What do you thought about the guys behind you in the quarterback room as they battle it out to see who's going to be second? >> Yeah. Um to be honest with you, I mean, having having Baze, Connor Basilac here last year, I think he's grown tremendously. Obviously, he's not getting a ton of reps, but he's a really really sharp kid. I think when he gets his chances, he takes advantage of them. Um Jake's had a hell of an offseason in camp so far. And then obviously you guys have seen Jaylen u make a lot of splash plays and uh so for him just the the growing aspect of the quarterback game. You know this system is u it's pretty tough to get down a lot of verbiage. So he's made tremendous strides in that. I'm proud of him in that regard and um yeah it's just exciting to see those guys duke it out. But um yeah it's quarterback room is important to all support each other. >> Brownie for taking >> Yeah, he was uh just getting hit from all sides a little bit. Uh but yeah, he's he's tough tough cookie. Um you know, our personalities are a little bit different, but he just he takes the hits and just gets back up and like nothing happened. So on with the next one. And um you know, it's it's different. It's a different style, but I respect the hell out of it. >> Understand this. How do you feel about >> um I feel like we're in a good spot with the understanding of the system, the checks, what we're trying to get done. Now it's just strictly about execution, physicality, and I think that's that's the part today that we were lacking. Um I I don't think that anybody's too far behind when it comes to the knowledge of what we're trying to get done. Uh which is which is great. That's what you want this point of camp, but also when you have that down, you need to the execution needs to be there. So, um yeah, like I said earlier, going to go back and watch the tape, but there's a lot of plays that we'll probably want back today. >> Bigger, we've heard uh you talk about his growth. Todd said that it seems like is slowing down for him which allows him to play faster. Have you just seen it from your perspective? How much has he grown just in the last couple of weeks? >> Yeah. Uh a lot. And you know, when you're able to as a rookie with his talent, his body, god-given ability that when you're able to not think as much and just go play and use that ability, good things happen. So, you can see it clicking just the the motions, everything that we're trying to get done. When he has a one-on-one matchup, he knows the ball's probably coming his way. And so, um yeah, he's making a lot of plays. It's just like I said earlier about a lot of the guys need to get their game legs ready. Um so he was he was hurting a little bit today. A lot of routes, a lot of reps that were down on receivers, but u those guys understand that. >> How do you think Bucky played in the preseason opener and then during practice? I >> think Bucky looks really good. Uh he put on a lot of muscle uh but still shifty as ever. And so u proud of Bucky and just that surgery sucks. I've gone through it. It's it's a pain. a lot of the same things routine every single day that you're itching to just get out there and and do what you want but not able to. And so he's done a great job rehabbing and coming back from that. And then I think he's he's looking really good right now. I I think his tracks when it comes to the run game, protection wise, I think his knowledge of what we're trying to get done in the pass game has come a long way. So he's he's taken another big step that we were looking for him to do. >> Thank you. >> Thanks, guys.

title: Rashid Shaheed: "We Grew A Lot Over The Last Week" | Seattle Seahawks
text: Wow. What's going on everybody? Going on sir. >> How's it uh what's the process like getting ready for a season when a bunch of you guys aren't playing in the preseason games? Like how's that changed what you need to get out of practice? >> Yeah. Uh just like you said, practice needs to be, you know, kind of the focal point. Um each and every rep, you know, you got to try to make it into a game rep and mentally. Um, yeah, just coming out and competing. And I feel like our coaches do a good job of setting up practice so you know, we get that working. >> Kind of a shot uh to the midsection like what was that like? >> Uh, just knocked the wind out of me. Um, you know, those situations they uh they come, you know, it's football, but um, you know, just happened in the joint practice and I was able to shake it off and um, you know, kind of just, you know, just move on to the next play. But uh, yeah, it definitely didn't feel good. Were you surprised he hit you? Is that outside the bounds of what you thought the scrimmage? >> Uh yeah, a little bit. Um wasn't really expecting it. Um that was also my former teammate, so I definitely wasn't expecting it from him, but it's all good. We talked about it afterwards and you know, it's all love, but yeah, it's a part of part of the game. >> You had a catch a few plays later that that you feel good. >> Uh yeah, definitely. Um just letting a little bit of steam out, you know. Um that's all it was. What did the joint practice allow you guys to do with Flor's [clears throat] offense? Because he talked about when you see the same defense every day. In some ways, you get limited to what you get can work on. >> Yeah. Uh we like the way that, you know, we kind of control the offense. Um we kind of went out and with the mindset of, you know, um just competing and I feel like he kind of let us go out there and just play our game. Um we got a feel of his play calling, you know, on on team drives, long drives, um and two-minute. Um, yeah, we feel like we got a a good feel of how he likes to call games and gets a feel for how the offense is flowing. >> What did you notice on that field? What was what did you notice about the feel of his play call? >> Yeah, uh, we liked his aggressiveness. We feel like we were taking a lot of shots downfield. Um, you know, his play calls were, you know, on time and on target and I feel like they were all, you know, executed in the right way and we just got to continue to do that um, for the next couple weeks leading up to game one. How similar does it feel uh from last year and what's different about it? >> Uh like around this time? >> No, no, no. I'm sorry. The offense specifically. >> Oh, yeah. Um the offense I feel like we've we have a good idea of, you know, how we want to operate and so does Flurry and I feel like he kind of came in and um we've been able to kind of just feed off that um our energy from last year. Um the offense is pretty similar. you know, there's some some nuances, but um I feel like we, you know, just came in and had the right mindset and, you know, continue to grow with, you know, all of us together with within the offense and um yeah, it's been good so far. >> And what are you learning about him either as a coach or a person? >> Uh yeah, like I just said, he he wants to move the ball down the field. He's he's aggressive. He wants um to run the ball. He wants us to be physical in in all aspects of the game. And uh with that mentality, you know, we just have to go out there and do it. Um I feel like we've done that up to this point. and uh we just got to continue to grow along with him. >> I know you didn't play on Sunday, but one of the things Mike McDonald wanted the team to work on was mechanics and in and out of the huddle and just some of those things. What did you see in terms of improvements there or where they're still going for? >> Yeah. Uh always room for improvement, but I feel like we grew a lot over the last week um from the first preseason game to the second. Um I feel like we honed in on those details throughout the week and uh we were able to go out there and execute them. Uh the young guys, they did a great job. Um it just put a lot of good on uh film uh out there and um yeah, I'm looking forward to the third game. >> What does this team lose without Jake? I mean, fans will look and see two catches last year. Obviously, the NFC Championship game was a big one, but like his impact seems to go quite a bit beyond that. Like what's his loss going to be like for you guys in that room? >> Yeah, know it's a huge loss. He's he's a heartbeat of the offense. Um, you know, we look to him for a lot of big plays and, um, you know, he's been that, you know, since he's been a part of this organization and, um, losing him, it definitely hurts. Um, we're just at this point, we're just trying to keep his head high. Um, it's a tough situation, but we know he's going to bounce back from it. >> As a wide receiver room, how do you guys feel about your depth because obviously you, Jax, Cooper, you guys are pretty established in the league. How do you feel about the depth field on the three of you guys, especially with Jake going out with injury? >> Yeah, uh, unfortunately with Jake going out, it definitely puts a little dent in it, but, um, we have guys that are going to step up. Um, I love our depth. Um, we have a lot of guys that can make a lot of plays, tons of talent, and uh, you know, we're all looking forward to all the opportunities we're going to get throughout the season. And, [snorts] um, yeah, we're a locked in group and, uh, we kind of feed, the offense kind of feeds off of our energy, and, you know, that's exactly how we want it. >> When you play impressions about Monty Foster, >> uh, everything, uh, his mindset, how he attacks every day. Um, he works super super hard and I'm just glad that it's finally coming, uh, out and for every for everybody to see. Um but yeah, no, I I try to stay in his ear, try to keep him locked in, you know, um he understands what it takes and uh I just got to continue to remind him that, you know, he's he's here and he has opportunity to do something special. >> What impression did you get from him last year when he comes in and joins you guys in December on the practice squad? Kind of runs out the string with you, but what what did you kind of get a sense from then and seeing how he's kind of taking advantage of the opportunity now? >> Yeah. Um he came in with the same mindset, you know, obviously it was later later on in the season. Um but you saw him make those type of plays at practices. um you knew that you saw his potential and um now he had a long off seasonason and you know with us and uh he was able to you know just keep his head down and work and like I said the work is showing and um he just has to continue to make plays and I think he's going to continue to do so. >> Rasheed when you were in New Orleans you had Alvin in the back field one of the top passcatching backs in the league. How does having a running back room that's heavily involved in the passing game open things up for you guys on the outside? Seems like that's been an emphasis with Brian Flurry this offense. >> Yeah, for sure. Um it opens up everything. You know, you always have um something else to key on. You know, with us going vertical, you have a running back that could you know, you could um dink and dunk to down the field and know as long as the coverage is is um you know, back, he could kind of work and um you know, just kind of do that for the offense and uh I think it's going to be a big part of, you know, what he wants to do and how we're going to move the ball down the field. You had the long catch uh from Sam in the championship game, but there's a few other deep ones that just you guys were like a hair off. Is that the kind of thing that gets easier when you have more time with your quarterback? >> Yeah, 100%. I feel like we've worked on it a ton throughout this offseason otaas and now through camp and we're starting to hit on them more. I'm starting to practice them a lot more and uh let things like that just take time and you know those little um uh this game a game of inches like we always hear and um now we're starting to kind of click and uh it's been good. >> Thank you.

title: Byron Murphy II: "We Have Everything We Need In Order To Be Successful" | Seattle Seahawks
text: with the trip. What's up? >> What's up? What's up? >> How you doing? I'm >> doing good. How you doing? >> What's going on with Chris? Can we go? What's going on with camp? >> Camp, man, uh, this is going pretty well. I feel like, uh, I'm in a great spot right now. You know, we finishing up camp. Uh, so I just got to take, you know, every advantage that I got, you know, every opportunity of camp left. So, just, you know, working on stacking days and getting better. >> Now, we've talked about it, Leonard Williams, and just that room. How important is for you guys? Can you talk about that room? >> Say it again. >> Your Dline room. Can you talk about about it? Just >> uh man, it's uh it's a lot of talent in there. A lot of dogs. Uh you know, a lot of a lot of versatile players that can do a lot of things, you know, far as pass rushing, stopping a run. Like I feel like we got everything uh in our D line. We got everything that we need, you know, in order to be successful. So, yeah. >> What is there left to do this week with one preseason game and a few more practices before the regular season? really just just sharpening up, sharpening up my tools. Um just, you know, uh just getting prepared, getting my body ready, uh my mental as well, and uh just getting ready for we going. >> Byron, for those of you guys that aren't playing in the preseason, what do you have to do to get ready? Like, does it feel like college again, like where you're going out in game one where you don't have somebody else you played in the leadup to it? Kind of how do you manage that? What's different about it trying to to get ready? Uh I say really just uh like we know we not playing but attacking it attacking the like the game day like we are playing you know. Uh also too just taking uh real mental reps um you know mental reps you know watching film just things like that like you just getting prepared for a game. So really just uh really just being a pro for real. >> Coach told us he expects more pass productivity in the pass rush from you this year. What does that mean to you? What what does that look like? Uh just me rushing. That's what it's going to look like. Just me rushing uh getting to the quarterback, but also too just uh working with the guys around me to get to the quarterback. >> Is that more opportunities up and down the line? What have you noticed already maybe pitching? >> Uh I'm getting I'm getting opportunities playing at, you know, rushing from the three, you know, uh a couple lower rushes here and there. Also too, rushing from the no. So really just, you know, being all around and uh taking, you know, uh every opportunity they give me. We're still just getting started, but you saw what Jaylen Carter got. You have to notice the defensive tackle marker. What do you think of that and where your goals are? >> Wow. Chill out there. [laughter] >> Uh, it's pretty cool, you know, to see. But, uh, I'm not really worried about that right now. I'm just, you know, focusing focusing what's, you know, what focusing on me, focusing on what's uh, you know, what's happening right now as training camp and just going into the season. You guys have a lot of you you got a lot of, you know, tenure plus vets in defensive line, outside linebackers for still relatively young player and coming up the last couple years. What have those guys meant to have all those veterans in your >> It mean a lot to me, man. I done learned a lot of ball over the last three years being with these guys. Uh I feel like Leo, Jay Reed, uh Law, they just helped me take my game to a whole another level. So having them guys, you know, give me a I feel like it g me a, you know, a lot of confidence in my play and just uh the ability, you know, to go play free and not have to worry about nothing cuz I know they got my back and I got theirs. >> You ever give them a hard time about being like the older guys in the group or anything or >> no? How big a difference is it trying to rush from the nose in the free tech for for people that don't understand the differences? How what fundamentally changes in that role for you when you're in the different spots? Uh well at the three you know you got a lot of space so you got uh a lot a lot more opportunities you know you can win B win in the B gap you can win B to A uh you know you can you can just mix it up you know from the three but from a nose standpoint man it's it's pretty hard cuz uh you know got the center and the guard right there so you pretty much rushing two really uh you hardly get any one-on- ones when you rushing at the nose. So man, it's uh it's a big it's a it's a bit difficult. You know, you got to be tight with your tight with your rushes, have have your hands ready, you know, when you at the nose position. So, uh every and then also too, everything just happening quicker at the nose spot. So, uh it's it's pretty challenging, but you know, I'm going find a way and you know, manage to get the job done. Byron, with it only being your third season, I it's year three though. Do you feel like some of the things that you've learned from those vets that now some of the younger guys on the team that maybe you've started to take on a little bit more of a leadership role? >> Oh, yeah, most definitely. Uh, I for sure I feel like I took a huge step in the uh far as like being a leader, leadership role, helping the younger guys, you know, no matter what it looks like far as like, you know, playing blocks, uh, reading formations, you know, um, uh, when it come, you know, pass rushing, you know, just little things just like just try to help them as much as I can, like just give them little nuggets, you know, to improve their game. >> What's the key in uh, playing off double double teams? How are we able to kind of you got more and more? How are you able to do that? Uh, I'm man, I've been playing doubles for a long time. So, and then the technique that I use, man, I've been using it for a while. So, it's really just like it's second nature now. So, when I'm playing a double or when I know I'm about to get a double, I'm not even thinking about it. I'm just I'm just reacting. >> What'd you get out of that joint practice? >> What did you get out of the joint >> Uh, I got a uh I got some good work in. Uh, I feel like that's what we needed, you know, going out there, you know, being in Tennessee, it was hot. Uh, so really just learning how to, you know, be comfortable with being uncomfortable. Uh, so I feel like that was very much needed, but feel like I got some great work out there. >> The, uh, rookie talent show, what was the highlight and the low light? >> Uh, I say the highlight was for me when, uh, man had the guitar. That that surprised me. I ain't know I ain't know he could play the guitar. And, uh, I say the low light uh, I don't know. I feel like everybody did good. I feel like everybody feel like everybody performed. Iron, for you guys as a defense, what Clark going down the preseason game, how tough is that for you guys to watch? Sounds like he might be out for a pretty long time. >> It's pretty tough, man, cuz you know, it's uh you hate to see that. You don't want to see nobody, you know, getting hurt or uh being injured or anything like that, but you know, we got Bud, you know, we got his back and uh you know, he could he could depend on us. So, whatever he got to do, you know, to get healthy, he can he can do that, man. So, he don't you know, he don't got to worry about nothing else. just focus on him and his recovery and getting healthy. >> Thanks, man.

title: Seahawks Final Week of the Preseason!
text: We are 15 days from opening kickoff of the Seahawks season, but still to come, another whole preseason game against a familiar face, NFL cutdown day, and a very important, almost practically uh addition to the Seahawks organization. What's up, twelves? This is the Seahawks collective by Hog Media. We are inching closer and closer to the start of the season. Even though it does feel uh like it was just last week that Mike McDonald was yelling, "We did not care for the first time with a Lombardi in his hand as a Seattle Seahawk." But before this season starts and they try to uh run it forward, still a few big things coming for the final days of the preseason. So, let's get into it. Here with me tonight are Seahawks insiders, Rob Stton from the Seahawks draft blog, who's going to have a lot of reframing to do if these rookies are going to go from college to the NFL, back to college. So Rob, we'll check in on the draft blog later. And Brian Nhauser, our Hawk blogger, keeping it a tight group here on the collective as of now, but stay tuned. You never know, maybe we could add a fourth box in here in the future. But hey, before we jump into it all with what's going on the Seahawks, we've now seen the Big 10 and SEC make some rules banning players who have signed or declared for pro drafts to uh re-enter college athletics. So Rob, like what have you been thinking during all of this because this really affects directly what you do with the Seahawks draft block? >> Well, I think it's another example of how college football has become a farce and um you know, it is ruined. It's not the sport that I kind of fell in love with about 20 years ago. And um yeah, I missed the old ways. I I I don't like all this transferring. Like I have a list of players who've transferred. It's enormous. It's usually like a it's probably like twice as long as a typical watch list just from the players who've swapped teams. And you know, players who who develop and and have success with teams, you know, then just go and transfer to Miami for a load of cash and to chase the glory in the last year. I'm not a fan of it. Like I don't like what's happened to the Pack 12. This is just preposterous. The players are just, okay, it didn't work out for me in the NFL this year. I'm gonna try and go back. You know, well done to the SEC and the Big 10 for basically saying, we're not going to allow this now. So, they're they're putting a stop to it. The other conferences should do the same. Um, I I really really want them to get a grip of this just disorganized chaos that has become college football. Well, I guess uh what players should do if you're looking to go back is just find the conference that's going to be slowest to make the rule change. Like get on top of it now because uh some conferences are already getting uh it going. But Brian, on things changing for you, I know that at this point of the season, your access to practice might change. So, what is what is your role just at the V-Mac even look like and and how does that look different going forward with the rest of the season? Yeah, it's it's a little bit of a a sad day when they let us know. I'll tell you the true story. So, uh there's a there's like a group text with PR and the Beat folks and I once we found out there's practice today and tomorrow and Thursday. I sent an a message to PR like, "Hey, is this going to be regular regular season rules or are we still going to get to watch practice?" And don't get a response. That means they probably don't know either. The coaches haven't made up their minds or they haven't told them or whatever. And so then we get down to the V-Mac and everyone's like, "Do you know? Do you know?" And nobody knows. And then we get the text, "Regular season rules." And so what that means is they trot us out in this like little pitiful line. Uh like people >> trot us out. >> It is. It's true. You know that. You know the drill, AB. and and we like take pictures and video of them stretching and jogging and then we are trotted back in uh to the media room to wait until practice is over. So, you know, I see Trayvon Diggs go out on the field and I'm like, "God, I would love to watch Trayvon Diggs practice today." I see Julian Neil in his uniform looking like he's going to practice. I've seen him do that four other times and then not actually practice. Did he actually practice today? I have no idea. So, and then you see you have other new names and faces. So, you get a little bit of information because before the Seahawks had announced that they had put some guys on IR, Mason Richmond, Bud Clark, which I know we'll talk about a little bit, there was new numbers and new faces. And so you're like, "Oh, if they have that many new guys, that probably means these other guys are going to be going on IR to create roster spots." So yeah, I think um that's uh that's kind of the state of covering the team during the season. And you know, eventually we'll start getting to talk to guys in the locker room and you get some conversations there. But for me, as somebody who really learns by watching and can assess by watching, it it's really tough to just be in a situation where you only get to assess and watch during the games. And uh so in some ways, I guess it's good because the all of us will now have basically the same information uh assessing this team going forward. Well, you'll have the first uh first take at any questions when you're at the the pressers, but certainly you feel so spoiled being there and then you get the you get trotted out, as Brian would say, and and uh and out to practice and get to see the warm-ups, but also probably seeing, you know, who's dressed, who's warming up, who's not, which is still valuable information uh for for folks to get ahead of time. But I do want to make note of just potentially new ownership officially soon. There was a meeting today in Atlanta. The league's owners are voting on whether or not to approve the sale of the Seahawks. Um, it should go through. There have been no red flags with the KOA family, which has just been so great as a Seahawks fan and covering the team. You know, there's no question about how impactful owners can be to NFL franchises with the decisions, the leadership influence, and even just like the publicity that they bring to organizations. You're seeing uh that around the league uh just even in the NFC West right now. So, no red flags on this deal and it looks like uh that it will go through. But just curious, Rob, your thoughts on this new ownership. You know, we've heard a little bit from ownership, but not too much. I did see something on Xenode uh commenting back. I believe it was on the discussion of grass or turf at Lumenfield and he said like I'll defer to uh the Super Bowl champions on that one. So, just would love like your first takes on what you've heard from this ownership so far. Well, I think that tweet was quite a a smart tweet because ultimately, yes, it was on a specific topic about the the turf, but it it also gave an example as to how they may well approach this to ultimately defer to the people who have done a very good job. And it by all accounts that tweet said to me, and I guess the proof will be in the pudding down the line, is that they are going to not come in here and reinvent the wheel. that they're going to come in and and place faith in the people who deserve the faith being placed in them in order to keep driving this franchise forward. So, I think that's good news. I'm looking forward to hearing from them. I'm I'm guessing they will do some kind of a press conference at some point. So, I'll be very interested to hear what they've got to say. And then the the other thing I would say is I just think what's somewhat a relief is that this has kind of just passed through without any real drama. There's not been any any divisiveness. What possible drama could there be with an owner, Rob? I don't know what you mean. >> Yeah. I mean, what could an owner possibly do that would be do not do not invite me to comment on the last 24 hours? We've been live on this show. We've been live on this show with crazy breaking news and we've been fortunate enough not to have to do um any ownership discussion. So hopefully we'll stay away from that with the Seahawks. But Brian, I know uh you're someone who really does do a a deep look into not only this team's X's and O's and the daily things that you see at practice, but really like the culture of the organization. So, just curious your initial thoughts on this ownership and and when we do get the news that this will be officially done. >> Yeah, I have I have mixed feelings. I I do and some of that has very little to do with the Koslas or whoever it would be. I think the the Paul Allen and Jod Allen era of owning this team was the best era of any professional sports franchise that I'm a fan of. Like, and you know, that includes Paul Allen owning the Blazers and it it wasn't as good as Paul Allen owning the Seahawks. And so, this has kind of been the golden era of Seahawks football. What you want, and I don't say this ominously, but I just what you want is for it to be a continuation of what it is. You don't want the Eddie Deardalo to to York family transition. Like you don't want like to go from champions to kind of not. And the reality is none of us know. They don't even know what this new era is going to look like. So I think there's a collective holding of breath that's going to go on and everything that they say or don't say is going to be used to help build a little bit more of a picture of of who they are and what kind of owners they're going to be and what kinds of stewards a you word that Venode used and I think is a meaningful one to the community as well as to the team and everything I have learned all the people I've talked to that that have familiarity with them that my interactions with people in and around has been really really positive. And that doesn't mean everything's going to be positive, but I think that signs are that these are folks with their heads on straight that want to win, that are going to invest in helping this team win in multiple different ways and that have the potential to bring some unique insight and unique advantages. Uh, for a team that loves chasing edges, I think this is a group that could help them find new edges. So, I'm hopeful, but I'm also a little mournful uh as this, you know, comes to an end. >> And he rhymes. Brian M. Hower. There you go, everybody. So, >> that's all I got for you, AB. >> Well, they did they did pay a high price for the team. So, they certainly will be investing in it and I'm excited to see uh what that holds for them this season. But before we recap what we saw in the Seahawks Titans game, which we'll get to, here's a quick video about an opportunity you have to take advantage of. Hey y'all. This year, I moved to Nashville, Tennessee, where there is always a concert, game, or live event to go see. And it's hard to keep track of it all. That's why I use SeatGeek, where you can find over 70,000 events listed. And right now, I got my eye on the Music City Kickoff, country music, and college football. I think that should work. And SeatGeek has your back. Every ticket is rated on a scale of 1 to 10, so you know exactly what you're getting. Plus, every ticket is backed by a buyer's guarantee. This app is so helpful to sift through all the different games, festivals, and concerts. So, write this down because there's a code just for you. Use Collective 10 for 10% off your next tickets at SeatGeek. Just download the app. Use Collective 10. And if you're going to go, go with SeatGeek. Hey, so uh the event's finally coming up. All right, Music City Kickoff. Let's go. Don't let me be the only one there, but we are loving what SeatGeek's doing. So, let us know if you get to uh use this cool opportunity and do something fun on your weekend. Uh what do you know? You know what? It's the summer time. You got to save it up while you can. But over the weekend, the Titans did come to where I am here in Nashville, Tennessee, and beat the Seahawks on the road 19-6. Seahawks are 0 and2 in their preseason games. However, Mike McDonald did say that he felt the team did get better from the week, the work that they got in at practice. Uh, so some some good, some highs, but also some heartbreaks that we saw with injuries come out of the Nashville weekend. Rob, I'll start with you. You've had some time to sit on this game. What stood out to you? We'll start with the highlight as a highlight from the Nashville weekend. The highlights, the obvious one is that the number two offense and defense played a very good first half against the Titan starters and uh you know they scored 16 points, could have had more obviously the missed kicks and only conceded three. Uh I thought there was a a difference in I thought the the organization of the two teams was marketkedly different, you know, and there was a coaching separation there between the two teams and their how prepared they were to play. There was the bit between the teeth from the Seahawks. Definitely they played with an edge in that first half. Clearly like responding to what happened the week before. Uh there was a lot of positive individual performances. The the block I mean that to see Christian Haynes pancake Jeffrey Simmons. I mean who would who would have thought we'd ever say those words. Uh you know two two big plays. Obviously the running play it's it's a blown coverage of the first one. The running play is perfectly executed. So, uh, came out of that feeling really good that, you know, my intention of the game was it kicked off at 1:00 a.m. was I had work the next day was to watch the first half, go to bed, wake up in the morning, and then watch the second half on a, you know, a condensed version of that. >> You probably woke up and thought, "Where am I? What is this? Did I click the right game?" >> No, cuz I'm a muppet. I I enjoyed the first half so much I watched the whole I decided to stay up and watch the whole game and I'm sat there in the fourth quarter thinking what am I doing? Like why am I watching this? Cuz the second half was awful. >> Well, Brian, I'll let you start at the first half where Rob may maybe should have gone to bed. Actually, preseason is when you got to give yourself that fluff. like you wake up, treat yourself, watch the rest the rest next morning, but we appreciate your dedication, Rob. So, so Brian, what was your highlight? I guess maybe from the first half or from the whole game. >> Well, I will say this. I I feel for Rob and for everyone who did watch that second half because it was rough, but it also it had every sign of being one of those preseason games where the team that won didn't win. and it just seemed like that was where this game was going to go. And what I mean by that is even if you read or listen to analysis from Titans reporters, fans, you know, whoever about that game, they weren't very happy about it. Like they were like, "The Seahawks backups whooped the Titans starters for a half." Yes. At the end, they took advantage of multiple Jaylen Milro turnovers and bad decisions on fourth down and, you know, a few other things to for Will Levis to to to win a game. I guarantee you guarantee you everyone in that Titans organization would have taken the opposite if they could choose to. They would have taken the loss and would have taken a strong first half over winning that game. And so what I really loved about the way that game started obviously is it was a complete it was a complete performance offensively and defensively. Jason Myers took the day off. Uh but you know you had the offensive line protecting you had the offensive line run blocking. You had the tight ends contributing in run blocking and in receiving. You had receivers. Montory Foster Jr. almost had a spectacular touchdown catch, very, very close. You had good quarterback play. Drew Lock didn't have an incompletion for, you know, most of that half. And then defensively, you had solid run defense. And and one of the things that really was disturbing to me, and I'm betting to the people in the V-Mac in that Dallas game, was how much they were manhandled on the interior part of both lines. The the Cowboys ran it up the middle and they were getting pressure right up the middle. And so this was the the opposite. And so I just I thought coverage was good. I I thought Michael Dansby had a really nice game. I thought um I thought Nehemiah Pritchette had a nice game. Obviously Chris Paul Jr. like I could keep going. There was a lot of guys DeAnthony Bell had a spectacular game. So it was great. And and like you throw in Conro Tulle and Jamie Sheriff, two guys that you want to see show something as edge rushers. It was pretty much everything that I had hoped would happen in this game other than winning it. >> Well, that's a good sign. >> Other than maybe Jaylen Milro playing a little bit better. >> Well, well, that's a good sign on the edge rushers. I know we talked about that last week, but you mentioned Jaylen Milro and I know that's a topic that Rob you've you've wrote about this week and I know you have been wanting to talk about, but just a question for you Rob first on that. Like I know not every NFL team will keep three quarterbacks on the roster and obviously with the great play that we saw from Drew Lock, not only in that first half, but really throughout the preseason, he's done a nice job. Do you think that is something the Seahawks will do is keep three quarterbacks? >> I don't know. I think that what might help Jayla Milro is there doesn't seem to be a a great debate as to who's going to be say the 51st player on this roster right now. like that it it does seem fairly predictable and these things are always a little bit unpredictable but I don't think there's a huge mystery as to who's actually going to make this team and if there were 56 players that they wanted to keep and they needed to keep a bit of extra depth say at receiver or safety or whatever because the injuries or any other position for that matter I think Milro could be in trouble because I I I just think we've here's what we've seen now we've seen a fairly unimpressive if we're being honest final season Alabama where he he did not play very well in a lot of the games. He had 16 touchdowns and 11 interceptions. Not great numbers in your final year of college football. A lot of those touchdowns came against opponents like Western Kentucky and Mercer.
