I know what will happen. I'll end up watching the whole game. Um, and I want to see I want to see a bit of, you know, some similar stuff to what we had in that first half in the last game. I want to see, you know, players really sort of saying, I'm going to be on this roster now and getting some clarity on that. I want to see Jayen Milro running as I was talking earlier and making some plays because, you know, I would rather him uh shine and and succeed and and have a great game than be proven right. Uh, you know, I want the Seahawks to win and I want the Seahawks players to have success. Uh, so I'd like to see that and and get a win. You know, let's have a win. I haven't won any of these two games yet. So, it'd be nice to see a win to send me off to Seattle on that. I mean, I will not I saying this, I will not be on the plane thinking of the third preseason game when I'm on the plane uh on that 10-hour flight. But, uh, it would be nice to have a win nonetheless against the Chiefs to finish things off. >> Brian, did you tell us where you were going to eat with Rob? Did you tell say the restaurant? >> I don't know if I'm going to publicize >> I don't know. Well, I was gonna say >> the hordes will be outside. >> You've got to be part of of my ring of honor in order to go to that. And uh Rob is is an honorary guest. You would absolutely be on the honorary guest list. >> Man, you guys, maybe I got to go. I got to go. Rob and I have never met in person, so I feel like I'll make it happen. >> He's very tall. >> Let's make it happen. >> Let's make it happen. Well, we'll see. We'll see. I I might care a little bit more about how this game goes. I don't know. It would be awesome to see. I don't know. I think I care more about I'm so excited about this next Hard Knocks episode. We have just been spoiled for this preeason getting to watch getting some more inside access. So, I do want to get to that quickly before we wrap up. But, but Brian, for you to walk away from the preeason just feeling extra confident about this team, what's one thing that you would love to see or even are interested to see? You know, I don't know if it's realistic, but I think the closest thing that would actually have implications for the regular season that would make me feel good would be like Trayvon Diggs looking like Tyrese Knight did in the first game. Like that would be like, oh man, like maybe he is healed up. This is his first off seasonason where he's been able to be healthy and not rehabbing. That would be pulling a rabbit out of the hat. Like that would be cool. For the most part, it is it is it would be a lie, and I try not to do those. Uh to say that there's anything that could happen in this preseason game that would have real implications. I don't want anyone to get injured, but there's not even in that case, there's not a lot of folks that are going to be on that field that are probably going to be on the 53man roster or play a lot of snaps. So, this is really to me it's for people that really love football, which I do, and really love reality and the the lives that people lead because there's guys that are going to be on that field that have been dreaming of making an NFL roster since they were a little kid. And this is their last ditch effort to do so. And I love every single one of those stories, whether or not they work out or they don't. And so, I'll be watching and cheering and and hoping that they get a moment that they and their families can uh can cherish. Well, a player I know Hard Knocks has been featuring is Uso Semalo, uh, who did get a little bright spot in the rookie talent show that you might get a sneak peek, well did get a sneak peek at, and we'll see tonight on Hard Knocks. Uh, he brought the bars with a guitar, did some singing, got the whole team going. So, I know we will get to see that tonight for the fourth of five Hard Knocks episodes. But Rob, what are you maybe excited to see or something that you would like to see in one of these final episodes from HBO? Yeah, I I always enjoy the John Schneider stuff just because I think it gives you an insight into how a front office operates, how a GM operates, kind of conversations he has. I mean, as as a bit of a draft geek and everything that kind of comes with the stuff that putting the team together. I, you know, you do kind of imagine how those conversations go and and what you know, the kind of conversation internally with the agents. That was quite an interesting conversation here on the phone about Terry and Arnold with the agent last last week. I think that was last week. So, all of that stuff is interesting to me. So, I uh I will have a lot more of that if if it's on offer in this episode, which I am staying up to watch for another hour because I've got the day off tomorrow. >> Let's go, Rob. Some some free sleep there for you and uh enjoyable time to watch the show for you. For you, Brian. We know we saw some Jake Bobo, too. Also, some digs, that conversation that Rob had mentioned. But the talent show is so fun. What are you excited to watch tonight? Yeah, I I I just hope that we see a little bit more of the the personalities and and some stories develop and now they had at least something happened in the game that was positive so they can try to pay off some of those stories instead of having all of them dead end as they did last week. So yeah, I mean whatever stories they're going to tell, I'm I'm eager to watch them and and you know, I've gotten to know some of the folks telling those stories and and they're working their tails off. So, I I'm I'm hoping that uh I'm hoping it's a little bit better of an episode than last week, to be honest. >> It was It was a little bit of a dead end. I won't I won't lie. I kind of was like, "Oh, it's over." Okay. So, hopefully we'll see a little bit more tonight. It's hard when you when you cover a team and you spend so much time watching them. It's a bummer when it ends. Uh a little bit of a a hang at the end there, but we want to make sure the twelves can keep up with what you all have going on and make sure we don't make them late for the showing tonight. So, Rob, what do you have coming up on your channel this week? Uh well, I've got a piece up there now which talks about uh three things Jaylen Milro and uh Jason Meyers and and a bit of trade stuff at the end. So go and check that out. And uh did a video last night on the on the YouTube channel. So uh go and check that out if you've got a bit of time as well. >> All right, Brian, what about for you? I know you have a million shows going on these days. >> A few fewer than a million now. So, we'll have Real Hawk Talk tomorrow night, five o'clock with uh Evan Hill and Jeff Simmons. And hopefully we'll have some ownership news to talk about in that episode. If there is ownership news, I will probably do an emergency pod after that breaks. And then we've got other stuff coming on the rest of the week. So, yeah, lots of good stuff coming up on Friday. So, it'll be here before you know it. >> It'll be here quick, but make sure you have your notifications on for Brian Brian Nemhauser's channel because we love those emergency pods. You got to freak out and have a little moment. What on earth just happened? Uh, and for all you twelves in Oregon, I recently interviewed Poncho Eupani Lauulu from Hawaii, the Oregon Center. He'll be his interview on Sports Spectrum will be dropping on Monday on our channel. So stay tuned for that. And uh, if you like some lacrosse, we got the Premier Lacrosse League quarterfinals this this weekend on Saturday. You can catch me running through the sidelines trying to keep up with the pace of play. And that sport is absolutely crazy. Just try to stay alive on the sideline. But that's all we got for you all tonight. Thanks so much for tuning in to the Seahawks Collective. From myself, Brian, and Rob, good night. Go Seahawks. And go watch Hard Knocks.

title: Brian Daboll, John Fassel & Gus Bradley Speak Before Bears Week | Press Conference
text: So, been grinding away uh pretty much the last week of training camp coming up. Uh with the practice against our guys today, then get on to Chicago. We put a lot on these guys in terms of installation. Uh I think Robert's done a great job of devising the way that he wants to practice, the amount of reps we've got. Uh the amount of times we've been in full pads, it's been very helpful. Uh certainly always trying to improve execution. Uh but happy with where the guys are at. It's been a competitive training camp. Uh still got a long way to go here. Uh but time is short. You know, we got about 20 days or 19 days until the first game. So, you know, keep doing the things we need to do in terms of focusing on today, getting better at the things we can get him better at. And uh it's been good. I've been been pleased with where the guys are at. >> What can be done to kind of work on Cam's downfield accuracy and connecting on more plays, you know, from 15 to 20 yards or or longer? And is that something that with in terms of accuracy and throwing the ball, is that is that something to work on in offseason or is that something that you can work on even as the season's going? >> Yeah. Well, I Well, I think that's a good question. You know, those those 15 to 20 25 yard plays. You know, there's not a lot of teams that just throw the ball 35 plus down the field. Uh I think Seattle was somewhere around the top and they were eight of 15 last year and the amount of times they did it. the the intermediate chunk plays, whether that's um layered throws, man-to-man throws, I mean, that's that's encompassing everybody. So, it's the receiver. It's incumbent upon the receiver to take proper angles. It's incumbent upon the protection and then ultimately Cam hitting the plays. Uh but that's just not on Cam. Uh certainly not on Cam, all of it. It's a combination of things and we've been working on it. we'll continue to work on. That's part of the execution stuff that, you know, we're going to continue to grind away at. Um, but that's an element of our offense that that we got to improve. >> Cam said after the game that he it feels like the offense isn't far away from kind of clicking the way you all would like. How do you see the progress and and learning this scheme and and getting it down to so that they can, you know, do it on the field? >> Sure. Uh, look, we're doing that every day and there's been really good days. There's been days where it hasn't been good enough. Um, but that's a collective thing. That's that's all of us in this together. And that's what offensive football is about is making sure everybody's on the same page, which we got smart guys. Uh, Mike has done a good job of bringing guys in that that can retain a lot of information. And then ultimately it comes down to executing the rep. Uh, and you're going to get different looks on on all those things, but I think the guys are in a good spot. Um, we got a smart, tough offensive line. That's where it starts. I think Cam has really grasped what we want to do. And, you know, we just got to continue to build and work on, you know, the execution part of it. And those are, you know, those are good to have. It's it's you want everything to be perfect, but those are good days to have when things aren't going right. Uh seeing the guys, how they react. Uh even these preseason games are are really good for for all of us cuz we've never been together in a game. So the communication on the sideline, going through the iPad, going through the pictures. Um they're all valuable experiences. >> How beneficial has it been for Carmona to kind of grab a hold of that job early just for the sake of continuity? Yeah, you know, that's an important part of of offensive line play as well is, you know, is as soon as you can get the five guys that are working together on a consistent basis because uh the communication in that area, sometimes it's one little word and when you're playing next to a guy for continual practices and in games, uh that's certainly a benefit. Uh so he's done a nice job. Uh again, these young guys, uh they're still learning the game of of the NFL. Uh but they've done a nice job and Carmona is is one of them. >> When he started out on fire, we kind of >> One more time, >> Carell Tate. He started out a really good start on fire, I guess you could say, but he kind of faded away a little bit. >> What can you do to to get him back on track? >> Well, I would say fading away obviously numbers, catches, that's that's what everybody sees, which I understand that it's a that's a job of a receiver. But in terms of what he's doing and how he's doing it, um, he's done a nice job. So, he's where he's supposed to be, uh, look, that that was a tough play and and look, we got to make tough plays in this league. But I have a great amount of confidence in in Tate and and how he goes about his business, what he does on the practice field. Um, look, I think everybody would love to have 15 catches. I'd love to have 15 catches. Um, but he's doing the right stuff. He's in a good head space. He's where he's supposed to be. And I have a lot of confidence in in Carnell. >> It seems like you're starting to move him around a little bit more as opposed to like just at X. Is that something by design that that came about or was that always the plan? >> No, I'd say again place a premium on these guys understanding different positions. So whether it's, you know, Tate or DK or Ell the five of those guys that have been going with the ones at a consistent basis, uh, they know really all the spots. Um, and that's important in terms of conceptualizing the play, being where you're supposed to be, uh, whether that's inside, outside. So, you know, we keep throwing that at him. Again, today is, you know, another day of kind of adding a few new wrinkles to kind of see how it looks before you really get going. Uh, it'll be an important day for us. >> You know, guys, obviously be making the final decisions, but how much do you voice your opinion on certain guys as you get close to these roster cuts being made? >> Yeah. Well, look, that's at the end of the day, that's going to be, you know, Mike and and Coach Sal's job. But there's definite interaction um you know, on a daily basis and then definitely after games with the the coaches and the personnel side and and you need that to be a pretty good organization. You need to have give and take. Uh you have to express what you think of the players. They're going to express what they think of the players. You come to a common ground, but at the end of the day, you know, Mike and and coach St are going to make those decisions. But the the give and take uh here is is been very good. >> When we hear Robert talk about the no game planning for preseason and we also hear about how vanilla the plays are where you're not necessarily running your own stuff. Where do these plays come from? Like what are you guys running in the preseason? >> We have tons of plays. So again, it's really it's more about the execution of the plays um more than anything else. So just going out there doing what you're supposed to do under competitive lights. Uh and making sure that you know your teammate can trust you, your coach can trust you. Um so again, you can pull from a lot of different things. And every team does it. It's not it's not just the Tennessee Titans. It's, you know, there's an evaluation part of it. There's also an execution part of it, which make no mistake, whether it's a practice, a preseason game, whatever it may be, we're looking for optimal execution um every time we're out on the field. How much grace do you have to get the players knowing that you're looking for execution and something that they might not be super familiar with? >> Yeah, look, everybody's got a job to do. So, when we go into whatever it may be, a practice where we're putting in, you know, however many new plays today or it might be a preseason game, it's going to certainly happen during the regular season game. That's our job. So, there's no excuses about anything like that. Um, you know, our job is to go out there and and and operate at a high level of uh execution every time we're out there. Considering the what they had to learn in terms of the system and principles and things and then some new guys and JC came back from injury. Has the offensive line especially in the run game maybe been the most pleasant surprise to you? >> Yeah, again it's it's the ultimate team game. So am I pleased with the offensive line? Are we pleased with the offensive line? They've done a nice job. Uh certainly we can be better all the way around in really all the spots, but those guys have done a nice job of communicating. It starts with slotty and you know getting things set for the guys and then working together. It's a they're banging on guys every play. Um you know they've played physical and they've played smart and those are two play good places to start. >> We've seen when Levis has been in there a lot of quarterback runs designed RPOS's with him keeping it and and whatnot. What what's kind of the I guess the entailment of that? >> Yeah, I think he can do it. Um, so, you know, that's part of our offense. Um, and I think he's pretty good at it. So, he's a big strong guy. Um, we've had other quarterbacks that are able to to do those type of things and and want to give him an opportunity to go out there and and show some things that he can do um that we like doing. You >> started by saying you're pleased with where the guys are at specifically with the first team offense. What are you most pleased with? Like, what have they done the best so far? Yeah, that's again every day I I appreciate their attitude. I appreciate their commitment to learning this stuff. And then going out there, there's been a lot of good execution and then when there's not as good execution because the defense plays well, too. They've done a great job of coming in collectively watching the tape, going through it, making the corrections, and then, you know, we talk about don't be an error repeater, make the same mistake twice. You know, that's what training camp is for, is to make sure that we're we're diving into the information. We're going to go out there and make mistakes. When we go out there and we get it again, let's make sure we nail that one. >> How has that translated into the two preseason games with the first team in your opinion? And like, what's the margin for error there? >> Uh, look, these guys have I'm pleased with where we're at. I'm pleased with mentally where we're at. Uh, when I say pleased, I'm not happy. We want to score points every time we go out on the field. But again, the process of which the coaches are going through with the players, the process that I see the players have, we're just going to keep building on that. And you know, ultimately it comes down to to execution and that's what we're working hard on. >> What do you think what do you think your offense is going to be known for this year? You come in, it's it's all new. You're new. You're learning these guys this month. >> You feel like you have your finger on the pulse of what you're going to be known for. >> Yeah, I think time will tell. You know, there's a long way to go here. Uh, and we're just at the the tail end of training camp. So, uh, I think keep the main focus, the main focus. Uh, be good at fundamentals. That's where it's going to start, particularly early on in the season. Take care of the ball. Make good decisions uh, with those who handle the ball and be a physical unit. Now, that's what we want to be. We got to go out there and do it >> between you and the people who are making all that decision. >> I think collaborative for sure. I think you know um Boroni and coach Salah and myself and the rest of the staff I think we all do a great job of collaborating on those decisions and the back end of the roster is made up of you know guys that can perform on special teams as well as be viable backups at the positions that they play on offense and defense. So, I think it's been pretty similar to every place I've been as far as making those decisions on who's the last five guys to make the team, then who's also the practice squad, which is a huge thing for us cuz our practice squad guys always end up playing, you know, two to three games a year minimum. So, it's just always an awesome collaboration of everybody contributing to what's best for the team. >> Are you a pound the table kind of guy? When you've got certain guys, you're like, I got to have this dude on on my unit. No, I I think I I feel confident that I voice my opinion on a player's production and potential. Production more important than potential. But I'm always cognizant of what's best for the team. And a lot of times, and I understand this, what's best for the team might not be what's best for special teams. And I think it's actually very common. And so I think years and years ago I come to grips with that because the longer I'm in the NFL, the less selfish I become. I think the less selfish hopefully everybody becomes where when you you first get started, you want to make sure like your squad is tightened up because, you know, I want to have a job. But as the years go by, it's it's, you know, and I can honestly sit up here and say this, it's way more about the team and what's best for the team. And special teams is always, I think, a factor and a part of that for sure, but I don't want to be selfish with, you know, this guy should make the team because he's great on special teams, but he can't contribute on offense and defense. And so, yeah, I think I'm proud of myself for my career has come the last probably 10 years where that's obviously been the number one driving factor is what's best for the team. Understanding that what's best for the team might not be what's best for special teams and that's okay. How does it help how does it help you and your your unit though when you see guys >> that are on the bubble, you know, guys like Chestnut, but he's a valuable special teams guy. When you see that him have success in the preseason games. >> Oh, it's it's awesome. I mean, me and Coach Stewart are his biggest fan when he's running the football. You know, give it to Juice, move the chains. You know, we're on the sideline hooting and hollering and we talk about this in the special teams meeting all the time. Most of the time, special teams is a way to get a roll on game day, especially for young guys, put a jersey on, being part of the 48 on game day, and then as their careers go, their roles most of the time change into starting offensive or starting defensive players. That's the goal. Even for us as special teams guys, very few times you have a guy whose career is going to be a special teams guy. Um, we had that in Dallas for five years with a player named CJ Goodwin. He was just special teams guy and he knew that and we knew that. Everybody else was in a developmental role to make sure they're available on game day to to be a special teams player priority number one because they're a backup, but at some point developing into an offensive defensive starter. And I've seen that happen over the course of years where I have a great special teams player and all of a sudden he gets an opportunity to start a linebacker and he does and he nails it and he gets paid to to do that and um I'm the I'm his biggest fan. So, it's to a long-winded answer to a great question is, yeah, when we see special teams guys in preseason or regular season performing at a high level on offense or defense, it brings incredible joy to me. >> You've been around Joy for a couple years here. What has allowed him to stay in the league as long as he has? What's he like on a day-to-day basis? >> Yeah, that's a fantastic question. And this might seem like a a bad answer, but it's the truth. his uh I don't know if there's a perfect word for it, just resilience, perseverance, kind of what I'm trying to say is um it always feels like Joey's on the bubble, but he's such a great kicker. He really is. And I think for him to have confidence and people that believe in him uh I think makes him play better. And I think he's an incredible kicker who over the next couple years hopefully, you know, he he becomes a staple of a team, which I think he is for us. He's, you know, he's 88 this preseason. Um, you know, has a new holder. He's just tough. He's a football player. He's got the mindset of, you know, a miskick. I bounce back. I don't freak out about stuff. I don't overthink stuff. And I think it's taken him a couple years to get to that point, too, where let me take a little bit of the thinking out. Let me just play the game. like if I was a linebacker covering a kickoff, what would be my mindset? Like just go, just kick it, just tackle it, you know? Um, so I'm I'm proud of him for his fight back when maybe he doesn't get what he wants contractually or he fights through some not bad days, but miss kicks like everybody does. He's just tough, man. He's tough and I'm proud of him. as you're going through this process and I understand you have your stuff to worry about, but how much time do you spend like keeping an eye on the other team's special teams unit and watching throughout the league? >> You guys were on fire today, man. Great, great, great question. Right now, I spend no time on it. Uh, it's all about us and during the preseason, right or wrong, I don't scout an opponent. I don't give our guys information on what they do. We're just playing. But when the preseason ends, so this Saturday is our last game, um I'll be given projects to go and look at certain players at certain positions to see how they performed on special teams. And I think a great example of that was Dorian Mousie last year. He got cut from Minnesota in the third after the third preseason game and we were needing of a linebacker, especially a special teams guy. So a Borggonian staff gave me some linebackers to look at and you know, Mousie showed up was like, man, if they cut this guy, like we got to jump on it. They cut him, we claimed him. So, that's kind of how the process goes. At least for me, I want to focus on our players, our competition, our techniques, because there's a lot to work on. Um, and then when I'm given projects, once the preseason games end, then I'll dive in for probably a week's worth on the projects that I'm given by our front office. And, um, that's kind of how it goes. When we when we hear so much about how important it is for the starters on offense, starters on defense to get these preseason reps, why is it less important or why is it maybe not being prioritized for Chim to go back there at least once in the preseason? >> Yeah, excellent. Uh we did it against San Francisco. Want him to go back there and just fair catch it just to get just to get a catch. A lot of times it's very unpredictable who's going to be on the field for us in the return game. And that's not saying anything. It's just um I think we know what he can do. We get a ton of reps in practice where he's not live and that's really the goal is, you know, get the great reps in practice, get a few touches in a game where he's not exposed. Um again, when we go p return or kick return, hey, give me 10. You know, we throw bodies out there, we count to 11 real quick and we're good. Okay. I can't sometimes predict exactly who's going to be out there, what's going to happen. So, it's a little bit of me just, you know, protecting an allp pro returner. >> As far as your gunner options, where does Bryce Hoffer kind of stack up? >> I think he's right there. I think he's right there in the top of the mix for us with, you know, quite a few other guys. So, he's been fantastic in the punt and punt return game, uh, as he's developing his kick, kick return game. Um, and he was a starting gunner for us last year. He's probably our gunner number one until he got hurt against the Rams. Um, so I think he's picked up better than he even left off before that injury just with some more confidence. But I think he's he's right in the top of the pack and I think we got a few good candidates and he's right there with the rest of them. >> His attitude kind of with one of the things that separates Bryce is his embracing of that role. >> I think so. Um, whether it separates him or not, I'm not sure. I think we have, I might be biased, but I think we have a ton of guys who embrace the competitive, you know, fighting for roster spot mindset. Uh, he's definitely one of them with absolutely the right frame of mind. And I think there's a lot of guys that have that same mindset, which is why I think our practices and guests ourselves have been more competitive than joint practices or preseason games. Obviously balls are not live so there's not the tackling part of it but from the ball snaps up until like the the returner gets tagged off in practice like our guys fight in a great way and it's and it's been good >> curiosity we fixate so much on the gunners when we talk to you are they really more important than the interior positions or just why why does that get so much attention >> because I don't think anybody pays attention or knows what to look for enough when you're looking at the core everybody talks about gunners returner uh maybe personal protector, but but nobody's really talking about that guard on punt team, that tackle on punt team, that wing on punt team, the 543 on kickoff. It's just harder to evaluate and maybe even see it. But man, those core bodies, those linebackers and pass rushers and safeties, you know, when it gets really messy inside, you don't see it because it's like, you know, but outside in the gunner world, there's one ones and there's a ton of space. We can see all that. But those core bodies, you know, those linebackers, I'll just say like linebackers are my gold pieces. Many of those guys we can get out there, the better we are. >> You touched on Julius earlier. What What has Chestnut done to kind of establish himself here for several years? >> Um, short of everything. >> Everything. I Everything. >> I mean, everything. tackling, blocking, returning, protecting, leadership, attend, like everything. I I everything, you know, he's he's one of the best I've ever had. Last year, we keep a point chart for production and participation for a regular season. My 18 years as a coordinator doing the same exact point chart. He had he scored the highest number of points in any regular season for special teams in my 18 years. He does everything. He's incredible. DAS and early training camp kind of showing a big picture of what this thing should look like and I think our guys understand that you're going to see kind of a renewed focus on the details now. Um, for example, like tackling, you know, some things I thought we tackled fairly well, but where there's some hidden yardage there, right? Like instead of being second eight, there was second and four. So, all these leaky yardage things, those are more detailed things, fundamental things that we're really going to hone in on now. So really, you know, narrow our focus. Let's get all that, you know, the big picture thinking. They understand that part of it narrowing in that. So there's stories like that that took place throughout the game. >> Guy like Anthony Hill, we see him making plays on the practice field and had had an interception in the preseason game. How do you know when a guy like that is ready maybe to ascend into a bigger role than maybe what he's had so far? >> You're right. You There is no doubt. you've seen him make some plays, some big plays in practice or in the games like you've seen. So now the big challenge for him is just the consistency. You know, I think everybody loves Anthony, but that trust of every play, play in and play out. Uh, you know, as far as making the calls, getting things set up, the checks, things like that from where he was to where he is now, much better. But I think that's the aspect now. It's just that more consistency. Is the lack of pressure from your Is the lack of pressure from your first unit on the defensive line more a product of of lack of scheming at this point or just lack of winning one-on-one? >> Yeah, I mean there's I think now you're seeing this like in certain situations it's more all right let's put them in this situation so we can best identify skill sets what they do well. So, you know, sometimes games, different things, you know, we might not call a game in a certain aspect in a in a game in a real game, but in this game, we need to see just how it looks. So, there's some of that going on just not only evaluate the players, but also the scheme. >> Are you seeing the kind of progress that you would like to from the secondary as a unit as far as communication and those things? >> Yeah. Uh, well, Hooker and Kub are both really, really good communicators. We're finding that out about those two right now. So, they handle the backend shoot. There's some things they're communicating to up in the front. Um they they do a really good job. Flat I think is playing very well for us. He's consistent. There's a lot of trust with him. Alante, I think for Alante, it was his training camp where he's just grown and grown and you're starting to see him be the true Alante now. Like he's tackling, he's physical. And we say as a defense, you know, you you kind of look at a defense to see how physical they are by how well your corners tackle and how physical they are. So it showed up. He hit a couple tackles. Flat has shown some in practice. So, those are all good signs from the back end. >> Bit of a football 101 question, but Robert talks a lot about the adjustment from match to vision. Can you explain the differences between the two styles and why one is advantageous in this? >> Sure. It's it's um let's let's call match more like man, you know, where your eyes are locked in, you're playing a man to where your vision now is on the quarterback. So, all of your the skill set that needed. Now, every team's going to play three deep. Every team's going to play split safety. Every team in this league is going to play man. But how much you know what's the percentage? And um you know they did a good job. They had all three last year. They played a little bit more match coverage where we're more a little bit more vision on the quarterback at times. So that's the process because when you're on the quarterback, your plant and break has to be elite. You have to to get your tightness in coverage. And so that there's a little bit of transition in that aspect, but that that's gotten better. but still not where we need it. >> Is it just coaching preference or is there an advantage to choosing to >> Well, it depends who you talk to, right? And and that's why everybody's going to have some sort of match coverage. So, it's not that you know what are you against it. It's just primarily what is your philosophy? And the theory is you know tighter coverage, you take away windows, zone coverage, you got a chance to get more takeaways, you know, because your vision's on the ball tips and overthrows and things like that. now you might have a stronger possibility of those things taking place. >> Anything more frustrating as a defensive coordinator than allowing chunk plays? And when when those happen, what's your process for reacting to the teachable moment? >> Well, there is a reaction even though it's preseason, right? But, uh, I mean, some of it there's always going to be unscouted looks in the season, you know? So, it was a great opportunity, a little bit of an unscouted look, but it's what a great message to send a team. Well, you're gonna have unscouted looks on Sunday and you're gonna have these opportunities. So we just weren't clean. That was, you know, the big run was more of a trickle down effect. We didn't do a good job in the line. We didn't do a good job in the second level. We didn't do a good job in the third level. So it was more of a trickle down effect like that. And it really gave us the opportunity to stress the importance of, you know, just don't guess, don't over analyze, just do your job and trust when you do your job, it'll all come together. So it was one of those moments. Although it was frustrating, you never like to give up a play like that. It was a great teachable moment. As we go through these preseason games, we we keep hearing, okay, well, you know, the the play calls are vanilla. >> What is very vanilla, like how much of a difference is there between the play calling being vanilla and you actually going out there and working your your actual scheme? >> Well, I mean, I would say that it becomes probably you're still working on your fundamental principles in preseason games. you're going out there and you're playing your coverages and you're really honed in on the skill set of the player. How good are we fundamentally? And more so than maybe, hey, this is a a tendency that we have. Let's go ahead and execute this pressure or execute this coverage and go about it that way. You're probably not seeing a lot of that in preeason. You're see you're seeing more can we execute and can we execute with a high level of execution and fundamental work. So, it's a little bit of a change in mindset, but I mean, you're you're still evaluating personnel at this stage. You know, we will this week. I mean, it's always you might have a number of your guys decide on, but there's always those who's the who's the other guys that you're looking at. So, it's important to put them in position and that's kind of what we did in the game was play more vanilla so we can just see them operate in space, try not to have a lot of thinking going on and see how they execute. >> How much do you have a degree of experimenting? Like I saw in one play, you know, Jeff kind of loop outside uh from the inside to to go in. Like that's something that he didn't do as much last year. Like how much do you experiment and see how >> th those things? That's right. That's part what I was mentioning before. All right, let's see their skill set. Let's see. Maybe he hasn't done that much. It might not be the most opportune time to do it. We may not do that in a game, but we need to see it. And so, you know, that that's a great example of it. Let's see, you know, what he can do, you know, how he feels about that at the comfort level. What do we need to work on and is that going to be a big part of what we do? >> What have you seen from a guy like Tony Adams and specifically with a new defense and a lot of new pieces in the secondary? Does he bring, you know, a weapon to you back? >> He's great versatility. So, he'll be safety. He can also play nickel. He's brings great energy, great spirit when he's in the game. There's a sense of calm with him. He understands by playing in the system the standard that it takes. So so valuable so valuable to all aspects of our of our defensive unit. There's tremendous trust in him. Tremendous trust in him. Whether he's playing nickels safety or free safety, strong safety, it doesn't matter. He's just um he's got a lot of plays under his belt in this system. >> How's Germaine been? Germaine Johnson. >> Uh good. Good. He's uh you know what? He's a physical player. He's again another one that understands the standard and um a quiet but presence player that u you know brings that to the line. I think you're seeing him and Jeffrey get you know gravitate towards one another and relationshipwise and that's always good. So I just he's been a great great addition. I can't say enough about him. How he handles himself, his work ethic, his professionalism, how he goes about it. He's been really good. >> You lost J for the season. How do you see guys that Jaylen Harrell? You see guys stepping up in the battle with kind of replace them. >> Yeah, there's always stories that will take place, you know, and and you're going to see there's going to be times where maybe a guy was a third teamer for us and all of a sudden he's going to get reps at the ones, you know, and let's see, you know, he he does good against the thirds. Let's see what he can do versus the ones. That's what you might see at times in this joint practice with Chicago. And it's, you know, see who can pick up that slack. Who's the guys that going to elevate with an opportunity presented?

title: Warner Talks Becoming a Team, Training Camp Progress | 49ers
text: What have you seen from Larry Ward today, out there? From Larry Ward, rookie Larry Ward. >> I'm sorry, say it one more time. >> Larry Ward, linebacker, uh undrafted rookie. >> Oh, yeah, Larry. He's uh Larry just continued to get better, man. I've loved what I've seen from Larry uh from the moment he he came onto the team, you know, you expect rookies to come in and bring great energy, and I think he's done that uh and he's continued to get better at playing the position. I know he has a safety background, but learning how to play off the stack off the ball linebacker, using his hands, getting on and off blocks, um being a physical player, you know, I think he's done a great job. >> All right, so Kyle said that, you know, Jed's arrest had no effect on the team in the field. I mean, it's impossible to ignore and and not see what's going on. So, what what's been the talk in the locker room among you guys about Jed? And you've obviously known him for so long, so what what are your your thoughts on it? >> Yeah, no, I mean, Cam, we're we're all aware, right? I think we all have social media, so we see things. Um but at the same time, you know, I got a lot of love, a lot of respect for Jed, and don't feel the need to to comment on the situation. I think the team is kind of the same way. Like, it was it really wasn't a conversation being had in the locker room. Of course, yeah, you notice it, but um at the same time, we're so hyper-focused in this building of of trying to prepare for week one. You know, a lot of guys are on the bubble trying to even make the team. So, you know, we're we're just trying to get better as a football team and letting that that, you know, that's a personal situation, letting it stay personal with with him. >> You obviously had Kyle's accident at the beginning of to start of camp, and you have this. I know they're not the same thing at all. They're not the football team, but does it just hit you like there's a lot of stuff been going on or outside this team this this just this last few weeks? >> Yeah, I mean, I didn't really put that together until you until you just spoke on it, because if I'm being so, you know, honest about it, training camp is a beast in itself when it comes to just football and preparing yourself uh for what a 17 game season uh entails. Kyle's done a tremendous job of, you know, recovering and being present for us as as the as the head coach. And you know, it's been a seamless transition for, you know, what he went through. We're we're so like I said, again, we're so hyper-focused on on what we got to do on the field. That that kind of stuff that may get, you know, there's different narratives and things that are talked about maybe whether it's social media or amongst you guys and everything or amongst the fans. In here in this building is it truly is all about football and trying to make sure we have the best product on the field for everybody, right? For ourselves and for everybody that's counting on us. So, I mean I that truly hasn't really been a thought in my mind or the rest of the team, I'd say. >> But through through the spring and even early in camp when you were asked how different you think the defense is going to look this year, I think you said, "We'll see." Now that you've been through basically all of camp here, how different do you think things are going to look on that side of the ball this year? >> Yeah, I mean it is going to look a little different. We do have similarities as well of things that we've run in the past. So, it's just really a blend of putting those things together and running them as seamlessly as possible. Um you know, the things that the thing that will always remain the same is the style of play. I always talk about, right? The the speed, the physicality, the energy that we bring with little wrinkles here and there as to what we'll we'll run in the season, but you know, it is a blend at the end of the day. So, I guess we'll have to see week one what that looks like. >> Is it enough Is it enough difference for you that this camp has been a little more challenging in some ways just in terms of the things you need to be aware of getting guys lined up, things like that? >> No, I mean at the end of the day, you know, I think that part's always come to me pretty naturally. And like I said, there is a lot of stuff that I've already done in the past that we're we're still doing. And so, for me it was honestly just getting back to form having not played football in a long time which that happened pretty quickly for me and uh yeah, just just continuing to get reps. >> You and >> and Brock have been chirping back and forth for for years now. Uh We noticed it the other day Brock was particularly loud. >> [laughter] >> Um >> You're ready, huh? >> Is that is that the most I don't know animated you've seen him and is it is it more so this year I mean has it been growing year to year with him? >> Yeah, it's definitely I think it's been a growth and you know, I love Brock with all my heart. I love everything that he's about the competitor that he is. Uh you know, the confidence that he exudes now to to send it back to me, you know, as long as I'm a far far enough distance away and can't retaliate you know, I'm just kidding. But yeah, man. I mean that's that's great. At the end of the day it's for me personally, I'm trying to create an environment that is as game like as possible, right? And and Brock's the same way. I think when him and I are going like that, you know, and I'm I'm chirping at him. I'm chirping at the offense all day and they're sick and tired of it and they finally get me and you got the whole offense cheering because I you know, they got me or something like that and we're on the 500th day of training camp and you you know, that kind of energy is out there. It's like man, you're doing something right, right? So I think that's what every building around the around the league is trying to search for at this point in in camp where it is kind of a lull of guys, you know, on the bubble trying to make it as a third preseason game coming up versus you know, guys who are truly trying to get better for week one and it's like how can you breed an environment of competition to where everybody's getting better at the end of the day. And so that's that's what it truly is all about. >> I know you don't have a lot of interactions with with Mac Jones just cuz you're on a different unit, but how is he in that in that the chirping department? >> I mean you you know Mac Jones. He he got he he got plenty to say. So he's not lacking in uh in things to say, but at the end of the day man, they're out there trying to play the position better than anybody. I think the the the talking and all that gets gets kind of lost in that that part is not as important as actually you know, executing and doing your job. >> I'm just talking about the training camp you guys have kind of made it in a few Have you seen a growing of comfortability in in Raheem's new system on the defense when it comes to the younger guys, when it comes to you guys all learning this new defense and if so, how? >> Yeah, I mean it's it's it's it's a constant, you know, process of finding, you know, mastery, right? What you do and, you know, we whether it's a new system, whether it's a new DC, which we've dealt with, you know, over the past what, five seasons, it's just a constant just everybody's starting to really familiarize each other familiarize themselves with each other through the process and, you know, I've talked about it won't be a finished product come week one, right? We're going to have to try to find what's the best product that we can put on the field to win against the Rams, but it'll be a continue, you know, a continual process of trying to figure out how to be the best defense for our team to ultimately win games. >> Frank, last >> Yesterday you guys traded for Deion Jones and I was looking at some of his numbers. He's only 31. He's had five seasons with 100 tackles. What, you know, he's a pro former pro bowler. Have you had a chance to talk to him? What do you think of that that addition? >> Yeah, I know, I loved it. You know, I I man, I've admired Deion's game for a long time. You know, he came out in 2016 and and flashed onto the scene pretty quickly over in Atlanta. I think he has like five career pick sixes. You know, they ran our cover three scheme. So early on my younger my younger days of, you know, trying to learn the system, we saw a lot of Atlanta tape and I watched him a lot. So, you know, like you said, pro bowler, has been around it, has great perspective for the room and yeah, I I really like the addition. I think he'll he'll help us.

title: 49ers Members Address the Media Following Day 17 of Camp | 49ers
text: What's up, guys? >> Was today the final day of training camp as you see it? >> Um, no. The It's our last practice. We got to walk through tomorrow and then final preseason game. How do you see it going at left guard right now, Kyle? Does it feel like it's close to being decided or is there still a lot up in the air there? >> Um, I mean, it's close to being decided and it needs to be close. You know, today is the second to last day that we'll get to evaluate. We'll get it on the game. So, um, you know, you got Connor and you got Carver who are both competing there and we got Rob Jones who's been hurt. So, we got to balance that off not having him the last two weeks. Um, but that's something we'll discuss and decide on who we want to play in week one. >> What What's the the long-term with the prognosis with him and and with Pleasants? How long do you expect them out? >> Who was him? >> Um, Jones and >> we expect him back um when we're on Australia. >> I'll get on the plane. >> Yes. Yeah. Hopefully we'll get him for our three practices before we go. >> And and just to kind of catch up, was Ror uh a broken rib? >> Yeah. And and is that similar to to what um the other broken rib was like? >> Uh no, it was different. Um Jordan James's was worse just where it was. Um he was he's close this week. Probably won't I'll be he won't go tomorrow or Thursday. Um but should be good after that. >> And then one more. Romelo height. What was he out? >> Um Romelo uh ankle >> and then one more off that. Is Christian Kirk's situation something where he would be a candidate for IR to start the season? >> Uh, yes, possibly. And we got a number of guys like that. So, we got to just see how that pans out here over the next few days. >> A Darren Low be one of those. >> Yes. >> How how hard or easy is it to make a final cut with so many guys and you've been through this before. I think just last year not knowing I mean you have to make a call. Okay, he will be ready for one or week two or where where is the mindset with this much influx injury wise? >> Uh, it's tougher. That's why you want as long as possible, you know, them moving it up this year on Sunday, you know, with us leaving to Australia so soon. So, it it just makes it a little bit harder to guess where those guys are going to be at. Um it's there's a difference though. I mean, most of our guys, you know, besides Ricky and everything, we know are going to be all right. How good are they going to be week one? How good are they going to be week two? Those are things we got to balance out. Um but when you know they're going to be healthy within those first four weeks, um then then it's not as complicated. It's frustrating because you'd like them to be there right away, but um it's if they're not going to be healthy after four weeks and you then you can decide about pup and things like >> New pup rules where guys can practice weeks three and four if they start season up making it easier with Mike and >> Yeah, we're allowed two of them now, which which is huge, you know, because it's always tough when you put guys on pup that they're not allowed to practice. Um but it's really good to get two of those guys back earlier. >> You have a timet for Nick Bosa and how is he doing? >> Um he's doing good. um hoping that he can get into practice next week and um we'll see how those three days go after the mandatory three days off. Kyle, >> do you have a any kind of a pitch count or anything on KD right now as far as practice reps? >> No, I we just been having them go with um non-competitive periods, you know, so that's the first four periods, routes on air, things like that. Just working with the quarterbacks, working with the O line. Um hoping next week when we get those three practices after the mandatory three days off, hopefully you can get in there a little bit more. >> You plan to play the starters? >> What's that? Do you have anything uh any update on Mike Evans? >> Um yeah, Mike had a his growing is tight. Hoping to get back him back next week also. >> Kyle, what's the plan for the final preseason game as far as how much the starters will play, if they play at all? I >> I don't think you'll see many starters. We just don't have enough time as as we usually do, so I'll be surprised if any of them are out there. Um there might be a couple. Um but it'll be closer to how week one was. obviously the the news yesterday morning uh about Jed. Um have you had an opportunity to talk to him or just kind of what's your your view and where you know where things are with the organization moving forward? >> Uh yeah, I got to talk to Jed uh the last two days um and today um obviously it's a very tough situation. I mean views for the organization going forward is is the same as usual. I mean there won't be any difference in that. Um but I know it's it's extremely fresh. I think it's an very very personal situation. Uh I got a lot of respect for Jed. I got a lot of respect for Danielle. Um their family does mean a lot to me. So I'm like, you know, with it with it being this personal, I'm trying as hard as I can to keep it that way. So >> your message your message to the guys today, what was that? >> Um I don't need much a message to the guys. That's um I think that's kind of irrelevant to our guys. just practically is it possible that Jed will be away from the team for a while or just not as much as a presence? >> Um I mean it's kind of it's been like that this summer anyways, you know, with him being out in Ohio and things like that. Does it go to somebody else? Has it still got to be Jed? >> No, I think No, it's the same as always. I mean, Jed has been as good as it gets since I've been here on letting the football people make football decisions. I mean, Jed always wants to be informed and a part of things, but Jed has been exactly what he said he would be. Um, and letting us make those decisions, and he always wants to know about them and stuff, and whether he's here in the building or a text away or on a phone call, that, um, doesn't change anything. >> I've noticed Al Guido on the field talking to you during camp. Is he sort of picking up the slack on site while while J's not here? >> No. Uh, no, there's no difference. I'll give >> I'm sure he does in other spots, but my answer is like from a football standpoint and you don't see much of a football standpoint from Allerg, >> will you be calling plays uh Thursday? >> Uh no. >> But you will week one, I imagine. >> Most likely. >> F you're between your accident and the whole story with Jed, is there any impact do you think on the football and on the team in any way? >> Um I mean I don't get how my story has an impact on the team. I mean, >> or just the fact, you know, some people say these are distractions. In any way, does it impact the football in any way? >> Uh, no. Just questions you got to answer. >> Kyle, you were jogging for a bit. Are you 90% now, would you say? How close are you? >> Um, as far as jogging as far as what you went through, >> um, yeah, I can probably run like a 5240 right now, I'd hope. Actually, I probably couldn't. um still not that strong. Um but I I wasn't before the injury. So the same as I've always been. Okay. >> Coach, >> you mentioned that just the questions you'll have to be uh that'll be asked. You have to remind your players not to let it be a distraction because not only will it be asked here, but when they go to Australia that their media is going to ask about that. Do you have to remind them? >> Yeah, I think you got to always be smart when you have situations like that. Just uh um not make it more not make yourself a part of it. Um, but that's that's what these guys deal with their whole careers. I mean, they're they got cameras in them all the time. They got cameras in their face right after games when they're not feeling right or something very emotional could have happened. Um, so, you know, when dealing with I feel something like this is actually easier for them and some of the stuff they have to deal with in the heat of battle with things um more personal to themselves. So when it comes to the way the team is run, you guys the green laws. So many guys are always very vocal about how well it's run and how well and what this team stands for. I mean obviously you kind of mentioned about the offseason things being, you know, detached from the play on the field, but do you have to reassure, especially the young guys that this franchise stands for a specific thing and carries things out a specific way? Yeah, I think what I mean what people speak highly of and how this has ran. I think it's ran from a complete football standpoint. I think that's what's refreshing here. Um I we have a building that doesn't I've been a lot of places but sometimes you know there's there's a bad article and you got to answer to people who aren't involved in football about how you feel about your defensive coordinator. You get a special you get a punt blocked and there's bad articles and you got to answer to people about firing your special teams coach. um someone gives up something or they gota get a bad PFF grade and you got to answer to non- football people about who you're starting. Uh I think that's what people love about this place. Jed's trusted over the football to people who are involved in football and players feel that. Um I've been in too many other buildings where things do trickle down and when they trickle down and things don't totally make sense that wears on players also. Um more than anything I think here is pretty black and white for them. They know it's always football decisions. Everything's always been football decisions and um because they know Jets put us in charge of making those. >> The Australia trip's about a week away. How excited are you to make that trip? >> Trying to get me in trouble. Um I mean I got I'm just hoping our team's healthy enough and has the time to get there. Um that that those are the challenges of it. Um you know just to get there to prepare for it. You know guys still trying to recover to get there the plane flight and things like that. But once you do get there and stuff, we're going to have fun playing in another country and it's going to be a cool atmosphere, things like that. That'll that'll all be good. Um, but right now, I'm just thinking of the challenges of getting our team ready for for those three and a half hours. >> Asked you about like you're going really early. The Rams are going pretty late. Was there an intention to get there super early to make sure you're totally, you know, have a feel for the place? Just what was the thought process in that that scheduling? Um, more just I mean I I would love to just show up the day before and just play, but I'm not the best when it comes to the science and everything on that stuff. So, you ask people who have done it a number of times. You ask people who study it, you take all their opinions in. Um, we've been strongly recommended to, you know, when you got a 19- hour flight and it's a 16 hour something difference. I forgot because I haven't asked since we were making these decisions. Um, but it's a big adjustment on the body. Um, so the recommendation for everybody has been to tell us when to go and, um, it's made a lot of sense and I know how our players feel also. Um, I was a little bit on the fence. Um, science wasn't what I was reported on and our players weren't at all. Um, so that helped me get off the fence. >> Even though Jed is not involved in the football side of things, he he is the face of this organization. when a situation like this arises it is it really your view that this has no effect on the team on the organization as a whole >> um my view is as the coach does it have effect on us as a team and that's what I continue to answer on from a football standpoint has no effect on us and as far as what we do dayto-day what we talk about and hasn't been mentioned in a meeting today it doesn't have to deal with what happens on the field um everything outside of there I think you guys can judge that better than me >> just three more three more guys for that weren't at practice today. Just updates on Puny uh cowing and stout. >> Pun had some residual effects. Um he was in the protocol, got out. He complained of some residual things after practice today. So he's most likely back in it. Um who else? >> Cowing and Stout. >> Cowing has growing. He's similar with Mike. Hoping to get him back next week. And Stout. Um I want to get it wrong. Stout hip flexor. Expecting him back next week. Kyle, when you guys traded for OCD Zoo, I mean, you knew what kind of player you're getting, but what have you seen in these four and a half weeks from him, especially since the pads went on? >> Um, it's been how we were kind of expecting. We knew we were getting a good player. Um, and so we've seen that. Um, I didn't know how the type of guy he fully was until we started really hearing it from around the league and people from there. And that's been cool to go through this whole camp with him. He's he's exactly how he's advertised. I mean, he's a true leader. He goes hard as can be every day. That's why it gets really annoying for the O line just because of how hard he goes. Um, they've been battling all camp. He's made us better. I think we've made him better and I'm real excited to have him on our team. >> Do you have a good idea with all you had to juggle with the injury? Do you have a good idea of what your team can be this year or are you still kind of I wait to see if this guy gets back, that player gets back? >> Yeah, it's the same as always. I mean, you got a decent idea in camp. Um, you got a decent idea before you go to camp when you see what's on paper to know where you have a chance, but you want to see how it all comes together. Um, I've had times where we've had a completely healthy camp and that's changed in the first two weeks. Um, and then you have to adjust throughout the year. Um, and I feel like we've done that. I've had times where we've been beat up in camp and you're worried about stuff and the season's gone really well in terms of injuries. So, I've been doing this a long enough time that I feel like you've almost been in every situation when it comes to those things. So, I try not to get too high or low with the stuff. Yeah, it's frustrating when you only have so many days to prepare for week one that you want everyone out there. Um, but I've learned enough not to overreact on it too much. Um the things that I really struggle with is when you lose a guy for the year like we did Ricky. Those are the harder ones. But um I used to get upset with every little injury, but unless it's a long time, um I've learned to life's too short to get too upset about it. It can end up being all right. >> Two more guys. Two more. >> Um is it somewhat encouraging? I'm sure it is encouraging to see what Dejon Stribbling has been able to do through the first two preseason games. title: The Good and Not So Good from Day 17 of 49ers Training Camp
text: The 49ers just finished their 17th and final day of training camp. Here's who stood out. The good, wide receiver De'Jean Shriblin. He's playing through a right shoulder injury and he's still the best wide receiver on the team and it's not close. Today he lost his one-on-one match up against Jack Jones who broke up the pass when Shriblin was running deep. After that rep, Kyle Shanahan called Shriblin over to him and gave him some coaching points. Whatever Shanahan said worked because Shriblin went on to dominate practice with one healthy shoulder. He caught four passes for roughly 80 yards during team drills. After every catch, he awkwardly flipped the ball back to a coach with his left hand because his right shoulder hurts. The 9ers need him to stay healthy all season and catch at least 70 passes. If you can do that, they'll win lots of games. Running back Christian McCaffrey, he practiced for the second day in a row and looked perfectly healthy. He caught three passes and carried the ball many, many times. I believe McCaffrey when he says he wasn't injured and the 9ers simply agreed to let him skip two weeks of camp. I think he wants a new deal and he's salty that the 9ers didn't give him one. Who knows, maybe they want to extend McCaffrey but haven't been able to get Jet York on the phone. More on York in a minute. Tight end Luke Farrell, he caught a touchdown pass from Brock Purdy in the red zone. Farrell is having a good camp which means the 9ers have three good veteran tight ends, him, George Kittle, and Jake Tonges. Those three should play alongside McCaffrey and Shriblin as much as possible. Forget Deebo Samuel and Kyle Juszczyk and use Mike Evans sparingly. If the 9ers overuse Evans, he won't make it through the season. Safety Marqui Seagal, he intercepted a pass that Purdy threw over the middle to Demarcus Robinson. The pass was high, Robinson jumped and tipped the ball into the air, Seagal dove and came down with it. Purdy is having a good camp but whenever he misses, he tends to miss high which is why he liked Juwan Jennings so much. Jennings would have caught this pass. Robinson isn't as tall so he tipped it to the defense. Safety Jaquiski Brown, he broke up a pass that was intended for Deebo Samuel during one-on-one drills. I could put Samuel in the not-so-good section but I want to be positive so I'll focus on Brown shutting down a wide receiver. It's always impressive when a safety does that. Defensive end Sam Okuwanu. He beat starting right tackle Colton McKivitz around the edge to sack Purdy during 11-on-11 team drills. Okuwanu has taken practically all the first team reps at defensive end at camp. That's because Nick Bosa hasn't participated at all and Romello Height has been in and out. Today he missed practice with an ankle injury he suffered against the Chargers. The not-so-good. Owner Jed York, he did not show up to practice. Apparently he lives in Ohio now and hasn't been around the facility in a while, which is odd. Didn't his parents turn the team over to him because they didn't want to live in California and run the day-to-day operations? Isn't that what York is supposed to be doing? Can he really run the team from Ohio while he's dealing with humiliating legal issues? Because for the past month team CEO Al Guido has been at practically every practice. If you didn't know better, you'd think Guido was the Niners owner. Maybe he will be soon. Quarterback Brock Purdy, he got intercepted trying to force a pass over the middle. Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris affectionately calls Purdy the layer king because of his ability to float balls over the middle with touch. This off-season those passes are often sailing a bit too high. Surprisingly Purdy's best throws have gone outside the numbers. He really misses George Kittle. Fortunately for Purdy, Kittle will be back soon. Cornerback Jack Jones, he gave up a 30-yard catch to De'Shawn Shribling then pushed him to the ground after the play. Keep in mind Shribling has a shoulder injury and was wearing a black non-contact jersey, which means Jones wasn't supposed to touch him, let alone push him to the ground. Shribling stayed on the ground for a few seconds and got up slowly. The team needs to fine Jones for that mental mistake. Nickelback Qwuantrezz Knight Stout, he missed practice with a groin injury. Deommodore Lenoir took his place at nickelback. No disrespect to Stout, but Lenoir is better at that position. Wide receiver Mike Evans, he missed yet another practice this time with groin tightness, which means Evans missed more than half of training camp this year. He never went more than a few practices in a row without getting injured. I expect this season will play out similarly. Wide receiver Jordan Watkins, he lost both of his reps during one-on-one drills. First to Samuel then to Jack Jones. Both times Watkins ran a deep comeback route and created no separation. They needed the same thing during 11-on-11 team drills and the pass got broken up. Watkins is a good athlete, but he can't get himself open or make contested catches, which means he's a system guy and a backup. Wide receiver Jacob Cowing, he missed practice with a groin injury. Like Evans, Cowing can't go more than a few days without tweaking something. Unlike Evans, Cowing isn't a future Hall of Famer. He still should make the team.
