title: Freiermuth, Jones, Fautanu, Allar & Roberts Press Conference (August 25) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: There's still more time in the preseason. >> Yeah, just focusing it on you know getting the body right for the for the season. You know it's been a it's been a long camp. It's been a great camp and I've just got to continue to stay healthy and you know get dialed in on you know when we start game planning for Atlanta. Getting into the groove of of being part of the game week. >> Do things get a little bit I don't want to say monotonous but just kind of the same routine over and over for knowing that you still have this amount of time before that first week? >> Uh yeah I mean I'm definitely excited to start blocking you know our defense and edge rushers and excited to you know go against someone else. Um But yeah I mean obviously it's just part of the job. You just got to show up every day and then and you know do what you're supposed to. >> So far what are the things that you've appreciated about a Mike McCarthy offense? >> Uh the use of the middle of the field and the use of you know the talent we have and I'm excited for you know what is what's going to come this year. >> Looking back at the past couple of games you've been able to play how do you feel you've performed and what are you looking to build on? >> Um First game it was it was solid I would say. Second game needs a lot of improvement. Um just me being back on the right side. I just got to get back to the feel of things you know getting getting the repetition over there because all off season I really was working on left but you know we we got to do what we can for our team so I just got to be prepared to play the right. >> How are you feeling physically? Because I I know it's been a hard road back for you with the rehab and everything. Now you've not just been playing you've been playing a lot. How do you feel like you're you're doing physically? I feel fine honestly. You know a little little gimpy here and there but for the most part you know like my neck's holding up fine. My legs feel great so you know that's all I really needed to be able to play this game from. >> Robert Hansley was telling us you're still working to get your groove back. >> Yeah. >> How how do you feel like you're close? Where where do you feel like you're at with your game? >> Uh coming out here and being able to go against these guys every day, you know, it's it's a it's a big step. So, you know, I'm not where I want to be at yet, but I'm for sure taking the right steps. I can feel it. Um you know, I just got to continue to show up each and every day and put my best foot forward. >> What's still lacking? Like what do you What's still lacking? >> Uh just like the technique the technique things, you know, a couple fundamental things here and there, but nothing too crazy. >> I know you've added a bunch of strength. Do you feel like there's some more there that that could help out, too? >> Oh yeah, yeah. Definitely can still put on a couple more pounds and you know, when when that happens, you know, the strength comes with it, so. >> So, you feel like you're you're ready to be the swing guy? >> Uh I honestly don't know. You know, I just got to be prepared to play both sides. So. >> But if say they make you the swing tackle, how would you handle it? >> I got I got to do what I can for my team, you know? Um I've been come I've came off the bench before. That's that um it's not a problem. Um not saying that's where I want to be, but you know, like I said, whatever I got to do to help my team. >> A lot of reps on both sides, too. >> Yeah, yeah, yeah. For sure. >> What are the challenges of doing that in the same game, going from playing left tackle, right tackle in the same same game? >> Uh it's it's pretty tough, you know, just being able to flip the plays, um your technique, footwork, you know, just everything. You got to flip everything, so it's I wouldn't say it's impossible, but it it's it's pretty tough, but you know, we this it's the NFL, so. >> Coach Reichow was talking about the importance of hunting for more explosive plays in the run game. Um what have you diagnosed when you've looked at the film and you guys might be just off a tick in that regard? >> Um obviously it all starts up front, just making sure that we're finishing our blocks and um not letting guys make arm tackles and especially that in the run game and then obviously protecting the quarterback uh better than we have been, so. I think that's obviously something that we can control and something that um we take pride in, so. >> Josh, sorry if you've already been asked this, but what has stood out to you so far about Max throughout this preseason? >> Yeah, obviously, you know, his his injury was unfortunate, but just the way that he comes to work and shows up in meeting and asks me questions. At least we sit next to each other in the meeting room, so he's always asking the right questions and um he's hungry. And obviously, him being back out here is good for him and good for us cuz it obviously elevates the room cuz he's a baller. He you know, he he sets the tone I don't know if you guys seen it out here, but I'm not going to say what happened, but if you you know, he a guy like that, he he's uh no matter he's in his first year, second year, third year, like he's a dog. So, he's bringing it. >> Do you expect to play more this next preseason game or >> I have no clue. I have no clue. I'm just preparing like I am. I prepare every week no matter the preseason or regular season like I'm playing, so um diagnosing diagnosing my opponent and um just watching film. Just what I do. >> How much are you looking forward to uh playing on a road stadium now you obviously first two preseason games being at home. Possibly having to use a silent count and all that stuff. >> Yeah, it'll be really cool. Uh especially with the new stadium there at Highmark and then I got Chase McSorley on staff over there in Buffalo, too. So, it'll be good to catch up with him and you know, Zane Zandis um the D-tackle over there now, too. So, it'll be good to catch up with a couple uh teammates and obviously uh former coaches there, too. >> What's most important for you this week when you go into this game? >> Yeah, I think just building off uh success and and learning from mistakes that I have made and and just continuing to show improvement um with operation and just how I'm handling the uh procedures and everything like that and operations. Uh so, I think just building off the things I've done well and then also just correcting the things I've I've uh messed up on or slipped up on. >> Drew, a couple of the throws the other night, the the deep ball to 81, the kind of improv play and the the sideline shot to 27, they're getting rave reviews on social media. Were they well received in the team meeting? >> Uh I mean, they showed the one to Lake down the sideline. Just we we emphasized playing above the 2.3 second mark both on offense and defense. So, scramble drill. So, Lake did a great Lake did a great job of, you know, just finding green grass down the sideline. And O-line did a good job of just giving me enough protection to be able to kind of get out and and create a throw for us. >> Drew, what did you learn overall from the tape in the second game? >> Yeah, uh there's just opportunities to be clean cleaner uh in progressions in in general and just stay disciplined to everything. Uh trust the trust the progressions, trust the footwork and everything like that. So, just get back to the basics. I felt like I I passed up a couple early completions. Um especially my first couple drives in the game uh that if I take it, it's going to be second and five or, you know, third and four. Uh a lot more manageable situations for us that, you know, put us put us at more at a uh advantage as opposed to the defense. >> Do you feel like you like all all the work that you've been doing on on your mechanics and footwork and everything like that? Do you feel like a lot of that stuff that you're working on is becoming more second nature when you're getting into games now? >> Yeah, I mean, I think uh from an upper body standpoint of mechanics, we haven't really changed much of anything. Uh now, footwork, it's still like just being disciplined with it like I was just kind of talking about. So, yeah, just keep continuing to build consistency in discipline in those those little things so that when, you know, I'm out in there in a game or practice, just I'm not thinking about that stuff. I'm just going out there and reading the defense and, you know, throwing where the ball's supposed to be going. >> You said in Latrobe that Aaron that you were talking to Aaron about improving on your deep balls. Do you have anything to say about that sideline throw? >> Uh no, we didn't really talk about that one too much. But, um yeah, Aaron's Aaron's been a big help in general. Um and it's been fun getting to learn from him. And I I look forward to keep learning from him and everybody in that room. >> What has he been like on the sideline during games? >> Yeah, he's been great. Uh he's he's been a great resource for everybody that's that's in the game. Whether it was Mason, Will, or myself in the game. Him talking about what he's seen out there, if he's seen anything different from what we saw on film. Predictions of what he thinks going to happen on the next couple drives or things to be ready for in certain situations. So, he's been he's like another coach out on the sidelines. So, having him and and Coach Arthur on the quarterback bench has been great so far, definitely for us. >> Yeah, we've asked you a lot about Aaron, but Mason's not in the easiest spot in between a future Hall of Famer and a couple young guys. How much do you appreciate his demeanor and and just the way that he said he goes kind of way back with you actually with some recruiting and >> Yeah, I mean, I So, the first time I met Mason was in the spring, obviously, but our dads had talked I think my sophomore or junior year of high school because my first OC at Penn State was Coach Yurcich and he had Mason at Oklahoma State. So, they they connected way back then and then Mason's been great. Like he he's great great for everybody. He he's helped me out a ton as well, too, especially, you know, in OTAs when I first got here and even through training camp and games like giving me reminders and and things to be looking for, asking me a ton of questions to make sure I'm I'm locked in on the game plan. So, I really appreciate everything he's done. He's He's a great teammate, great person to be around. Definitely one of the the funnier guys on the team, so it's always fun to be around him and general. >> I know it's a small sample size, but after these two recent games, what are your conversations with Coach McCarthy like? What How is he handling things? What are What are those conversations like? >> Yeah, I mean, I think it's just continuing to build off the fundamental success that I've had and then again, just keep keep stacking and keep finding ways to get better. You know, I think the good thing about, you know, Friday, even though I didn't go out and play as clean as I wanted to, it gave me a lot of things to learn from and it really grow from, especially focusing on these these last couple practices at camp giving me opportunity to, you know, not just see all the the stuff, just really hone on things that I need to, you know, stay on top of no matter if I'm playing well or playing bad. >> Uh just from team meetings, you know, obviously coach McCarthy uh very detailed uh structured you know he knows what he wants. He wants what he wants. So uh you know, it's like I said, I got here kind of late in the game, you know what I'm saying? So I just kind of just been focusing on getting myself, you know what I'm saying? Prepared and stuff like that, but just what I see from a team perspective, very structured, very detailed and stuff like that. So yeah. >> How comfortable are you with the coordinator? And maybe tell the other guys what to expect. >> You talking about PG? >> Oh, I'm very comfortable with PG. I know uh his expectations, uh what he expect out of players, how he kind of go about uh step by step of getting the uh the defense ready throughout the week and whatnot. Uh and such and such. So you know, when guys ask me, you know, I kind of be like, "Nah, you know, that's that's how he is." And you know, "But if you do this, you do that." You know, whatever question may be and stuff like that. So yeah. >> You've probably gone to Buffalo about a billion times in your career. Is it Is it going to be weird to see a new place over there with the new stadium? >> Oh, they did get a new stadium. Oh, yeah, that'll be a little weird. It's going to be a little weird, but I didn't been there so much. Uh I'm still used to driving in on them back roads, you know, through the >> You're probably still going to be doing that. >> community. So yeah, yeah, yeah. So I haven't really even thought about it though. >> You had told a story on the TV broadcast which I was unaware about you. You caught a touchdown pass from Brady. >> Oh, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. We needed to score. I said, "You want to score? Put me in." Nah, he threw me the ball. And it really wasn't a bad pass. I had to go back shoulder. I took it to the house. >> Were you like filling fullback? >> Yeah, that year, man, we had some great fullbacks. Uh James Develin, I think he was dealing with an injury that year and whatnot. And then Jakob Johnson was on our second string, he got hurt and whatnot. And uh yeah, it's just all hands on deck, man. >> Remember where the ball was? Uh probably it. about 40, so about 40, so. Whatever it was going to be, it was going to be a touchdown, so. >> You said back shoulder, though. >> Yeah, back shoulder. Yeah, man. I I know they talk about Tom a lot, but hey, I feel like I made him look good that time. [laughter] >> Hey, this is your second time with Patrick Graham. What stands out to you about him? >> Uh man, just his poise, his poise, his control his command of the defense, how he puts us still puts players in position to be the best player, you know what I'm saying? To to their being. And and when you one of them elite players, he tries to go in man, he he'll study that one player and see like, oh, if they get better at this, man, they can really take it to the next level and he knows that that's even going to be even more of a thing for the the defense and opposing teams only looking at you for this and you start hitting them with that, now they're all off balance and that's just like I said, man, I'm always telling you he's just a brainiac. And and defensive minded, like he's always thinking ball and stuff like that, man. You know, he haven't changed one bit. I enjoy being around him and stuff like that. I'm excited for the upcoming season. >> Has your energy or your chippiness jumped up since you put on the uniform? >> Mhm. >> Do you take pride in being that guy to be up in that stuff? >> Absolutely. And I'm not pulling off. >> Eric, you I know we're not here all of training camp and during Joey's kind of contract situation, but you've dealt with contracts before and you've known Joey for a little bit. >> What advice or or what do you tell him during this whole situation? >> Honestly, like I just kind of stay out of it. I wish him nothing but the best. You know, I hope he gets exactly what he's valued at. You know, me and Joey has a great relationship on and off the field and what not. But I for me, my personal I've always been with teams and players is in a negotiation, I kind of just stay out of it and just, you know, look at that player be like, man, I I you get exactly what you got it for. >> How do you guys keep up with being, you know, a distraction from the team when something like that is going on? >> Joey's always a good player. Joey's a good person on and off the field. You see him, man. He He's not even He He him himself not even a distraction. You know, we do day-to-day business and stuff like that and obviously we know when it's time to wrap it up Joey will be there. >> You give young guys any advice when it's, you know, bubble bubble game like this and you're coming down to to the end here? If they ask If they ask, man, I I always just tell them, man, go out there, take it one play at a time, you know, uh and whatnot. You know, me myself, I I hope to be playing cuz I I still need to get some things uh ironed out and whatnot, but you know, I I've never went into a season and I I know it's kind of uh naive of me. You know, a lot of people say, "Oh, that's naive." But I've never went into a season even my 10 years ever feeling like Like I've always been like, you know, "Well, we didn't get no call." And then, you know, I just go to work the next day, you know, and stuff like that because I think it's just it's it's it's for myself. It keeps me prepared. It keeps me never feeling comfortable.

What's been some of your observations of how they performed and what are some of the things that go into that ultimate decision? >> Well, I I think it's, you know, I mean, you obviously want offensive players that excel on special teams or defensive players that really excel on special teams. It's it's uh I'm not I'm not a I'm not a fan of a guy that's just a he's a he's an ex- he's an exceptional special teams player, but he doesn't contribute on offense and defense. That's just my personal preference. Um I I I've spoken on it back in the beginning here. Uh have talked about it numerous times through camp. You know, we want players that can play all four downs. Uh so, you know, so it's important for these these running backs, after the first two is, you know, who's playing the best? You know, who's playing the best on offense? Who's through you know, contributing uh to be a be a first, second, and third-down player. I think every play caller uh in the league would prefer to play with running backs that can play on first, second, and third down cuz when you have to you know, you you create tremendous tendencies when you start running your backs in and out of the game based off of down and distances. So, we prefer not to play that way. Um so, you know, that that's a big part of it. And then and then really the determining factor a lot of times in that third, fourth running back is is what kind of player he is on special teams. So, that's that's how I view it. That's kind of I would that's the priority that that I I would put in as far as the checklist. >> Last one? >> Mike, obviously there's a business side to all of this, but personally, how tough is a week like this where you have to make decisions like this? >> I I think uh personally for every head coach and I I mean, I can't speak on everybody, but I I I know for me I'm not looking forward to the next four days. Um you know, you know, I've you know, I've been here with these men since April. You know, I I see the time that they put in. I'm not just talking about the CBA regulated time. I'm talking about the weekends. You know, you you you're the early mornings. Um so, you know, I'm a I'm a big believer in what I've just have always worked you know, extensively on weekends. Um just just the design of how we do things here. So, you you know who's in here. You see the guys putting in the extra time. So, um it's you know, 68 players. I mean, that's what's going to come out of this 90-man roster. And you know, you you want to see everybody get an opportunity. I think it's important for me to accomplish that here in Buffalo and then then we'll we'll see it how it sorts out. But yes, it's not uh it's it's not a great day when you you're telling a guy that you know, he's not part of the 68. Um but I I think the most important thing is you be honest and tell him where he is and and what he's done and what he needs to work on and you know, so and history holds true, we'll we'll probably work together again maybe again someday. So that's just the reality of of my personal experience. But yes, this is this is a very stressful, difficult uh you know, string of days here for for these men. >> All right. >> Thank you.

title: JOEY PORTER JR. CONTRACT IMPASSE? Steelers Running Out of Time Before Week 1
text: Steelers breakdown podcast. He's pen live Steelers beat reporter Nick Farah. I'm John Lucy. We are now live on YouTube and Facebook taking your questions in the chat for Nick. And of course the big topic right now bubbling up in national NFL media and of course all things Pittsburgh. It's not so easy signing PZY Jr. We got Ian Rapaort using the Iword impass. We got Mike Gafolo saying the Steelers really haven't even made Joey Porter Jr. an offer. We got talk of a premium trade for the Steelers if they were going to deal Porter uh first round pick or the equivalent of that. And we got uh Mark Cabali, one of Nick's colleagues, saying that the Steelers are not 100% sure a deal is going to happen with Joey Porter Jr. before the start of the season. And we know once the season starts, the Steelers do not negotiate. We're going to go right to Nick for uh what he's hearing from his sources about how this became such a contractual disaster for Omar Khan and company. >> Well, I think you know there's a different planes of thought here um kind of being wedged. I think the Steelers like Joey Porter Jr. as a top 10 corner. I think Joey Porter Jr. thinks he should get top three money. And there's distinctions. There's arguments to both sides. I think you can really make an argument that he is one. I think you can make the other argument that hey, they're reasonable to wait on this or at least try to get a compromise. He probably is asking for market resetting money. I think that is realistic for him to start with. I think the Steelers are clearly trying to say no, we don't want to pay you market resetting money. Um the Steelers are late to the party, right? They are. Um, Deon Witherspoon's deal is done. $33 million per year, 101 of that guaranteed. Derek Stingley's deal got done back in March, then Saw Scarnner, then Trent McDuffy, then Denzel Ward. Since the Pittsburgh Steelers could have signed Joey Porter Jr. all the way back in March if they wanted to, five different quarterback contracts have eclipsed one another and set the market rate. So, the Steelers now, if they were to pay Joey Porter Jr. 33.1 million which is more than Witherspoons. They obviously would be paying a significant amount more than they would have if they had paid him in March rate. We know the Steelers really don't negotiate many contracts though outside of their free agent contracts uh in before the the draft either. So they have a window. This might be something they need to start looking at really extending their young players before the draft because more and more teams are doing it. It's driving up the market. This happened with TJ Watt where that same market that once was, you know, between 35ish got driven all the way up to 41. Now they caved and paid $41 million to usurp the Miles Garrett deal, but that was something that happened with Porter. He's in a tough spot because I think the Steelers obviously want to get him under contract, but market resetting money, I think that's a lot to ask. We're talking about an elite man coverage quarterback that has no doubt had the best season of his career. Cut the penalties in half last year. Got his hands on the football. I know the picks aren't there, but the PBUs are really encouraging. Corners love if you get your hands on the football, even if it's not a pick. If you can get in there and get PBUS, they love that. And that's something Porter has done really well. Um, he is someone that was frankly an eraser last year. Um, I thought his masterpiece, even though the Steelers lost this game, was his performance against Nico Collins in the wildard round where he played incredible. I thought he was one of the best players on the field that game. Um, so that is the argument, right? He hasn't allowed a touchdown since his rookie year. Um, in man-to-man coverage, he hasn't allowed a touchdown. The one touchdown he did allow his rookie year was a zone coverage bust. Um, and we're talking about a guy that has very rare traits for man coverage uh quarterbacks. the Steelers are going to play a lot of man-to-man coverage. It's why they signed Jamal Dean, who was another press man corner. Um, so there's an argument to say, well, you're going to fit the scheme to Joey Porter Jr. and then clearly sign Jamal Dean with the idea in mind of having Joey Porter Jr. be his running mate. Otherwise, why would you sign another press man corner? And Jamal Dean even said to us back in March when they signed him, Patrick Graham, the Steelers defensive coordinate, told him, "You're going to do a lot of bumping. You're going to do a lot of press. You're gonna do a lot of stuff. It's tailor made for Joey Porter Jr. Even still, you can only play man coverage so much in the National Football League. You're probably going to play it at most 50 55% of the time. That leaves a whole 50 to 45% in zone. And I think that's part of maybe where the Steelers are a little bit kind of treacherous here. You know, they haven't we keep hearing this idea of they want to see him out on the football field, right? That's one thing we keep hearing about. And I wonder if part of that is they just want to see him play in a match zone and they want to see him how he fits into these zone coverages because I think that since he came into the league that has been a weak point of his. You know, he hasn't been bad at zone coverage but he hasn't been elite >> and I think you know can you be good at zone coverage? That's going to be the question for him. He's an okay tackler. He's not a great tackler. So there are some questions I think that they have where they're like how well does he fit into this other 50% because they're going to play match zones. That's what the National Football League is nowadays in terms of coverages. And if you're not a super versatile corner right off the getup, it's hard to pay you topofthe-line money. Now, one thing I think working in Porter's corner is Denzel Ward got $31.2 million. I like Denzel Ward. He's an agent corner that is probably on the same level as Porter if you don't want to take Porter over him straight up. I mean, I think there's an argument to say Porter's a better corner. So, that to me is a really strong argument. in Joey's corner, but the Steelers have a lot of leverage. They could tag him next year. Um, it's hard to for me to foresee Joey Porter Jr. sitting out any games of his rookie contract. Um, so he doesn't have a ton of leverage. We know the Steelers, as you mentioned, do not negotiate into the season. Um, and so I think that there are a lot of different angles to look at this at where I think the Steelers might have some questions just about how good is he at zone. You know, he's not an elite tackling corner. good tackling corner, but an elite tackling corner. So, I think there's like a different scope here of, you know, Porter wanting to maybe reset the market versus the Steelers who maybe are more like 28 29ish million per year. That's probably about a 6 million per year difference. That's not small. That's pretty large in terms of this. And that's why you are hearing the word impass. Um, I'm not sure if I believe they haven't put an offer down. I haven't gotten that on the record or anything like that, but I do know that these sides know each other's range, what they're comfortable with. They've had conversations. There have been proposals thrown from Joey's side to the Steelers for sure that the Steelers have then turned down. Sauce, I think between Stingley and Sauce, I believe there were two weeks.
